The location of the proposed Arch, at Memorial Circle, will interrupt the highly significant relationship between the Lincoln Memorial, across Arlington Memorial Bridge, to Arlington National Cemetery and Arlington House. One of the most symbolic landscape vistas in Washington, DC, the vista was designed to represent the post-Civil War reconciliation of the north and south of the United States. Arlington Memorial Bridge was intentionally designed with a low profile to respect the visual and symbolic vistas connecting the National Mall and National Cemetery. If constructed as planned at the proposed location, the new Monumental Arch will obscure the intentional axial and aesthetic relationships between the Lincoln Memorial, Arlington Memorial Bridge, and Arlington House. In addition, the proposed location of the Arch, at the entrance to Arlington National Cemetery, is inconsistent with the solemn historic character of Arlington National Cemetery. The hallowed resting place of 400,000 veterans and their families, Arlington National Cemetery is a powerful reminder of American military sacrifice, selfless service, and national unity, all within sight of the monumental core of the Nation's Capital. Distinguished by the Tomb of the Unknowns, Memorial Avenue, and rolling hillsides of uniform rows of simple headstones. The Arch, as proposed, would dominate Arlington National Cemetery, and be inconsistent with its hallowed character of solemn graves with powerful, unadorned white markers. Finally, it is important to note that review of the proposal under Section 106 of the National Historic Preservation Act has not yet been initiated. It is imperative that all procedures for formal approval be followed. No administration may disregard procedure and protocol simply because they don't like the rules or the timeline. We are a country founded on procedure, it is why we have been so successful for the last 250 years. If we disregard approvals and procedure now, we will no longer be the powerful democracy we claim to be. Sincerely, A concerned citizen Jennifer Neale

name: Kathleen Tindle
text: Dear Esteemed Members of the National Capital Planning Commission, I would like to express my sincere concerns about the proposed New Monumental Arch. The Commemorative Works Act states that new projects should not interfere with existing commemorative works. From my understanding of this project, in its proposed dimensions, the arch would interfere with the existing commemorative works of the Lincoln Memorial and Arlington Cemetery. I would urge the NCPC and the National Park Service, under Section 106 of the National Historic Preservation Act, to participate in a thorough review and consider alternatives to the design and location of the arch. In this process, the project re-design would then be brought before Congress for their approval, as required by the Commemorative Works Act. Both of my parents are buried in Arlington National Cemetery. I would feel personally distraught if this arch, as proposed, moved forward. The location, height, and scale would interfere with the visual landscape now enjoyed between the Lincoln Memorial and Arlington National Cemetery. Moving forward with this project would disrespect the veterans, including my parents, buried in Arlington National Cemetery. Sincerely, Kathleen Tindle

name: Brooks Thorlaksson
text: I am unalterably opposed to this project. It does not fit into the current environment, it does not represent democracy, and it will be an architectural monstrosity, outsize and representative of a past era.

name: Cherith Bevers
text: There is NO need for this arch and I am strongly opposed to this project based on expense and how it will infringe on the sanctity of Arlington National Cemetary!

name: Vicky Rankin
text: This proposed project would take away from the simplicity and the beauty of the current landscape. Arlington National Cemetery is a powerful reminder of generations of sacrifice and a place of comfort to their families and to our country. To build a huge vanity arch that completely takes over the view of both Arlington and the Lincoln Memorial would be a slap in the face to everyone who has ever served and to everyone that cares about what our country stands for. The American people overwhelming DO NOT want this arch and this idea needs to be shut down before it's too late.

name: Sandra Decker
text: Do NOT build the arch. Respect our Veterans, and leave the space open, as intended. Our country does not build monuments to flatter a living person's ego. Shame! This offensive plan must be stopped, the citizens of this great nations do not want it. If the existing rules for such a proposal are followed, and it goes through the legal process, it will be DENIED. Make sure it does.

name: Sheila Parks
text: I have serious concerns about the proposed arch. The location of the proposed Arch, at Memorial Circle, will interrupt the highly significant relationship between the Lincoln Memorial, across Arlington Memorial Bridge, to Arlington National Cemetery and Arlington House. One of the most symbolic landscape vistas in Washington, DC, the vista was designed to represent the post-Civil War reconciliation of the north and south of the United States. If constructed as planned at the proposed location, the new Triumphal Arch will obscure the intentional axial and aesthetic relationships between the Lincoln Memorial, Arlington Memorial Bridge, and Arlington House. The unprecedented height and scale of the proposed Triumphal Arch, will overwhelm the Lincoln Memorial, Arlington National Cemetery, and Arlington House. The proposed Arch would be double the size of the Lincoln Memorial and would risk disrespecting this powerful and beloved monument. As such, the Triumphal Arch is inconsistent with the McMillan Plan and subsequent planning decisions that have stewarded the National Mall as a unified composition characterized by long, open, and uninterrupted viewsheds, with a clear hierarchy of monumental elements, that culminates at its western end at the Lincoln Memorial. Most importantly, the proposed location of the Arch, at the entrance to Arlington National Cemetery, is inconsistent with the solemn historic character of Arlington National Cemetery. The hallowed resting place of 400,000 veterans and their families, Arlington National Cemetery is a powerful reminder of American military sacrifice, selfless service, and national unity, all within sight of the monumental core of the Nation's Capital. Distinguished by the Tomb of the Unknowns, Memorial Avenue, and rolling hillsides of uniform rows of simple headstones, Arlington National Cemetery is a living memorial that honors thirty funeral services each day. The Arch, as proposed, would dominate Arlington National Cemetery, and be inconsistent with its hallowed character of solemn graves with powerful, unadorned white markers. There is no need and no precedent for a sitting President to deface the National Mall with their own likeness or vanity projects. Please honor the existing monuments and the gravesites of our soldiers and deny this permit and the project as a whole. Thank you, Sheila Parks

name: Susan Graham
text: Please do not build the arch, it will block our beautiful views.

name: Patricia Aitken
text: I strongly object to this proposed action.

name: Linda Walters
text: I would like to express my disapproval for the proposed Monumental Arch. The location of the proposed Arch will interrupt the highly significant relationship between the Lincoln Memorial, across Arlington Memorial Bridge, to Arlington National Cemetery and Arlington House. One of the most symbolic landscapes in Washington, D.C., the vista was designed to represent the post-Civil War reconciliation of the north and south of the United States. This proposed arch has no significance relating to these scared memorials. It will diminish what the heroic efforts of soldiers laid to rest at Arlington. It is simply another vanity project by Mr. Trump. I respectfully request that this project not be approved in any form. Linda Walters

name: Esme Sifuentes
text: I am totally opposed to the proposed arch, which would change the vista, emphasis, and the symbolism of the current monuments. I'm outraged that this is being considered.

name: Cathy Lavin
text: Wasteful spending of my money, destroying the significance of Arlington National Cemetery. This vanity project should not take place.

name: Linda Howard
text: The Arch is not needed for any purpose and destroys the view and ties between the Lincoln Memorial to the Arlington National Cemetery. This is a symbolic National treasure, and the view should not be altered for the whims of a few.

name: Carol Doehne
text: No arch. There is absolutely no need to bring this obscene vanity project anywhere near the hallowed grounds of Arlington National Cemetery. This plan is an insult to all those buried there. A Trump Arch has no place in our nation's capital, where it would overwhelm the existing memorials.

name: Debra Bridson
text: I would like to express my objection to the proposed monstrosity Arch. This would distract from the spectacular views of our most treasured sacred grounds Arlington National Cemetery. Please do not allow this to proceed. There is no public benefit. Thank you, Debra Bridson

name: Darci Minnella
text: I stand with the veterans who admirably supported our country through their service and agree that this newly proposed arch will interfere with the aesthetic of what is currently in place. This is nothing more than one of Trump's many vanity projects, that the country cannot afford at this time while we're in the midst of a war he started, paying $4.45 per gallon of gas and his additional vanity projects (reflecting pool and ballroom) are running significantly over cost. I know someone personally who is buried in Arlington, therefore I want the dignity that the current entrance to the hallowed grounds remain to stay as is.

name: Anne Currie
text: The new monumental arch needs to be either eliminated or significantly reduced in scale as to not obstruct the view of the other historic monuments along the National Mall.

name: Ginny Barnes
text: Disagree with establishment of this arch- too large, inappropriate for area-does not reflect national values

name: Annie Riggs
text: I wholeheartedly disapprove of the construction of this monstrosity. All management of and construction on Public lands should be guided by the will of the people of the United States, not that of the person who temporarily happens to hold the office of president. The design of the arch is poor, without positive significant meaning behind it, and has been pushed through by politically appointed cronies of the current administration. Not to mention that it will detract from the beauty and spirit of the Lincoln Monument & Arlington National Cemetery. Our tax dollars should be better spent on the people of this country rather than appeasing the ego of the president. Please do not allow this monstrosity to go forward.

name: Stacey Gustafson
text: This project is an abuse of public funds and disrespectful of previous memorials.

name: Kristy Katz
text: This Arch overpowers the unobstructed current view. Arlington Cemetery does not need an oversized Arch at it's entrance. We need to keep the solemn, long and low view we have. The United States does not need an Arch because other countries have one. The taxpayer needs relief these days, not vanity projects. Do not approve this wasteful use of taxpayer money. Thank you

name: Alberta Lindauer
text: There are many other things much more important to the welling being of the citizens of this country than a New Arch. Many citizens can't afford the basic necessities so spending money on this is shameful. It is widely known it's not something most citizens want and certainly don't feel the need for. The wants and desires of 1 man should not override the wants and needs of the American people.

name: Suzanne Thompson
text: NO to this absolutely hideous monstrosity.

name: Tina Vasen
text: I formally register my strong opposition to the proposed 250-foot Independence Arch in Washington, D.C. This [vanity] project represents an unprecedented and inappropriate alteration to our nation's most hallowed ceremonial landscape for several critical reasons: Obstructs Historic Sightlines: At 250 feet tall, the arch would irreversibly block the celebrated, protected view between the Lincoln Memorial and Arlington House at Arlington National Cemetery. This carefully preserved axis was deliberately designed to symbolize national unity. Bypasses Legislative Process: The Commemorative Works Act explicitly requires express authorization from Congress for new monuments on federal reservations in the capital. Bypassing Congress undermines the established democratic process for our national memorials. Disregards Public Consensus: This unilateral vanity project is being forced through despite overwhelming public dissent, with early public comment periods reflecting near-unanimous opposition to the scale and necessity of the structure. Aviation and Traffic Hazards: Positioning a massive 25-story monument on Memorial Circle introduces distracting visual clutter and potential hazards to the ceremonial gateway and nearby Reagan National Airport. Monuments in the nation's capital should honor established, universally recognized legacies of service, not a sitting president and I strongly urge the commission to reject this proposal. Thank you.

name: Lori Carpenter
text: This monument is a monumental waste of taxpayer's money. Its sole purpose is to feed Trump's ego. PLEASE don't approve it.

name: Christina Christl
text: I wish to express that I do not want this arch. I think it's size and location will alter the existing memorials experience in such a way that diminishes them.

name: Andrea Burns
text: No arch. Out of scale. Will sink. Thank you.

name: Chris Helmsworth
text: I am writing to express my opposition to the construction of the arch. Such a structure is out of scale for the rest of the monuments in D.C. Moreover, it would block the view to Arlington Cemetery, a place that I have visited many times and is as close to holy ground as exists in this country. Additionally, while it is clear what other monuments in D.C. commemorate, the purpose of this monument is unclear at this time, and will likely have less meaning to future generations. Please note not approve this construction.

name: peg patton
text: I oppose the Monumental Arch. The location of the proposed Arch will interrupt the highly significant relationship between the Lincoln Memorial, across Arlington Memorial Bridge, to Arlington National Cemetery and Arlington House. One of the most symbolic landscapes in Washington, D.C., the vista was designed to represent the post-Civil War reconciliation of the north and south of the United States. It is because this viewshed carries so much meaning to the country that the National Trust has raised concerns about the proposed Monumental Arch, whose scale, location, and design will disrupt this important visual and symbolic vista. In addition, the Arch will dwarf the Lincoln Memorial and disrupt the long, open, and uninterrupted viewsheds, overwhelming the entry to Arlington National Cemetery—the hallowed resting place of 400,000 veterans and their families and a powerful reminder of American military sacrifice, selfless service, and national unity, all within sight of the monumental core of the Nation's Capital.

name: Cindy Nord
text: The country is in need of funding for so many more important things. The arch project serves no purpose and is nothing more than more eye candy for the president. It means NOTHING to the people of the USA. It is just another distraction from important national and global issues.

name: Lisa Hardigan
text: We don't need any more projects to inflate the president's ego.

name: Theresa McClean
text: My comment to the National Capital Planning Commission, please do not allow this President to change Washington's historic landscapes. This great National capital is being transformed into a Trump Real Estate development and Kingdom instead of what it should be, and what it is OUR NATIONAL CAPITAL!

name: Stacey Van Veen
text: What is this a monument to? I don't want it. If it is built, I will hope that it will be demolished as soon as possible.

name: Greg Friedmann
text: We deeply oppose this arch, as it would destroy the open and symbolic vista between the Lincoln Memorial and Arlington House, once the home of Robert E Lee. It would be an ugly intrusion into the DC landscape. Greg and Beth Friedmann Ashburn VA

name: Theresa Talbott
text: I am writing to express strong opposition to the proposed "Trump Arch" project. At a time when the nation faces significant unmet needs in core public services, it is neither fiscally responsible nor ethically sound to allocate resources to a monumental tribute of this nature. Public funds — whether federal, state, or local — should be directed toward programs that strengthen communities, not toward symbolic structures that offer little practical benefit. Many Americans are struggling to afford basic necessities. Programs such as healthcare subsidies, SNAP benefits, and housing assistance remain underfunded, leaving vulnerable families without the support they need. Investing in a large commemorative arch while essential safety‐net programs face cuts or shortfalls sends the wrong message about our national priorities. It suggests that political symbolism is being elevated above the well‐being of the people government is meant to serve. I am also deeply concerned about the proposed location near Arlington National Cemetery. Arlington is a solemn, sacred space dedicated to honoring those who served and sacrificed for the nation. Introducing a large, politically charged monument risks disrupting the historic landscape, overshadowing existing memorials, and altering the contemplative character of the grounds. Any addition to this area should reflect broad national consensus and serve a unifying purpose — this proposal does neither. I urge you to reject the project and instead focus on investments that directly improve the lives of Americans and preserve the integrity of our most hallowed national sites.

name: Elizabeth Boswell
text: Please stop that ridiculous arch. It is obscene. I saw General Lee right before he came down in Richmond. That is what Americans do to unwanted monuments.

name: Kristina Peters
text: "Asking for forgiveness rather than permission" is not an appropriate way to construct an overly large and intrusive arch or any other offensive edifice. There is a proper way to add a monument to the landscape of Washington DC and this procedure seems to have been ignored. What I have read about the arch indicates that it will dwarf the Lincoln Memorial and relegate the sacred ground of Arlington Cemetery to an obscured view. I am against the building of an unnecessary memorial that serves no purpose and is unwanted. Please do not approve this travesty. Thank you.

name: Marla Taylor
text: I would like to be on record as being against the construction of the arch. It is an unnecessary addition at taxpayer's expense, and it will obscure the view of other memorials.

name: K Thomas
text: Washington DC is a sacred place. Any monument should be approved by the people and voted on, not simply erected without collaboration and consensus. As a US citizen whose ancestors date back to the 1600s, I do not approve of this project.

name: Norene Stephens
text: I have several concerns: 1. It will change a very lovely scene as well as being much too large and high 2. We are not Paris we do not need an arch 3. It doesn't celebrate 250 years of our country. 4. Safety concerns as it is too high for approaching planes at the airport Please stop the waste of money that could be used to help those who are suffering to provide for their families with the high cost of living.

name: Theresa Reichley
text: I do not want to see an arch disrupting the view of our National treasure Arlington National Cemetery. I do not approve of a sitting president erecting anything to honor themselves. No exceptions.

name: Lynne Presley
text: How ridiculous. Haven't we allowed this person to destroy enough of our history? Where is the money coming from? Why deface the entrance to Arlington. We have money for an arch but not enough to feed our children, or seniors or other less fortunate people. We don't need an arch. This is not Russia, Nazi Germany, or North Korea. This is the United States of America. No arch.

name: Jeanette Wenzel
text: Totally unnecessary. This president has done nothing for this country and/or the citizens of the United States to deserve a monument in his name. He has only divided us.

name: Pamela Abbott
text: It is unacceptable to me that we create the proposed Monumental Arch. When gas and food prices are up, and families are having a hard time making ends meet, why would we think this is the time for another monument. I hope the committee will vote no to any arch, ballroom, etc. at this time. Trump said private funds would be used and that's shown to be another lie from this administration.

name: Eleanor Barker
text: This proposed Arch will interrupt the vista that unfolds from the Lincoln Memorial, across Arlington Memorial Bridge, to Arlington National Cemetery and Arlington House. One of the most symbolic landscapes in Washington, D.C., the vista was designed to represent the post-Civil War reconciliation of the north and south of the United States. I'm concerned that the proposed Monumental Arch, whose scale, location, and design will disrupt this important visual and symbolic vista, will dwarf the Lincoln Memorial and disrupt the long, open, and uninterrupted viewsheds, overwhelming the entry to Arlington National Cemetery—the hallowed resting place of 400,000 veterans and their families and a powerful reminder of American military sacrifice, selfless service, and national unity, all within sight of the monumental core of the Nation's Capital. My husband's grandfather is just one of the many revered service members interred at Arlington, and this site should remain as intended: an enduring monument to their sacrifice. Not an enduring monument to one President whose impact on the history and trajectory of this nation is still very much in question. Furthermore, the Eternal Flame has been a constant and permanent feature of the Washington-to-Arlington landscape for the past 63 years. It seems that the arch project is being pushed forward with no substantive analysis of how its negative affects on that specific memorial and the sacred space that Arlington National Cemetery embodies will be mitigated. I submit that the project before the National Capital Planning Commission is deficient and that it cannot approve this project in its current form.

name: Sara Scholtens
text: Dear Commission Members, I am writing to encourage you not to approve the proposed monumental arch in Washington D.C. This particular arch is inappropriate and would be a garish addition to our nation's capital. Indeed, it is being foisted upon the American people with our own hard earned tax dollars. The arch is in actuality a monument to a self-aggrandizing charlatan, not a monument for anything else. Please do not be fooled into thinking this is anything else. I also encourage you to sideline this arch so tax dollars, paid by the public, can used for the public's benefit. There are many truly needy citizens in American who would benefit from the funds that would be wasted on this arch. Thank you for reading my comments. Sincerely, Sara Scholtens

name: Kimberly Stone
text: To Whom it May Concern, Please do NOT approve the monumental arch. I object to: - its disruption of the current intentional relational design between the national cemetery at Arlington and the Lincoln Memorial - the process employed - the use of taxpayer dollars for this project regardless of any new proposed location Thank you for your consideration.

name: Susan Nodine
text: I strongly oppose the proposed memorial arch. It will obscure the view of the Lincoln Memorial while highlighting the home of Robert E Lee. This is nothing but another vanity project for the president. Arlington National Cemetery is sacred ground. Please do not allow this monstrosity to be built.

name: Edith Gibbens
text: To block the entry to Arlington National Cemetery is an act of disrespect. It is totally unacceptable. Please do not approve this or any other change in the future

name: Barbara Hall
text: I have visited Washington DC and been very proud of the Capital area and how favorably it compares with Paris, London, Rome, and other capital cities, in my experience. A huge arch, dwarfing the Lincoln Monument and destroying the views between the Capital and Arlington Cemetery, not to mention the needless expense to taxpayers, is a horrible idea. Given how this administration has proceeded with other abominable projects without approval from anyone other than handpicked cronies, I doubt that public opinion will make a difference, but here's my attempt. Thank you for making an effort to include we, the people.

name: Monica Warner
text: In addition to the demerits that this project carries in terms of placement and design, this project is too expensive for the nation's budget. Taxpayers are already struggling for basic necessities like groceries and fuel. We do not need another monument or project to stroke a sitting President's ego. Thank you for your consideration.

name: Anita Schlaht
text: I am not in favor of this addition to Washington D. C. I have visited D.C. several times in my 73 years. And additions like the statue of MLK and monuments to wars we continue to fight honoring those who have died are appropriate. A president building a monument to himself does not add to the landscape. It detracts and cheapens our capitol. What has he accomplished that is worthy of a permanent commemoration? Let history decide in the future if he deserves this honor.

name: Connie Hale
text: I am against building the Monumental Arch. The arch doesn't suit the area and the construction cost would be better spent elsewhere.

name: Barbara McKinney
text: This arch should not be allowed. It would take away the solemn ambiance of a sacred place devoted to those who gave their lives for this country.

name: Fran Landess
text: I would like to register my opposition to the proposed Monumental Arch. First, I am concerned about the siting on the Arch which would interrupt the sight lines between the Lincoln Memorial and Arlington Cemetery. Second, the height of the monument is completely out of scale with our other important memorials. Third, the plans for the monument have not been reviewed by the National Park Service and the National Historic Preservation Act. Finally, it feels completely inappropriate to build a huge monument to a living President and falsely projects his place in history. Thank you for your thoughtful consideration.

name: Karen Strong
text: Regarding the proposed Arch at the entrance to Arlington National Cemetery: I oppose this proposal for four reasons. First, it would overshadow the entry to Arlington National Cemetery, a hallowed ground that makes its own historical and personal statement which should not be overwhelmed by a triumphal Arch. Second, The Memorial Bridge that connects the Lincoln Memorial to Arlington National Cemetery (and former Lee Mansion) is an intentional and powerful symbolic statement about the Civil War, its cost to the nation, and the restoration of the United States following that war. The proposed Arch would interrupt this meaningful visual connection without any compelling rationale for doing so. Third, the proposed size of the Arch is disproportional to the historic monuments along the Mall in DC. This says more about the ego of the person trying to force the building of the Arch than it does the greatness of our country. The current president claims (and accepts others' claims) to be the greatest American president of all time. The size of the proposed Arch is a symbolic statement that he is more significant than Washington, Jefferson, Lincoln, and FDR. It is really a Trump monument, which is entirely inappropriate during the president's term or, indeed, during his lifetime. And fourth (but not least), the idea of a triumphal Arch is inconsistent with the character of America. We do not have a history of monarchy or royalty or empire. We are a country of the people, by the people, and for the people. That's why the White House is not an imperial palace. That's why the Capitol Building is the centerpiece of the capital city. A grand and huge triumphal Arch is a monument to empire. It does not represent the greatness of America. In summary, I deeply oppose the proposed Arch and request that you deny permission for it to be built. Thank you.

name: Deborah Armstrong
text: The country doesn't need a monumental arch. We have much more important infrastructure needs - repairs to our roads and bridges. The arch is inappropriate and a waste of resources.

name: Barbara Knuckles
text: The proposed arch does not fit with the spirit of the rest of the monuments. It is oversize, unnecessary and disruptive. I strongly oppose it.

name: Susan Bennett
text: I don't think this arch should be built. It will destroy the view of the approach to Arlington National Cemertery which should remain as it is to honor those who made the ultimate sacrifice. It's just another vanity project for Trump and he even has said as much. PLEASE do not allow this travesty to continue.

name: Charles Vavra
text: I am STRONGLY opposed to the proposed "Monumental Arch". Its proposed location will be a desecration to Arlington National Cemetery, one of the most hallowed places in America. It will be an insult to all those who gave their lives for American and their ancestors. In addition, at a time when the national debt is skyrocketing and people are struggling to pay for gasoline and groceries, it is a waste of money. I urge you to vote AGAINST the construction of this monstrous vanity project Thank you Dr Charles Vavra

name: Amy Corr
text: There are far more humane priorities for such amounts of money, and current aesthetics are respectfully balanced. Divert these funds to sustain disadvantaged US citizens, or preserve our parks.

name: Melissa Visek
text: The proposed arch is a vanity project for Trump and should not be built. It is huge, ugly, and unnecessary. When asked who it was for, Trumped replied "me". Some may say he was joking, but he was not. While Americans are finding it difficult to survive paycheck to paycheck, spending American tax dollars on this monstrosity is not good stewardship of our tax dollars. In addition, the location of the proposed Arch will interrupt the highly significant relationship between the Lincoln Memorial, across Arlington Memorial Bridge, to Arlington National Cemetery and Arlington House. One of the most symbolic landscapes in Washington, D.C., the vista was designed to represent the post-Civil War reconciliation of the north and south of the United States. It is because this view carries so much meaning to the country that the National Trust has raised concerns about the proposed Monumental Arch, whose scale, location, and design will disrupt this important visual and symbolic vista. In addition, the Arch will dwarf the Lincoln Memorial and disrupt the long, open, and uninterrupted views, overwhelming the entry to Arlington National Cemetery—the hallowed resting place of 400,000 veterans and their families and a powerful reminder of American military sacrifice, selfless service, and national unity. This arch should NOT be built, not only for the reasons stated above but also because of the chaos of construction at such a busy trafficked area. How will traffic be rerouted during construction? You can't build something of this monstrous size over a heavily traveled area without seriously interfering with traffic.

name: Melissa Morgenson
text: Please do not approve the plans to build a monument arch in Washington, DC. The location of the proposed Arch will interrupt the highly significant relationship between the Lincoln Memorial, across Arlington Memorial Bridge, to Arlington National Cemetery and Arlington House. The plans for the arch are positively hideous and will detract negatively from all other monumental structures. As one of the most symbolic landscapes in Washington, D.C., the original vista was designed to represent the post-Civil War reconciliation of the north and south of the United States. It is because this views carries so much meaning that the National Trust has valid concerns about the proposed Monumental Arch whose scale, location, and design will ruin this important visual and symbolic view. In addition, the Arch will dwarf the Lincoln Memorial and disrupt the long, open, and uninterrupted views, overwhelming the entry to Arlington National Cemetery—the hallowed resting place of 400,000 veterans and their families and a powerful reminder of American military sacrifice, selfless service, and national unity, all within sight of the monumental core of the Nation's Capital. This cannot possibly be built given the horrific plans. Please do not approve it.

name: Stacia Ehlen
text: Please do not allow any additional monuments to be built. The new arch would disrupt the sanctity of the area.

name: Sue Kayton
text: We already have enough public monuments in Washington DC and do not need another one. Please do not spend taxpayer money on this wasteful, ugly project. Thank you.

name: N. Kathleen Wenzel
text: As a taxpayer, I object to this consideration of building this monstrosity in the proposed location. It appears to be nothing short of a vanity project for this president proposed without thought to the impact it will have on the current views and highlights of that corridor. It is oversized, grandiose, ugly as designed and serves no commemorative purpose. It has not undergone the requisite historical or preservationist vetting or contract bidding as required by law and custom. This president does not own the federal land and is not authorized to create all these projects without the valid review, consent, and assessment of the various commissions in charge of approving these projects and appropriate Congressional allocation and acceptance of bid contracts. This "project" has not been undertaken in the appropriate and proper stewardship of public land and taxpayer dollars as required. Please do NOT go forward with any approval or permit any building or clearing of federal land for this "project".

name: Cynthia Greenleaf
text: As a citizen who brought my aging father to Washington DC for the first time in his life, I can attest to the impact the open vistas and dignified national monuments have on a new and patriotic visitor. My father took off his hat at the Lincoln Memorial, stood speechless and moved at Arlington, and quietly read the inscriptions at the Jefferson. He had traveled all over the world, but said nothing - not the pyramids of Egypt, not the great churches of Europe - was a more spectacular sight than his own national capitol. I am therefore disheartened and horrified by the prospect of a garish, oversized arch designed to dwarf the exiting sobering monuments. In fact, I would consider it an arch to nowhere. There is no particular triumph to point to, no understandable content to justify this proposed, massive monstrosity. I agree wholeheartedly with The National Trust for Historic Preservation in the United States and ask that this monument to arrogance and hubris not be allowed to tarnish our beautiful national capitol.

name: Jo Levy
text: As a former resident of Alexandria, I remember with pleasure the feeling of tradition and humility that is stimulated by the monuments in Washington and Virginia. A "triumphal arch" has no place in the same category as the Lincoln Memorial, the Vietnam wall, or the Washington Monument. In addition, my in-laws are buried in Arlington cemetery. My father-in-law served with pride during World War II and the Korean War. He saw and suffered from the damage done by war, and he would be horrified to have the horrors of warfare and the memory of those who endured them associated with a monument to pride. Please do not build this arch. Thank you for listening.

name: Janet Gollofon
text: Dear NCPC, I write in opposition to the building of a Triumphal Arch in our nation's capital. This project would greatly harm the historical design of the view/vista from the Lincoln Memorial to Arlington National Cemetery. It is an ill-conceived vanity project by one man. A huge waste of money, money that could be spent in so many other useful ways. At a time when our country is facing so many challenges, a project such as this seems absolutely ridiculous. I urge you to reject and oppose its construction immediately. Thank you.

name: Michelle Lalor
text: An arch this large, at this location, will pull focus from the hallowed ground of American service members. This is not a place for sightseeing and posing for photographs. People, FAMILIES, come here to grieve. What a horrible idea, please do not agree to this.

name: Julia Lawrence
text: Do not build this arch. It is not needed nor wanted by the majority of US Citizens. Our tax dollars are better spend trying to make our lives better than to build an arch. It looks terrible. It will be an eyesore.

name: Pam Foy
text: I'm absolutely opposed to the Arch being built. It is a waste of taxpayer money and a slap in the face to our nation's veterans. Thank you for your consideration.

name: Janis Artz
text: We do not need or want this monstrosity. It will ruin the dignity of the area. Please do not allow. Thank you

name: Tanya Pead
text: National Capital Planning Commission I am writing to urge you to deny the building of the proposed Monumental Arch. The location of the proposed Arch will interrupt the highly significant relationship between the Lincoln Memorial, across Arlington Memorial Bridge, to Arlington National Cemetery and Arlington House. This area is one of the most symbolic landscapes in Washington, D.C., a vista that was designed to represent the post-Civil War reconciliation of the north and south of the United States. It is because this landscape carries so much meaning to the country that I am deeply concerned about the proposed Monumental Arch, whose scale, location, and design will disrupt this important visual and symbolic vista. In addition, the Arch will dwarf the Lincoln Memorial and disrupt the long, open, and uninterrupted views, overwhelming the entry to Arlington National Cemetery—the hallowed resting place of 400,000 veterans and their families and a powerful reminder of American military sacrifice, selfless service, and national unity, all within sight of the monumental core of the Nation's Capital. Above all, this arch is political propaganda. When asked what the Monument Arch was for, Donald Trump has directly pointed to himself. The use of this type of monument is to assert a show of power regardless of public consensus. Please deny the approval for building this Arch. Thank you

name: Julie Strange
text: I am writing in opposition to the proposed Triumphal Arch. The location of the proposed Arch will interrupt the highly significant relationship between the Lincoln Memorial, across Arlington Memorial Bridge, to Arlington National Cemetery and Arlington House. One of the most symbolic landscapes in Washington, D.C., the vista was designed to represent the post-Civil War reconciliation of the north and south of the United States. It is because this viewshed carries so much meaning to the country that the National Trust has raised concerns about the proposed Monumental Arch, whose scale, location, and design will disrupt this important visual and symbolic vista. In addition, the Arch will dwarf the Lincoln Memorial and disrupt the long, open, and uninterrupted viewsheds, overwhelming the entry to Arlington National Cemetery. The cemetery is the hallowed resting place of 400,000 veterans and their families and a powerful reminder of American military sacrifice, selfless service, and national unity, all within sight of the monumental core of the Nation's Capital. It is important to keep this view uninterrupted. And while the Commemorative Works Act, codified mainly at 40 U.S.C. §§ 8901–8909. Under 40 U.S.C. § 8903(c): "A commemorative work commemorating … an individual … may not be authorized until after … death of the individual …" may not apply to this particular location proposed for the arch, the intent of the law is to ensure that the Nation's most significant commemorative landscapes are not used to elevate contemporary political figures or movements before history has had the opportunity to judge their lasting significance and legacy. The proposed Triumphal Arch is inconsistent with both the spirit of the Commemorative Works Act and the longstanding bipartisan tradition of preserving the monumental core of Washington, D.C., as a place of national unity, reflection, and historical continuity rather than political spectacle or personal glorification.

name: Pamela Schiffleger
text: I strongly oppose the proposed Monumental Arch at Memorial Circle. For anyone who knows this landscape firsthand—whether from the Lincoln Memorial, Arlington National Cemetery, Memorial Bridge, or the circle itself—this is one of the worst possible places to insert a massive new structure. This proposal would destroy one of the most beautiful and meaningful viewsheds in the region. This is not an empty traffic island in need of a centerpiece; it is one of the most significant civic and commemorative landscapes in the country. As the National Trust for Historic Preservation has noted, this site carries extraordinary visual and symbolic meaning. The open vista connecting the Lincoln Memorial, Arlington Memorial Bridge, Arlington National Cemetery, and Arlington House was intentionally designed to express national unity and post-Civil War reconciliation. Arlington Memorial Bridge was kept low specifically to preserve these relationships and viewsheds. Placing a triumphal arch of this size and scale at Memorial Circle would interrupt that carefully designed composition, dwarf the Lincoln Memorial, and overwhelm the solemn entrance to Arlington National Cemetery. A monument of this scale is simply incompatible with a place defined by openness, restraint, and reverence. The proposal also fails on basic public use and access grounds. Memorial Circle is already difficult to navigate, and adding a major new destination there would only worsen traffic confusion and create a pedestrian nightmare in a location that is not easy or intuitive for people to reach on foot. If the goal is to create a public monument, it should be placed somewhere people can safely and comfortably experience it—not in a location that degrades a historic landscape while creating new circulation problems. I urge the National Capital Planning Commission to reject this proposal, require full historic and environmental review, and consider alternatives that protect this nationally significant vista rather than permanently damaging it.

name: Kimberly Burkard
text: I am opposed to the proposed Monumental Arch at Memorial Circle on the George Washington Memorial Parkway, near Arlington National Cemetery and along the Potomac River. name: Jim rogers
text: This is a horrible and unnecessary project. Please do not proceed. Any future new national monument should be carefully planned with public input

name: Catherine Nardone
text: The proposed 250-foot "Independence Arch" in Washington, D.C. is an egregious misuse of taxpayer funds. This vanity project holds no genuine historical meaning and threatens to permanently desecrate the solemn vistas between the Lincoln Memorial and Arlington National Cemetery.

name: Carroll Walsh
text: i am writing to oppose the construction of the proposed Monumental Arch at Memorial Circle. At an estimated $15 million, this is an irresponsible use of public funds at a time when our deficit is soaring out of control and many Americans struggling to make ends meet. The proposed location will interrupt the deeply meaningful visual and historic relationship between the Lincoln Memorial, Arlington Memorial Bridge, Arlington National Cemetery, and Arlington House — a corridor that honors those who gave their lives for this country. The arch would stand more than twice the height of the Lincoln Memorial , overwhelming a landscape that belongs to all Americans and to the memory of our fallen. Washington already has a world-class collection of monuments. This project prioritizes spectacle over substance, and federal dollars should instead go toward the maintenance of existing memorials, veterans' services, and infrastructure. I urge the Commission to reject this absurd waste of taxpayer dollars.

name: APRIL WENNERSTROM
text: Dear National Capital Planning Commission, I am writing to express my strong opposition to the proposed construction of a "Trump Memorial Arch." National protected spaces that preserve natural beauty, shared heritage, and historically significant sites rooted in broad, enduring national consensus. Introducing a monument that commemorates a single, recent, and highly polarizing political figure risks undermining the integrity and nonpartisan spirit that the country demands. Such a project would fundamentally alter the purpose of gateway, shifting them away from reflection and preservation toward contemporary political expression. We have a responsibility to steward public lands and gateways in a way that is inclusive, educational, and respectful of the diversity of perspectives held by Americans. Memorials within the system have traditionally been reserved for individuals and events whose legacies have been evaluated over time and whose contributions are widely recognized as unifying. Establishing a monument of this nature at this moment not only departs from that precedent but may also set a concerning example for future proposals driven by short-term political agendas rather than enduring historical significance. I respectfully urge the Commission to reject this proposal and to reaffirm its commitment to preserving the space that transcend political division. With limited space and resources, it is essential that decisions about monuments reflect careful, long-term consideration and emphasize unity, education, and conservation. Thank you for your attention to this matter and for your continued stewardship of our nation's most treasured landscapes and gateways.

name: Jennifer Stocz
text: I am writing to oppose the proposed Monumental Arch at Memorial Circle and to urge the National Capital Planning Commission to reject the current concept. The vista connecting the Lincoln Memorial, across Arlington Memorial Bridge, to Arlington National Cemetery and Arlington House is one of the most intentional and meaningful landscapes in the United States. It was designed to represent the reconciliation of a divided nation after the Civil War. Arlington Memorial Bridge was deliberately kept low in profile precisely so that this symbolic relationship could remain unbroken. The proposed Arch would sever that connection — visually, symbolically, and permanently. The scale of this structure is simply incompatible with its surroundings. At a height that would dwarf the Lincoln Memorial, the Arch would not complement the existing monumental landscape — it would dominate it. The long, open viewsheds that define the National Mall and its western terminus at the Lincoln Memorial reflect more than a century of deliberate planning. That tradition of restraint and careful stewardship deserves to be honored, not overridden. I am also troubled by the proposed location at the entrance to Arlington National Cemetery. This is a working memorial. Thirty funeral services are held there every day. The Cemetery's character — solemn, unadorned, defined by uniform rows of simple white headstones — is itself a form of tribute. An oversized triumphal arch at its gates is inconsistent with that solemnity and risks reducing one of our most sacred national spaces to a backdrop. Finally, I want to note that the required Section 106 review under the National Historic Preservation Act has not yet been completed. Approving this project before that process concludes would bypass a legal safeguard that exists specifically to protect historic resources like these. The NCPC should not move forward until that review is finished. I urge the Commission to reject the proposed Arch in its current form and to insist on a process that respects both the legal requirements and the irreplaceable character of this landscape.

name: Alicia Zeedyk
text: The proposed arch is disrespectful to the soldiers at Arlington. Please do not allow this monstrosity to happen. Than you.

name: Claire Fleisch

name: Bruce Katz
text: I am utterly opposed to the creation of the Monumental Arch. Its design is more monstrous than monumental and its proximity to Arlington Cemetery is offensive. Arlington is a deliberately quiet memorial site meant to honor those who served to protect the country. The tallest structure in the cemetery is the 90-foot high flagpole. Its massive size would celebrate neither duty nor sacrifice but only itself. "Triumph" is precisely the wrong message to be conveyed at so sombre a site. Frankly it looks like the kind of self-congratulatory structure that Napoleon might have ordered built -- or worse, that might have been proposed in Berlin back in the 1930s. Moreover it would be an eyesore, interrupting the current line of sight from the cemetery to the Lincoln Memorial and the Mall. Look: This Arch is not America. name: Laurie Feldman
text: I have read the following comments from the National Trust for Historic Preservation and agree with each and everyone of their concerns: We respectfully submit the following comments concerning the current proposal by the Executive Office of the President and the U.S. Department of the Interior to construct a new Triumphal Arch at Memorial Circle on the George Washington Memorial Parkway. We urge the U.S. Commission of Fine Arts ("CFA") to consider these comments in connection with its responsibility under the Commemorative Works Act, following consultation with the National Capital Memorial Advisory Commission, to approve site and design proposals for commemorative works so that such works do not "interfere with, or encroach on, an existing commemorative work and to the maximum extent practicable, protect open space, existing public use, and cultural and natural resources." We would also remind the members of the CFA that the Commemorative Works Act requires the project to be approved by Congress. After reviewing the revised concept plans that have been submitted to CFA, the National Trust remains concerned about the location, height, scale, and design of the proposed Triumphal Arch, the manner in which it interferes with existing commemorative works and fails to protect existing public uses and cultural resources. Notwithstanding comments and recommendations by Commission members at the April 2026 meeting, the modifications to the proposal have been minimal. Most notably, the 68-foot-high sculpture at the top of the proposed Arch has not been removed or reduced, contrary to the Commissioners' recommendation. The location of the proposed Arch, at Memorial Circle, will interrupt the highly significant relationship between the Lincoln Memorial, across Arlington Memorial Bridge, to Arlington National Cemetery and Arlington House. One of the most symbolic landscape vistas in Washington, DC, the vista was designed to represent the post-Civil War reconciliation of the north and south of the United States. Arlington Memorial Bridge was intentionally designed with a low profile to respect the visual and symbolic vistas connecting the National Mall and National Cemetery. If constructed as planned at the proposed location, the new Triumphal Arch will obscure the intentional axial and aesthetic relationships between the Lincoln Memorial, Arlington Memorial Bridge, and Arlington House. The National Trust is also deeply concerned about the unprecedented height and scale of the proposed Triumphal Arch, which will overwhelm the Lincoln Memorial, Arlington National Cemetery, and Arlington House. The proposed Arch would be double the size of the Lincoln Memorial and would risk disrespecting this powerful and beloved monument. As such, the Triumphal Arch is inconsistent with the McMillan Plan and subsequent planning decisions that have stewarded the National Mall as a unified composition characterized by long, open, and uninterrupted viewsheds, with a clear hierarchy of monumental elements, that culminates at its western end at the Lincoln Memorial. In addition, the proposed location of the Arch, at the entrance to Arlington National Cemetery, is inconsistent with the solemn historic character of Arlington National Cemetery. The hallowed resting place of 400,000 veterans and their families, Arlington National Cemetery is a powerful reminder of American military sacrifice, selfless service, and national unity, all within sight of the monumental core of the Nation's Capital. Distinguished by the Tomb of the Unknowns, Memorial Avenue, and rolling hillsides of uniform rows of simple headstones, Arlington National Cemetery is a living memorial that honors thirty funeral services each day. The Arch, as proposed, would dominate Arlington National Cemetery, and be inconsistent with its hallowed character of solemn graves with powerful, unadorned white markers. Finally, it is important to note that review of the proposal under Section 106 of the National Historic Preservation Act has not yet been initiated. We understand that the National Park Service will be initiating Section 106 consultation soon, but the statute mandates that the review process be completed "prior to" approval of the project. 54 U.S.C. § 306108. In addition, based on past experience with Section 106 consultation in the National Capitol region, the proposed plans will be improved in response to the collaborative review and comments from the expert professional staff of the involved agencies, including the Commission itself. We urge the Commission members to await the Section 106 process, which has not yet been initiated.

text: I agree with the statement from the National Trust. When we visited Washington in 2000, the unobstructed view from the Arlington Cemetery to the Lincoln Memorial was awe inspiring. One of the most symbolic landscape vistas in Washington, DC, the vista was designed to represent the post-Civil War reconciliation of the north and south of the United States. The National Trust is also deeply concerned about the unprecedented height and scale of the proposed Triumphal Arch, which would overwhelm the Lincoln Memorial, Arlington National Cemetery, and Arlington House. The proposed Arch would especially diminish and disrupt the iconic and powerful presence of the beloved Lincoln Memorial. The proposed location of the Arch is also inconsistent with the solemn historic character of Arlington National Cemetery. As the hallowed resting place of 400,000 veterans and their families, Arlington National Cemetery is a powerful reminder of American military sacrifice, and national unity, all within sight of the monumental core of the Nation's Capital. The Arch, as proposed, would dominate the National Cemetery, and would be inconsistent with its solemn and hallowed character.

name: Mary Crawford

name: Lauren Geiselhofer
text: I respectfully oppose the proposed Monumental Arch at Memorial Circle because of the impact it could have on one of the most historically and symbolically important landscapes in the country. The existing viewshed between the Lincoln Memorial, Arlington Memorial Bridge, Arlington National Cemetery, and Arlington House was intentionally designed to represent unity and reconciliation following the Civil War. The openness and uninterrupted visual connection between these landmarks is a meaningful part of the experience and historical significance of the site. The proposed Arch would introduce a very large new structure into a space that currently draws its strength from simplicity, openness, and reflection. In my opinion, its scale and placement could disrupt the historic relationship between these landmarks and compete with the character of the surrounding memorial landscape. Arlington National Cemetery is an especially solemn and sacred place honoring generations of service members and their families. Any additions to this setting should carefully preserve the dignity and clarity of the space rather than become a dominant visual feature. While I appreciate the intention behind creating new memorials and public spaces, this proposal feels out of place within the historic context of Memorial Circle and the monumental core. I encourage the committee to reconsider this proposal or explore alternative locations that would have less impact on this nationally significant landscape.

name: Cheryl Shipley

name: Susan Wohlander
text: I do not approve of the proposed Trump arch in Washington, D.C. because I believe our nation's capital should reflect unity, democratic values, and respect for the broader history of the United States rather than elevate a single modern political figure in such a grand and permanent way. Monuments and architectural landmarks in Washington are traditionally reserved for honoring presidents and leaders whose legacies have been fully evaluated over time and whose contributions are widely recognized across party lines. Creating a monumental arch dedicated to Donald Trump while political divisions surrounding him remain intense risks deepening national polarization rather than fostering civic pride. Washington, D.C. is not meant to serve as a platform for political branding or personal glorification. The city's memorials are intended to honor sacrifice, constitutional principles, and the enduring institutions of American democracy. A Trump arch could easily be viewed as partisan symbolism rather than a unifying national tribute. Regardless of one's political beliefs, public monuments should strive to represent ideals that bring Americans together. Additionally, there are more pressing priorities deserving public attention and funding, including infrastructure, veterans' services, education, and preserving existing historical landmarks. Building a massive new monument centered on a living and highly controversial political figure sends the wrong message about national priorities. For these reasons, I believe such a project would diminish the dignity and historical balance of Washington, D.C. rather than enhance it.
