text: Dear Mr. Cook, I am concerned about the location, height, scale, and design of the proposed Triumphal Arch, and the manner in which it interferes with existing commemorative works and fails to protect existing public uses and cultural resources. I feel the unprecedented height and scale of the proposed Triumphal Arch will overwhelm the Lincoln Memorial, Arlington National Cemetery, and Arlington House. In addition, the proposed location of the Arch, at the entrance to Arlington National Cemetery, would be inconsistent with its hallowed character of solemn graves of our beloved heros. Finally, Section 106 of the National Historic Preservation Act mandates that a review process be completed "prior to" approval of the project. I believe we must wait for such approval to initiate any construction on this arch. Sincerely, Margaret Hoppenrath

name: Karen johnson
text: I do NOT support the building of the eyesore arch. Please do NOT. let them build this. It serves no purpose and takes away from the historic meaning of the current view. Please vote NO!!!

name: Heather Hall
text: This arch absolutely should NOT be built. It is a gaudy monumental eyesore that we the taxpayers should not indulge the administration at this time of obscene inflation, escalating gas and grocery prices and the massive reduction of healthcare and food aid needed by a huge section of taxpayers. In addition the proposed location is completely inappropriate, blocking planned views and obstructing access. Do your jobs to protect these sacred spaces from tawdry clutter. If he wants a massive monument have him pay for it himself on his own property at a golf course.

name: McCaslin Donna
text: This arch looks European, not American. Such placement will dwarf the Lincoln Memorial and obstruct the view from Washington DC your most important and sacred armed forces cemetery in Arlington. Not to mention the traffic mess. Allowing the current administration to reshape the capitol city in his tacky, gold, ornate Mar a Lago image any further would be a mistake. It will take years to return OUR HOUSE and Capitol to its tasteful & simple grandeur.

name: John Valter
text: This arch is a tribute to one man's vanity and should not be built.

name: Ellen Carpenter
text: The proposed "Monumental Arch" is a monument to one person's ego. It does not belong anywhere on the National Mall and certainly not interrupting the sight line from the Lincoln Memorial to Arlington National Cemetery. Please do whatever is necessary to STOP this monstrosity from happening.

name: Karen Fitzgerald
text: Please do not permit the proposed new arch to be built. The current landscaping of the area symbolizes the outcome of the Civil War with the cemetery and Lincoln Memorial in alignment.

name: Ellen Kruger
text: Hello. Thank you for providing an avenue for comments on this historical and important piece of our American history. I have been fortunate enough to visit Washington DC with my son on his 8th grade trip. The experience was immeasurable, not only for me but for all the students. Understanding the design and purpose of the placements of monuments was a significance i did not understand until I visited. In an strongly, STRONGLY against the costume of this arch in every way. Not only does it have a negative impact on the views from Lincoln memorial to Arlington, or had no historical purpose commemorating fallen heroes or milestones in the creation and saving of our democracy. This is a vanity project by the current administration. It is an expense that is unnecessary and vulgar in the face of struggling families across this nation. It is a repulsive proposal, which I strongly suspect, if completed, will cost millions more in the future to deconstruct. Please put a stop to this ego fulfilling eye sore in our nations beautiful Capitol. Thank you.

name: Jonathan Gittins
text: I would prefer that this not be built. If previous administrations and congresses did not feel this was necessary for America 250, then I'm not sure why one person would supercede those decisions. As a taxpayer, I would want to ensure that, if this were built, it would be done in a way to minimize costs. This current administration seems to find a way to inflate costs to include all the grift. There would need to be a rebidding process to ensure this. One person cannot just decide to give it to a certain firm and then allow costs to balloon because each group involved needs to get their cut.

name: Clare Fahy
text: I feel that the new monumental arch should not be built at Memorial Circle for the following reasons. 1, The scale of the arch is extremely large compared to the buildings and existing memorials nearby. It will dwarf the size of the Lincoln Memorial. 2, The arch will disrupt the view to and from Arlington National Cemetery. This is hallowed ground for Veterans, families and the American public. The view is part of the respectfully atmosphere established there many years ago. 3, The arch's design, oversized scale and poor location do not fit with the other symbolic buildings and grounds in this beautiful area. I urge you to vote against building the memorial arch.

name: Donn Brous
text: I am opposed to the proposal to build the Monumental Arch. My reasons are the same ones you are no doubt receiving from many members of the publlic. My primary objection, among others, is that it will not be a good use of money when we have so many people in need. My second objection is that the proposed design/size is inappropriate. It diminishes the current "landscape" of monuments that are so breathtaking as is. It is not a good fit. There are dozens of other higher priorities. Please vote against this proposal and any modification that might be offered. We don't need it.

name: Donna Henrickson
text: The Legislative Branch of Congress reviews and votes to or not to approve every taxpayer project proposal in the U.S. Has NCPC, CFA, NPS and AOC weighed in to the Legislative Branch regarding the new arch proposal and passed their recommendations to Congress yet? Only the Legislative Branch of government has authority to authorize taxpayer funded projects. The congressional House and Senate's job is to analyze the need for every proposed project that requires taxpayer funding, how the location and surrounding location of a project will be impacted, ensure that there is not already a similar project U.S. citizens are already funding, determine how much it would actually really cost to complete the proposed project if it is approved, including maintenance costs into the future with taxpayer funding. After your input, and congressional consideration, project go to the next level of being bid out to find the most knowledgeable, skilled, reliable contractor capable of completing potential projects through SAM in order to consider realistic cost numbers to move the project to a vote. The arch idea cannot move forward until the requisite bid documents, including architecture schematics, build out timetable specs and realistic budgetary documents for the project have been analyzed and voted on by the entire Legislative Branch. The congressional House and Senate's job is to analyze the need for every proposed project that requires taxpayer funding, how the location and surrounding location of a project will be impacted, ensure we don't already have a similar project U.S. citizens are paying for, determine how much it would actually really cost to complete the project if it is approved, including future maintenance costs with taxpayer funding. After a complete analysis, The Legislative Branch takes a vote to make sure every State in all 50 United States gets to weigh in on the decision to approve or not to approve every project with a congressional vote. — that's the way America works. The arch idea has not been approved. It is still way too early in the approval process. Images have been seen already breaking ground without approval. Please submit your observations and recommendations to Congress as soon as possible to enable a vote in the House and Senate. The Trump arch, should it be built, is arguably a more disgusting attack on Washington, D.C., than the ballroom. That's because the arch would pretty much wreck the carefully designed sight lines of the nation's capital city. It would block the sight of and ability for funeral processions going to Arlington National Cemetary and the many families visiting Arlington National Cemetary daily. It would dwarf the Lincoln Memorial, blocking the sightline between that and the memorial for Ulysses S. Grant. The current arch plan would totally obliterate the building height limitations in the national Capital area which are currently set at 130 high in the U.S. Constitution. The proposed 250 foot height of the Trump arch + the 68 foot statue on top of the arch makes the arch 318 feet tall — the equivalent of a 30 story building. This arch project will need to be submitted to Congress for review and a vote by all Senate and House representatives from all 50 States. Please consider the following points in your recommendations for this arch project: — We have learned that an arch idea was submitted to Congress 102 years ago, so the arch project should not need congressional approval. That is false. Times have changed. Among other changes in the past 102 years, we now have airplane and helicopter landings in multiple locations throughout Washington D.C. to factor into the situation now. — We have learned that the proposed arch will not be a traditional arch. It is now intending to include many galleries, a gift shop, 30 stories of elevators and stairs, an observation floor and be 250 feet (20-25 stories) plus a 68 foot statue on top making it approximately 30 stories tall. — With the building limit set at 130 feet in the D.C. National Capital region, what would we be observing from the top of a 250 foot tall + 68 foot topper arch? Roofs. Now that we know the arch is envisioned to be a gallery, gift shop, observation tower tourism destination, where would people park? — The only thing we have seen of the design of this arch is the gift shop trinket of the French arch, just like one I bought in Paris. We have seen a round about looking idea to get past the arch in a vehicle. But now that it is a tourism destination, parking there or getting around the round about is a whole different story. It does not look like there will be space for a giant parking lot there. We definitely need more of a plan for Congress to assess what would really become of the National Capital memorials already there. — The building height in Washington, D.C. is still strictly limited. Governed by the federal Height of Buildings Act of 1910, buildings on commercial streets are generally capped at 130 feet (about 11 to 12 stories).The exact regulations in the District of Columbia vary by location: Commercial Streets: Height is restricted to the width of the street it faces plus 20 feet, with an absolute maximum cap of 130 feet. Pennsylvania Avenue: The section between the U.S. Capitol and the White House has a slightly higher exception of 160 feet. Residential Streets: Generally capped at 90 feet (or less, depending on the specific width of the street). Because these are federal regulations enforced by the National Capital Planning Commission and local zoning laws, changing them would require an act of Congress. — This arch project, as it sounds now, seems like a duplicate taxpayer project. The many Smithsonian museums on the National Mall already are America's taxpayer funded treasure. Our cherished United States Smithsonian Museums already have a long standing program of documenting the history of the United States of America as our premiere tourism destination. The Smithsonian already encompasses many buildings with historic exhibits, galleries and museums, many gift shops, many many elevators and stairs, and, offers several observation towers for airplane viewing and public astronomical observatories for viewing the sun and stars. The Smithsonian has several facilities dedicated to observation: Astronomical Observatories: The National Air and Space Museum on the National Mall in Washington, D.C. features a public observatory where visitors can use safe, solar-filtered telescopes to observe the Sun, the Moon, and other objects in space. Observation Tower: The Donald D. Engen Observation Tower at the Steven F. Udvar-Hazy Center in Chantilly, Virginia (near Washington Dulles International Airport). It stands 164 feet tall, offering a 360-degree view of airplanes taking off and landing, complete with live Air Traffic Control audio streaming. Research Observatory: The Smithsonian runs the Smithsonian Astrophysical Observatory (SAO). Headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, it operates alongside the Harvard College Observatory as a major center for studying the universe. Thank you so much to each of our organizations, NCPC, CFA, NPS and AOC for your stalwart watch over our National Capital memorials and historic treasures. And thank you for your valued recommendations to the Legislative Branch of Congress to ensure our Senators and House Representatives have the information necessary to make the best possible decisions as they vote for or against newly proposed ideas. Thank you for insuring we are putting ultimate respect and care front and center for the United States of America's national treasures.

name: Deas Bohn
text: This construction is a travesty. Yet another vanity project that benefits no American citizen, denigrates existing monuments, illegally uses tax payer money. Do not approve this construction.

name: Kathi Marak
text: Dear Sir or Madam, I strongly oppose construction of this garish project in Washington DC. Our nation's capitol is carefully and thoughtfully laid out to stress the ideals of its citizens. This arch in no way reflects the people's image of our great country. Thank you, Kathi Marak

name: Diane White
text: I am not in favor of this new proposal for the monumental arch. It would disrupt the view and hinder the sentiment of Arlington National Cemetery. Also, no living president should erect a monument that is "dedicated" to him or his name. Money issues are not clear and the arch or building of it should not be paid for by taxing or going into further debt. It is not clear to me from where this money is really coming. Right now especially the American people are paying higher prices for gas, supplies etc. This is not an appropriate time or way to spend additional money, even if "donated".

name: Mary Callahan
text: As a US citizen I strongly oppose the construction of the proposed monumental arch.

name: Jan Adamczyk
text: Absolutely not. This is a vanity project not a memorial consistent with our values. We do not need or want this and it disrespects those buried at Arlington. Use the funds to help veterans rather than creating a stain on the landscape.

name: Sandy Shoulders
text: Under no circumstances should this project move forward. Glorification of this administration is already to the level of grotesque. These are the things that tyrants and dictators do, not the president of the United States. Stop the project please.

name: Helen Clark
text: I oppose this project as it will ruin the sightlines to Arlington Cemetery. Arlington Cemetery and the soldiers buried there (and their families) should always take precedence over this vanity project. It would be an architectural monstrosity, way too large in scale, and not at all complementary with surrounding memorials.

name: Lisa Grohsman
text: This is an unnecessary project at taxpayer expense. It will cause more traffic accidents at even more cost to taxpayers. Donald Trump has an ego problem. No American taxpayer wants this monstrosity.

name: Barbara Hoffman
text: I am totally opposed to the erection of the new Monumental Arch. America does not need this arch. It would inappropriately frame views in both directions, and it adds nothing significant to the beauty of our nation's Capital. It is also inappropriate because its purpose is to glorify a current sitting president.

name: Lisa Ey
text: Please stop the construction of the Washington D.C. Arch. It's massive size will obstruct the views of the Lincoln Memorial and disturb the tranquil and solemn views of Arlington Cemetery. One person should not be allowed to destroy the amazing architectural scenery in America's Capitol. Something like this and construction at the White House needs to go through hearings where the citizens are involved in the discussions and Congress votes on releasing funds for these extremely large and extremely expensive projects. Right now so many citizens are homeless and in dire financial situations due to the bad economy. Now is the worst time to fund such vanity projects. Please stop this waste of taxpayer money and divert the money towards helping citizens who are hurting!

name: Carolyn Sundquist
text: Please do not approve the Monumental Arch. The location of this arch will desecrate the most symbolic landscapes in Washington. The relationship of the Lincoln Memorial, across the memorial Bridge to Arlington Cemetery and Arlington House would be overwhelmed by this gaudy and unnecessary tribute to the most corrupt president to have ever lead the United States. It's bad enough he is destroying the White House, which does not belong to him, do not let him taint this historic representation of the reconciliation of the north and south after the Civil War.

name: Sandra Mack
text: This arch is nothing more than self agrandisement for Donald Trump. It would destroy the solemnity of the space between the Lincoln memorial and the entrsnce to the Arlington national cemetary. It is an expensive waste of federal taxpayer funds. We need to focus on the real issues plaguing the American people, not on "decoratng" the solemn national parks.. please stop funding this self serving nonsence.

name: Michelle Oconnell
text: The location of the proposed Arch will interrupt the highly significant relationship between the Lincoln Memorial, across Arlington Memorial Bridge, to Arlington National Cemetery and Arlington House. One of the most symbolic landscapes in Washington, D.C., the vista was designed to represent the post-Civil War reconciliation of the north and south of the United States. It is because this viewshed carries so much meaning that I have concerns about the proposed Monumental Arch, whose scale, location, and design will disrupt this important visual and symbolic vista. In addition, the Arch will dwarf the Lincoln Memorial and disrupt the long, open, and uninterrupted viewsheds, overwhelming the entry to Arlington National Cemetery—the hallowed resting place of 400,000 veterans and their families and a powerful reminder of American military sacrifice, selfless service, and national unity.

name: Virginia Gowen
text: There are so many other needs in this country. I just shake my head and am astonished at this project. It is placed in an area that will visually destroy what is meant to be a historical connection between Arlington and Lincoln. Building a monument to oneself is an awful idea. Who the heck does this? Wouldn't it be great if this were something that all of the voters could have a say in? Why can't this be a ballot question?

name: Kathleen Stephenson
text: Please do not allow he building of this arch in this spot. Adding or changing monuments in Washington DC should be a highly intentional and rare process done after thoughtful consideration and evaluation of the messaging and of the effects on surrounding space and structures. It should never be done at the whim of one person.

name: Joyce Hervey
text: No New Monumental Arch! NO NO NO This is a waste of tax dollars and interferes with the already beautiful scenery we have. This is the United State of America, not the Trump States of America. NO New Monumental Arch! NO NO NO

name: Tanya Zimmer
text: I am totally opposed to the construction of the monument memorial arch . It is too big . It doesn't align with historical representation of the current monuments in Washington DC . It is especially objectionable in terms that it overshadows the Lincoln Memorial which is one of our most treasured and beloved memorials . Please oppose its construction.

name: Patricia Cole
text: The is America. This is the United States of America. Any president of the United States who insists upon building monuments to himself while in office is not a president of a free country. This ugly, unAmerican arch is a copy of other arches around the world - there is nothing unique, interesting or beautiful about its design or its intent. It will be an eternal blight on the landscape of our country's capital. Letting the LEAST popular president in the history of the United States build himself a gold-bedecked monument while he is still in office is an affront to democracy. It would be a monument to failure. If this thing gets built, I will, personally find a way to go spit on it before I die. I imagine many Americans will find a way to express their personal displeasure with this horrific tombstone of a structure if it is ever constructed. Once constructed, I feel certain it will be the first monument to an American president which will be demolished the first time Democrats are in control of both the House and the Senate again. This is a total waste in honor of a would-be dictator's ego. Surely we could find a better way to spend out time and our money.

name: Ann Wells
text: It's unnecessary, too expensive, unsightly, does not fit in with the rest of the city and should be something erected only in memoriam. Please do not let this project move forward. There are so many ways This money can be spent to better effect for individuals, for the nation, for society in general.

name: Dawn Leijon
text: I am AGAINST spending money for a new monumental arch. I have been a DC resident since buying a house in 1999. Reasons: 1. it will destroy the currently unencumbered view from Arlington House over to the national mall 2. the design feels like a copy of the Arc de Triomphe rather than a totally original American creation; I recall the controversy around the Viet Nam memorial, but it's a stunning, unique tribute that's very moving to walk through - if we want a new monument, we need to have a contest to find original ideas that suit who we are now 3. the location doesn't give it space to breathe or be appreciated from a distance; rather, it will just be a distraction as people zoom around the Parkway and over the Memorial Bridge 4. given the state of American families - high prices, not enough housing, lots of car debt, majority paycheck-to-paycheck - it feels like it's a waste of money AND it doesn't feel like there's much to celebrate with a monument at this point in time

name: Ruth McDaniels
text: This arch is not needed, it is being built with out authorization to suit 1 person. The arch will make the landscape of DC ugly. It will tower over everything except the Washington Monument, we are a democracy not a monarchy or anything else. We have rules and 1 man can't control/demand this be done. This commission needs to stand up and support the citizens of the US and not be manhandled by this bully. Vote NO on this and followup to make sure it's not done

name: Laura Bell
text: What exactly is this monument supposed to represent, other than a monument to the vanity of the current president? It has no educational, cultural or historical value. It's an insult to the veterans of this country and should not happen.

name: Sarah Zeigler
text: The proposed arch will not only highlight the home of one of the most notorious traitors to American history by framing Lee's home, it is a vanity project to celebrate none other than the traitor currently in the Oval Office. At a time when most Americans are struggling to pay bills the cost alone should be shameful and prohibitive as our tax dollars should be used for helping those hurt by this administration's policies It would be an eyesore paid with stolen money whose only purpose is to feed the ego of one man Do not let this proceed

name: Judy Walsh
text: Hello, as a citizen with many family members who are veterans that actually served our country, I vote no on this proposed vulgar, ostentatious arch. It is ugly and heralds back to Communist displays of power. It blocks the perfectly planned views that honor our veterans. Please choose to preserve and dignify the memory and valor of our veterans and not indulge an egotistical narcissist that only wants what he wants as usual and overlooks and ignores and tramples on what the rest of us hold dear. Thank you.

name: Gayle Groshko
text: I stand in opposition to the Arch. Its location would diminish the solemnity and grace of both Arlington National Cemetery and The Lincoln Memorial. Please do not desecrate these two historic landmarks. Respectfully, Gayle Groshko

name: Joan Axilbund
text: I support the objections of the National Capital Planning Commission, especially the concerns about the height of the structure and its location. I also object to the fact that the proceudre for reviewing the proposed arch is not being follwed.

name: Karen Truslow
text: My comments are specifically addressing the potential impact of this massive and overbearing project on the line-of-sight between Arlington Cemetery's Eternal Flame, which marks the gravesite of President John F. Kennedy and was intended to remain perpetually visible across the Potomac in the City of Washington, DC. The Eternal Flame has been a constant and permanent feature of the Washington-to-Arlington landscape for the past 63 years. Cross the Memorial Bridge tonight, at twilight, and you will still see a tiny flicker from the gravesite of an assassinated president. It now appears to be threatened by a project of great mass and considerable impact on the surrounding landscape, lacking sufficient consideration for the sacred space that Arlington National Cemetery embodies. I know of no substantive analysis in the project record that addresses the aspect of the Eternal Flame and its intent when originally conceived. Apparently this little point-of-light has been missed, overlooked, or simply ignored by the current president. I vehemently oppose the construction of this self-aggrandizing monument that would forever mar the landscape of our nation's capital.

name: Maria Powers
text: I am concerned about the cost and necessity of this arch. I can not conscience the use of tax payer money for discretionary spending on a decorative arch for many millions of tax payer dollars when spending cuts have been made to program like SNAP, and Medicaid. Literally, the current administration and Republicans in Congress have voted to take food and health care away from the neediest Americans. And now, there is a proposal to build a multi-million dollar arch. It's indecent that it will sit near Arlington Cemetery and immoral given the difficult budget situation. Shame on the commission for this unAmerican project. Shame on you for stealing from the American people. You can take this Arch project all the way to the midterm and presidential elections and winning votes for the Democrats.

name: Valter Ezerins
text: This arch would be a waste of tax money . Furthermore it would disrupt the purposely created view that currently exists. This project ignores American values. Do not approve this gross project.

name: Beverly Walsh
text: To Whom it May Concern, I strongly disagree with the building of a Memorial Arch on the Memorial Circle near Arlington National Cemetery. For a long list of historical, factual, and common sense reasons See "The National Trust for Historic Preservations comments to the CFA". This is just stupid and yet another waste of US Taxpayer money at a time when we have NONE to spare. This is the wrong Memorial in the wrong location. We already have a time tested Memorial, Arlington National Cemetery. Add to that all the rest of the historical memorial buildings throughout DC which have been strategically located forr specific reasons. The current administration is doing way too much to our (the American people's) capital city and it has to stop. Maybe one change or addition ever. 109 yrs or so but this is just to much. Stop the madness now, before it is too late. We the people did not ask for this, and do not want this, or any of the other vanity projects this administration has proposed. Sincerely Beverly Walsh

name: Lisa McKinney
text: I object to the monumental arch proposed by President Trump. The scale of the structure is too big for the site. The disruption of the view shed and the diminishing of the Lincoln Memorial that would result from the construction of the Arch would be a blight on the WDC landscape. I hope the commission will deny this proposal or, at the least, require a significantly reduced size.

name: Lynn McIntyre
text: This is the most disgraceful structure to be built as a yet another vanity project for an insane president. The fact that it will overshadow the hallowed ground of Arlington cemetery is unspeakable. To allow this to happen is a slap in the face to all of the families that have their loved ones buried there. If this so-called committee allows this to happen, you will be forever viewed as being on the wrong side of history. Lynn McIntyre

name: Edi Kramer
text: I am gravely concerned with the location, height, scale, and design of the proposed Triumphal Arch. The manner in which it interferes with and attempts to destroy existing commemorative works and fails to protect existing public uses and cultural resources is, in my opinion, totally unacceptable. I feel the unprecedented height and scale of the proposed and uncalled for Triumphal Arch will overwhelm the Lincoln Memorial, Arlington National Cemetery, and Arlington House, our national treasures and historical pride. In addition, the proposed location of the Arch, at the entrance to Arlington National Cemetery, would be inconsistent with its hallowed character of solemn graves of our beloved heroes. It seems none of that is of any importance to a man who as a Candidate ran on the phrase, "Make American Great Again" and here he is proposing to destroy and dismantle all we have stood for in pride in our country. Make it great again? He is tearing it down in order to put his name in its place. I can still remember his words describing our soldiers as, "Losers". Why would America want to erase all our fought for history for one man's vanity. Finally, Section 106 of the National Historic Preservation Act mandates that a review process be completed "prior to" approval of the project. I believe we must follow our already in place but this Act and wait for such approval to initiate any construction on this arch.

name: Angie Park
text: Please do not approve an arch that would disrupt the history of the Arlington Cemetery and surrounding areas. There is not a need to add an arch that is as awful as what has happened in and around the White House.

name: Renee Wilfong
text: Good morning, I am opposed to the building of this arch. Families are struggling to afford food and Healthcare and we want to put funds towards this project seems ridiculous. This is not a priority for the American people. This benefits no one.

name: Marcy Redmond
text: Please.......no arch. Washington DC is the nation's capital, not a monument to one man who feels the need to put his name on everything.

name: Diane Valeri
text: My mother, who served as a Lieutenant/nurse in WWII is buried is Arlington Cemetery. The proposed oversized arch will interfere with the honor , quiet and peaceful resting place for her and for the others patriots who gladly served their country. Please stop it!

name: Allan Small
text: A neo-fascist, ego-maniacal travesty that will obscure the dignified historical view of the Potomac, Arlington National Cemetery, and Arlington House, as well as dwarf the Lincoln Memorial and the Washington Monument. This must absolutely be stopped.

name: Judy Colton
text: I am opposed to the building of this for aesthetic reasons and because I take my pride in our national historical monuments, not some garish tribute to a corrupt and incompetent leader like Trump.

name: Andrea Reich
text: This proposed arch is nothing but a vanity project for Trump. It will block the view from the Lincoln Memorial to Arlington Cemetary. Also the scale is way out of whack with the rest of the historic buildings in Washington, DC. In addition, the arch is inappropriate next to Arlington Cemetary, which is a solemn place. Please do not allow this monstrosity to be built.

name: Barbara Boyer
text: The people do need an arch built to "honor" Trump. The focus needs to turn back to helping we, the people. It's our money, not his piggy bank. NO

name: Pamela Riffe
text: I am strongly opposed to the Monumental Arch proposed by President Trump. 1) it is an obscene waste of taxpayer dollars at a time when so many programs that ordinary Americans rely upon are being cut. There are so many other more responsible ways to spend that money. 2) As a long time former resident of the Washington area, I am very familiar with that traffic circle. It is a navigation nightmare on a good day, and adding the spectacle of the arch will be an unwelcome distraction that will draw the eye of drivers while simultaneously adding more pedestrian traffic to the fray. Bad idea. 3) It's placement is affront to Abraham Lincoln's legacy. It interrupts the sightlines between the former Lee Mansion/Arlington Cemetery and the Lincoln Memorial and actually frames the home of the defeated Confederate general, which those who still hold a torch for the South's Lost Cause will celebrate. It's wrong. 4) The scale of it is excessive and its design completely out of character with the city. 5) I also concur with all of the objections to the arch set forth by the National Trust for Historic Preservation. Please do NOT approve this project--especially at this particular location.

name: Karen Mauger
text: We supposedly can't afford to give health care to those who need it. We supposedly can't feed hungry children. We supposedly can't get homeless folks the help they need. People are not getting the health care they need so they can put groceries on the table. Those groceries are more and more expensive. Gas prices are up and up. BUT the wasteful government has money for a stupid ARCH that will add to the destruction that this administration is doing in Washington DC. Please get a grip and vote NO to this absolute waste of money project. If this money is to be spent, put it somewhere where it will help the PEOPLE of this country that could really use it/need it. Who cares about an arch. Who cares about a ballroom for only the elite. Who cares about the blue in the bottom of a reflecting pool. Who cares about a wrestling match at the White house......Normal people DO NOT CARE or want these things. Get a grip and listen to the normal folks....vote NO

name: Deborah Piper
text: The American people do not watch this Arch, nor want to spend taxpayer money on it. Read the room, vote NO! Trump is not the King, it's time to start to stand up to him!

name: Jeanne Megella
text: I oppose the construction of the arch. Not only will it dwarf the Lincoln monument, but will also make the view from the Washington mall to the cemetery very different from what it was planned to be since the Cival war. I don't feel that that needs to change for all those men and women who gave all. Some things so sacred need not to change. We need to keep traditions that have long been this country's call.

name: Marianne Vanevic
text: This is a terrible proposal. It will ruin the current sight lines and degrade the dignity of Arlington National Cemetary.

name: Virginia Parra
text: This arch is out of proportion either way surrounding monuments and also blocks the view of Arlington House and Arlington National Cemetery. It is not necessary and a waste of taxpayer money.

name: Vickie Underwood
text: Not in favor. The monument is an ego trip for a despot and locating it in the National Cemetery is a travesty. Vickie

name: Margaret McCarty
text: I strongly object to the construction of this arch. First of all, it will obscure and diminish the impact of the Lincoln Memorial, a focal point on the Mall. Secondly, a monument with the Trump name is highly inappropriate given his felony convictions. There have never been monuments dedicated to sitting presidents, and Trump simply doesn't deserve another monument to his vanity. Please do not allow this project to move forward.

name: Deborah Guydish
text: Enough of our public buildings and monuments in Washington DC have been destroyed or altered for the worst. These federal sites belong to the people, not the administration in power. There is no need for an arch except vanity. This is no time for another ill conceived monument when so many are suffering economically and from brutal discrimination. Please refuse this project completely.

name: Anonymous Citizen
text: Hello. I do NOT want the arch built. It's a waste of taxpayer money and shouldn't even be included on America's list of priorities.

name: Victoria de Monterey Richoux
text: No arch to obscure the view from the Lincoln memorial to Arlington National Cemetery. No one president unilaterally marking territory all over the historic Capitol without approval from Congress and NTHP.

name: Valarie Gilmour
text: The monumental arch is not needed or wanted by the majority of Americans. It is a waste of taxpayer's money, and it will be an eye sore.

name: Robert Allan
text: Please accept this submitted in opposition of the proposed gateway arch between Arlington National Cemetary and the Washington Monument. This is an ill conceived project that was not even on anyone's radar screen five years ago. Existing buildings and memorials have been the result of years of thoughtful planning and input from affected stakeholders vs a project that the current administration is aggressively pushing forward. It will break existing sight lines which are unimpeded from the district towards Arlington placed in an area that can only seen from vehicle. It's scale is out of character for Washington towering over familiar tourist area where people can come learn about our history and learn about the people who have contributed to our great nation. Finally its proximity to the Potomac flightway creates a new and unnecessary obstacle for migrating birds and aircraft heading to and from Reagan National. There are better ways to celebrate this nations 250th anniversary. Remember graduating high school in 1976 when we celebrated with events, focused on our history in ways that helped build community, not the type of edifice we would expect to see in China, Russia or North Korea, nations led by powerful dictators! The arch speaks against democracy, it is, as proposed unAmerican! Please send this project to the scrap heap!

name: Mary Frances Gordon
text: As a child there were often times when my father was gone for extended periods. I didn't quite understand what was going on till many years later. My father was active duty for 30 years. My mother was a Army nurse during world war 2. I understand now what they both went through and what they gave up for this country. They never spoke about what they saw but I Found out later they had horrific stories. Both of my parents are buried in Arrlington. Just the idea of a self serving arch for this president has made me sick. I mean physically sick. Every time I hear about it my stomach turns to liquid. The whole thought of this arch and it's scale Is obscene. Please for the sake of this Nation and all of the heroes that are buried in Arlington, Please do not allow this to be built in our great capital. This administration is hurting our Capital, Please please stop this project. Most sincerely, Mary Frances Gordon

name: Kathryn MacAlister
text: Please, no. Do not approve. Historically inappropriate.

name: JoAnn White
text: Please, NO more of Trump's ego-driven projects. Besides, it looks like the arch Hitler wanted to build.

name: Rebecca Jess
text: Absolutely not! This excrescence has no place in the nation's capital. We do not need yet another monument to Trump's bloated ego. If he wants an arch (besides the golden ones at McDonald's) let him use his own money and build it at Maralago.

name: Gregg Zollinger
text: The location of the Arch is a terrible idea. If disrespects the current monuments and the miltary who gave their lives for this country. Frankly it is disgusting that it is being considered.

name: candace challenor
text: Please do nto approve the Triumphal Arch at Memorial Circle on the George Washington Memorial Parkway. After reviewing the revised concept plans that have been submitted to CFA, I remain concerned about the location, height, scale, and design of the proposed Triumphal Arch, the manner in which it interferes with existing commemorative works and fails to protect existing public uses and cultural resources. It is the wrong thing in the wrong place.

name: Janiine Babcock
text: I respectfully but strongly oppose the proposed arch. It does not fit with the other monuments and the gravity of the location. This is NOT what our country and citizens need or want and does not contribute to a sense of awe or grandeur to the site. Instead it demeans and detracts from the solemn beauty of the area. I'm a 29 year military veteran, I will be buried in Arlington next to my husband, also a 29 year veteran. These area mean a great deal to my family b

name: Ivor Chapman
text: This is not a monument suited for the proposed location. It imposes on the existing topography and its line-of-sight symbolic memorials, and it destroys some of the core human and Constitutional values that America stands for.

name: Janet Shorter
text: For decades, Washington DC has been a model of thoughtful, tasteful design and architecture that has been admired by millions of citizens and visitors alike. No one person, even the president, should ever have the right to unilaterally make changes to this iconic landscape with no regard for thoughtful discussion, permitting and historical preservation. His only narcissistic goal is to erect monuments to himself, which has never been allowed before. Please, we are begging you, stop the destruction of our beautiful capital.

name: Beth Elzer
text: Re: CFA 21/MAY/26-1 Memorial Circle, George Washington Memorial Parkway, Washington, DC. New Monumental Arch. Revised Concept. I am writing to voice my opposition to the planned Monumental Arch. This is not what our tax money should be going toward in times like these — it is outrageous that this administration is spending money on grandiose projects of this nature. The project needs to be approved by Congress. This has also not happened, which is further eroding the coequal branches of government we are supposed to have. Furthermore, the aesthetic disruption to the space in terms of scale, location, and design will disrupt this important visual and symbolic vista. This is an affront to the solemn intent of the space. Regards Beth Elzer

name: Nancy Herrington
text: This arch is inappropriate because of its size, destroying the esthetics of the area. It interrupts the view and relationship between the Lincoln Memorial and Arlington Cemetery. It should not be built.

name: Diane Hyra
text: Thank you for this opportunity to share my thoughts on the proposed New Monumental Arch. I feel this project is unnecessary and ill-advised. Its proposed location would ruin one of the most beautiful vistas in our nation's capital. I had the honor of crossing the bridge from Arlington National Cemetery to the Lincoln Memorial as a Returned Peace Corps Volunteer during the celebrations for the 50th anniversary of the Peace Corps. How different that memory would look if Lincoln's DC home had been obscured. Please deny this project from going forwrd.

name: Jonathan W Bayless
text: There is no benefit to this proposed Monumental Arch, it will only interfere with existing monuments. It would be a distraction from the real purpose of our nation and the historical symbols already existing in the Washington DC area.

name: Dustin Burger
text: We do not need another vanity project for a facist dictator.

name: Laura Hale
text: Based on the design, location, and lack of any need for this project, I wholeheartedly oppose this project moving forward. This is a vanity project that has absolutely no place anywhere in Washington DC, let alone the proposed site. Furthermore, not one penny of taxpayer dollars should be used toward the construction of this eyesore. Many of the citizens of this country are suffering financially right now and this project wreaks of "let them eat cake". NO, NO, NO to this construction.

name: M Wagner
text: After reviewing the revised concept plans that have been submitted to CFA, there are strong concerns about the location, height, scale, and design of the proposed Triumphal Arch, the manner in which it interferes with existing commemorative works and fails to protect existing public uses and cultural resources. Notwithstanding comments and recommendations by Commission members at the April 2026 meeting, the modifications to the proposal have been minimal. Most notably, the 68-foot-high sculpture at the top of the proposed Arch has not been removed or reduced, contrary to the Commissioners' recommendation. The location of the proposed Arch, at Memorial Circle, will interrupt the highly significant relationship between the Lincoln Memorial, across Arlington Memorial Bridge, to Arlington National Cemetery and Arlington House. One of the most symbolic landscape vistas in Washington, DC, the vista was designed to represent the post-Civil War reconciliation of the north and south of the United States. The Triumphal Arch is inconsistent with the McMillan Plan and subsequent planning decisions that have stewarded the National Mall as a unified composition characterized by long, open, and uninterrupted viewsheds, with a clear hierarchy of monumental elements, that culminates at its western end at the Lincoln Memorial. Finally, it is important to note that review of the proposal under Section 106 of the National Historic Preservation Act has not yet been initiated. We understand that the National Park Service will be initiating Section 106 consultation soon, but the statute mandates that the review process be completed "prior to" approval of the project. 54 U.S.C. § 306108.

name: Kathie Reilly.
text: Absolutely not! Do not spend my tax dollars on such triviality. The sole purpose of this arch is for one person's (Trump) self glorification. We must not compete with historical European arches. Wartime is over. Please spend the money on historical landmarks that are threatened.

name: Deb Sheppard
text: Calling on The National Capitol Planning Commission to reject the proposal for this huge monstrosity. As the grandmother of six young people I believe that this project sends the wrong message to future generations. Rather than a deliberative process, seeking input from affected stakeholders, neighbors, and experts, it appears to be an attempt by one man to leave his mark on our nations capitol. Virtually every other museum, memorial, park and Federal building standing today is the direct result of the democratic process, which while messy resulted in the best of the best. Americans does not need nor want something of this scale breaking up the elegant view shed between the district and the hallowed ground of Arlington National Cemetary. Similar to the destruction of the East Wing of the White House this is the latest indication that American is moving towards having authoritarian leader calling the shots. When last we read the Constitution it was clear that we have three equal branches of government. Has Congress allocated funding or are we allowing the executive to make whatever changes he feels suit his mood? Please reject this horrible project!

name: Darcy Gaines
text: I am an American citizen and do NOT want this arch to be built. I have several close relatives buried at our National Cemetery and do not want their memory to be overshadowed by this construction. I am, as many others, a Mayflower child! The money used in this construction should be used for the many citizens who suffer medical conditions. Thank you Darcy Gaines

name: Linda Eyerman
text: Opposition Comments - Proposed Trump Arch A project of this scope and expense should not be a partisan issue. National historic preservation has always been a core value of our country, and changes (additions or deletions) should not proceed unless there is broad-based, near-unanimous support. That is not the case here. My opposition is based on the following. 1. Expense. The costs of the project is enormous. Paying for it will require either raising taxes or reducing needed programs, neither of which most American taxpayers want. 2. Vanity Project. This project would be the first to honor a sitting president while he is in office, and in this case one who is politically-divisive. Monuments should be reserved for those for whom there is a broad consensus of support. 3. Scale. The proposal is for a monument that is out of scale with the surrounding environment, way too big and bold in comparison to other monuments like the Lincoln Memorial. 4. Location. The location of the proposed arch, leading to Arlington National Cemetery, is at odds with the purpose of the Cemetery which is to honor those who served in our military. This is not an arch honoring fallen soldiers; it is intended to honor President Trump who did not serve. 5. Orientation. The orientation of the proposed arch showcases a building owned and lived in by Robert E Lee, a general who led an unsuccessful insurrection against the United States in order to save a system based on slavery. This is an insult to the vast majority of Americans who oppose slavery and support equality for all. Thank you for considering my comments, and I ask that you decide this issue with courage and based on core American values, not under pressure from the Trump Administration.

name: Joanie Shumate
text: Please please please do not build this arch. It blocks the views that deserve to be seen not obscured. This is just one of the insane number of vanity projects of a demented old narcissist that needs to be ignored. Please do not let this monstrosity be built. Listen to Americans.

name: Mary Pallon
text: This proposed arch is unacceptable due to the sight view of Arlington National Cemetery and its large size is not compatible with the other monuments in the area. The tone it sets also does not match with the other monuments and the cemetery. Finally, this should have been put before congress.

name: Amy Lewis
text: Spending money on this is an absolute waste of tax payer dollars. It also needs to go through a design process like every other monument.

name: Claire Kegerise
text: I urge you to reject the plan for this "Monumental Arch" that will restrict the view from the Lincoln Memorial to Arlington National Cemetery, damaging the inter-relatedness of these two sites. This monstrosity is nothing but a vanity project, wasting millions of taxpayer dollars that could be used with much better effect elsewhere.

name: Robin Stanton
text: I oppose building this new arch which is wildly out of scale with the dignified landscape if Washington D.C. The location of the proposed Arch will interrupt the highly significant relationship between the Lincoln Memorial, across Arlington Memorial Bridge, to Arlington National Cemetery and Arlington House which is one of the most symbolic in Washington D.C. I also object to any new monument glorifying a sitting president. Monuments to people should be reserved for honoring someone's memory after they have died, when the full scope of their impact can be evaluated.

name: Pam Olson
text: Please do not let this lunatic build an arch anywhere, especially not in front of our national cemetery Arlington!!!!!

name: Nancy Paris
text: I do not want my taxes to go toward a monument. This is not needed and I think it destroys the view. Please stop this project. Thank you

name: Nancy Van Deusen
text: No arch blocking the scenic vista from the Lincoln Monument to Arlington National cemetery. This would destroy a very historic view designed to represent reconciliation after the Civil War. Don't let our country lose this. Also the money could be better spent on helping the American people with health care, child care and relief from high gas prices. This would be a giant waste of money.

name: Mary Jane Lynch
text: This proposed arch is a monstrous blot on the landscape. I strongly oppose this waste of taxpayer money. I hope this committee starts listening to public sentiment and not just obey this corrupt regime.

name: Chris Gates
text: I do not believe this monument should be built. The size and location is inappropriate. Mr. Trump has done nothing to deserve any monument. This is just another vanity project by someone who has no appreciation for our country's history. The sacrifice of our veterans must not be minimized by the vanity of a draft dodger.

name: Kelly Gibbs
text: Not just NO, but HELL NO!!!!!!

name: Douglas Oreck
text: I don't want to pay for this defacement of the Arlington Cemetery, nor do I want to pay for its future removal.

name: Cheryl Leatherwood

name: Georgia Niemeyer
text: Please do not allow the building of a new arch. This is not an appropriate place for such an arch. We do not need a monument to Trump.

text: My first concern is that the arch will overshadow the focus on Arlington. As Arlington Cemetary is so integral to our history and ongoing respect for our military, this is inappropriate. As funding is cut from housing, food, childcare, and health programs, it is inappropriate to build an unneeded monument.

text: The Memorial Circle where the Memorial Bridge ends and the entrance to Arlington Cemetery begins is an integral part of an already existing memorial. Changing it in any way is disrespectful to the American people. The memorials belong to the American people, not a sitting president and therefore may not be changed in any way.

name: Elaine Freund
text: I oppose the monumental arch. It desecrates an existing memorial the reflecting pool. I also oppose on the grounds that this is a vanity project for our president and since so much has been taken from us by him, he does not deserve the privilege of constructing anything that will live on in such sacred grounds.

name: Jan Hartje
text: Hello. Please do not allow the vanity Monumental Arch to be approved. Do not allow it to be constructed. It will ruin the view, and it is absolutely tacky looking. Thank you!

name: Karen Smudde
text: From Arlington National Cemetery, which was built after the Civil War to unify the nation, there is a sweeping view of Washington, the Lincoln Memorial, and the Washington Monument. This arch would disrupt that view. It's disrespectful to veterans. It has not been approved by Congress.

name: Karen Grant
