It also impacts the significance of the Lincoln Memorial as well as everything that is impacted by sight. This is just completely unnecessary but something that the American tax payers should not have to support no matter what. At a time when people are homeless, hungry and doing without necessities, any unnecessary spending should not happen, especially something that is only an ego trip for someone that has no consciousness (or really cates) about real impact.

name: Maria Hein
text: The monumental arch has no place in Washington, DC. There is no need for it. We have many appropriate monuments representing the history of this country. The placement, in particular, of this arch is particularly troubling. It deflects from the truly important and reverent view to the National Cemetery at Arlington. I am VERY opposed to what is really an epic demonstration of Donald Trump's ego. Again, it has no place in our nation's capital. Thank you. Maria Hein 3612 NE 17th Ave Portland, OR 97212

name: Jancy Muensterman
text: I protest the construction of this atrocity. This is a total disregard for the sanctity on approach to Arlington National Cemetery. The proposed arch to 'honor' this disgusting draft dodging buffoon is a waste of money that could be used to better American lives. I highly PROTEST! This disgusting individual is not worthy of walking on the hallowed ground of Arlington let alone defacing the White House and it's complimentary buildings.

name: barbara smead
text: The unneeded cost is a minor reason why building this arch should not be built. The view of the combined existing monuments will be minimized but most importantly the historical significance of current landscape tells "our story" of America's growth. This Arch has no Historical value to add to that landscape. The vulgarity of this unnecessary building is an afront to Americans.

name: Catherine Gilbert
text: I am writing in opposition of the proposed Arch on the National Mall. I share the written concerns of the National Trust about the size and placement of the Arch. The National Mall is a treasure for all those visiting our nation's capital. Thoughtful consideration has gone into each Memorial that has been placed on the mall. Allowing for an honoring of past presidents, memorials to fallen victims of wars while preserving the views of Arlington National Cemetery. As proposed, the Arch would overshadow each of these and take away to sightline to Arlington. I am grateful that the National Trust has sought to preserve the dignity of the National Mall. If an Arch is desired, a thoughtful process of careful consideration of its size and placement needs to be completed. Thank you.

name: Betsy Aller
text: I respectfully submit that the proposed Monumental Arch is both unneeded and poorly planned in terms of location, scale, design, and intent. The National Trust for Historic Preservation has clearly and thoroughly stated their findings and support for opposition to this proposed structure. Please listen to these experts, whose goals are to preserve the dignity of our capital, in recognition of our honored past and for future generations. Thank you.

name: Cathy Burton
text: This arch will alter the historical meaning of the connection between Lincoln and Lee (Arlington Cemetery). I oppose this on many levels for many reasons.

name: Catherine Byerts
text: I am very much against the current President disturbing any more of the current appearance of Washington. His recent proposals will not enhance this glorious city but will cheapen what citizens have grown to love. The White House interior has been ruined with gaudy gold paint and plastic ornaments. Please do not ruin the Nation's Capitol.

name: david groh
text: I think this is a good idea and should be approved.

name: Andrea Tenne
text: This proposed project will not only draw focus away from the Lincoln memorial as it will dwarf it in size, it will also take away from the solemn and dignified approach to Arlington National Cemetery. I was just there recently, on that circle on foot, watching respectfully as the buses carrying honor flight veterans based by. I can not image what that would look like and feel like if the arch gets built. I would find it completely disrespectful.

name: Betty Kanne
text: I believe the New Monumental Arch should be stopped. The idea should be abandoned. The location of the proposed Arch, at Memorial Circle, will interrupt the highly significant relationship between the Lincoln Memorial, across Arlington Memorial Bridge, to Arlington National Cemetery and Arlington House. One of the most symbolic landscape vistas in Washington, DC, the vista was designed to represent the post-Civil War reconciliation of the north and south of the United States. Arlington Memorial Bridge was intentionally designed with a low profile to respect the visual and symbolic vistas connecting the National Mall and National Cemetery. If constructed as planned at the proposed location, the new Triumphal Arch will obscure the intentional axial and aesthetic relationships between the Lincoln Memorial, Arlington Memorial Bridge, and Arlington House. The National Trust is rightfully also deeply concerned about the unprecedented height and scale of the proposed Triumphal Arch, which will overwhelm the Lincoln Memorial, Arlington National Cemetery, and Arlington House. The proposed Arch would be double the size of the Lincoln Memorial and would risk disrespecting this powerful and beloved monument. As such, the Triumphal Arch is inconsistent with the McMillan Plan and subsequent planning decisions that have stewarded the National Mall as a unified composition characterized by long, open, and uninterrupted viewsheds, with a clear hierarchy of monumental elements, that culminates at its western end at the Lincoln Memorial. In addition, the proposed location of the Arch, at the entrance to Arlington National Cemetery, is inconsistent with the solemn historic character of Arlington National Cemetery

name: Elizabeth Schaefer
text: The proposed 'Triumphal Arch' will prove out of touch with the aesthetics of L'enfant's vision and the McMillan plan. It's too big, ostentatious, and vainglorious. The new monuments of my lifetime have been moving in terms of words, & deeds: Vietnam War Memorial, MLK Memorial, Korean War Memorial, FDR Memorial, among others. The style is bombastic & wreaks of militarism, celebrating victory, over the sacrifice of those committed to the goal of freedom and democracy. I have become accustomed to the wheels of government moving slowly, allowing thought, reflection, & community input. This rush to build marks it as unprecedented, and ill-advised.

name: Gretchen Hein
text: I do not believe that the triumphal arch adds anything to the national monuments. In my opinion, it does the opposite. I have been to Arlington National Cemetery and have toured it. The arch detracts from the respect and honor we as a country owe our soldiers. I love touring the monuments. It has been a hilight of my trips to DC. I do not want the honor I feel for them to be married by a gaudy arch that does nothing to honor the sacrifices and acts the folks portrayed by the existing monuments. The funds dedicated to this project would be better used to restore and maintain our existing monuments and parks. Sincerely, Dr. Gretchen Hein Calumet, MI

name: Cherilyn McLaughlin
text: The scale of the proposed arch is not appropriate for that area. It's a vanity project and nothing more.

name: Eric Walker
text: I am writing to express my vehement opposition to the proposed 250-foot triumphal arch at Memorial Circle. As a citizen invested in the preservation of our national heritage, I urge the reviewing body to reject this design due to its inappropriate scale and devastating impact on our historic visual landscape. The National Mall and its surrounding ceremonial spaces were intentionally designed to emphasize balance, democracy, and national unity. A structure of this scale—standing at roughly 20 to 25 stories tall—would completely disrupt the symbolic hierarchy of the nation's capital. It would dwarf the Lincoln Memorial and sever the historic, intentional sightline between the Lincoln Memorial and Arlington House. This vista was designed to symbolize the healing and reconciliation of our nation; obstructing it with a massive neoclassical arch destroys that powerful historical lesson. Furthermore, the proposed inclusion of gilded statues, lions, and gold eagles introduces an aesthetic of triumphal spectacle that is entirely out of character with the dignified, understated neoclassicism of Washington's core monuments. Our public spaces belong to the American people and should reflect our shared democratic values, not the grandiose aesthetics of a singular administration. I request that the commission reject this proposal in its entirety. Sincerely, Eric Walker

name: Donna Krivoski
text: I respectfully submit these comments to the National Capital Planning Commission in reference to the proposed Trump Arch at Memorial Circle in Washington, DC. I request that you consider all ramifications of this unnecessary and costly project and reject it. The size of the proposed arch would shamefully dwarf the Lincoln Memorial and it would interfere with the designed view and connection between the Lincoln Memorial and Arlington National Cemetery, both of which would be extremely disrespectful. This braggadocious, grandiose monument would disrespect the solemnity of the National Cemetery and all who are buried there. Please note that this project has not gone through the proper channels for review and approval or disapproval by Congress. It's time our laws and the duty of Congress stop being ignored. It's time to remember and respect the dignity and purpose that accompanies our symbolic national monuments. Please do justice to our national spaces and reject this proposal. Thank you. Donna Krivoski Easton, PA

name: Elizabeth Rackley
text: The proposed "Arch" in Washington, D.C. feels less like a tribute to democracy and more like a monument to ego. The power of the capital has always come from its restraint — the clean lines of the National Mall, the openness of the memorials, the sense that no one individual towers above the republic itself. An enormous arch risks turning that balance into spectacle. Washington is not Las Vegas or Dubai. Its monuments carry moral and historical weight because they are rooted in sacrifice, humility, and civic ideals. Dropping a massive triumphal structure into that landscape evokes imperial capitals and authoritarian pageantry more than American democracy. At a time when trust in government is fragile, spending enormous sums on a vanity landmark would strike many Americans as tone-deaf and self-congratulatory. The city does not need a louder symbol. It needs leaders worthy of the symbols it already has.

name: Walter Gilbert
text: This is a colossal waste of tax payers money. I am opposed to this arch!

name: Linda Bickford
text: I absolutely hate the idea of this stupid arch— everyone hates it. It's just going to ruin Washington. But what's the point of commenting or even caring? Until Congress becomes the third branch of government like they're supposed to be, Trump just does whatever he wants. It's obscene and corrupt and yet here we are. Two plus more years of this vile administration— will we survive? Not sure.

name: Celeste Young
text: The proposed Monumental Arch will overshadow Arlington Cemetery, bridge, and the area and vista views that have traditionally been so important to the architecture and design of Washington, DC. I hope the committee will review the size and location. Celeste Young 513 Schaum Court Glen Allen, VA 23060

name: Jeanne Dooley
text: Please do not approve this arch. It is a horrible testimonial to an awful president. Its design is not at all in line with the rest of the beautiful and powerful monuments in DC. Do not destroy the beauty of our nation's capital with this egotistical ridiculous tribute to felon Donald Trump.

name: Cheryl Johnson
text: The Mall in Washington DC and Arlington National Cemetery are important sites in this country. The monuments and structures were chosen and defined by a sense of humility and honor. When citizens visit, and when visitors come from other countries, a sense of respect for those who have gone before us and respect for our nation's history (both good and bad) is evident. The Arch, with its gaudy appearance, does not fit in with the other structures and gravestones. Its intent is to honor one man, except that man is building it. So there is no honor. There is no reverential respect, or awe. There is no understanding of a bigger narrative than his own self-importance. That is why the Arch doesn't belong.

name: Farooq Ahmed
text: Why are we wasting money on a bloated wanna be dictator's bloated project when there are potholes throughout the city that haven't been fixed?

name: MICHELLE BRUMBAUGH
text: This arch is completely dishonorable and does not take into consideration the planned eyesight between the Lincoln Memorial and the national cemetery with the graves of men who died during the civil war during Lincoln's tenure as President as well as the many who have served since that time. We need no more expenditures for vanity projects when the people of this country are seeing cuts to programs and services they depend on for education and healthcare. The dismantling of the East Wing without required approval, the claim that all expenses for rebuilding would be covered by private donation and the subsequent attempt to finance the rebuilding expenditures through public funds already proves that this cost would be born by private citizens, most of whom do not support this garish, inappropriate memorial.

name: Jason Barbour
text: I do not support building this arch. It will take away from the existing memorials and views of Arlington National Cemetery. It is also an unnecessary expense. I do not approve of my tax dollars being used to build this arch.

name: Ann Carlson
text: Washington D.C. is a very important place to me. I have visited on numerous occasions and love the history and symbolism of so many of the structures. They are meaningful precisely because they are simple and their design and location provide honor that does not detract from their meaning. I am very concerned about the "monumental arch" and very opposed to its construction. It is not consistent with the manner in which our capital has been built over the years. It is large, overly ornate and seriously interferes with sight lines of a true place of honor. We are not Rome, nor should we want to be, nor are we a country with thousands and thousands of years of history that included periods of large and ornate structures. Building this because we can, in no way means that we should. There are many ways people of the United States will celebrate and honor our 250 years as a country. None of us need this arch to do so. I sincerely hope this project is reconsidered.

name: Patricia Markle
text: I am adamantly opposed to the building of Trump's New Monumental Arch. As a citizen of the United States of America, as a resident of Northern Virginia for nearly 30 years and as the great-granddaughter, grand-daughter, great-niece, niece, daughter, wife, mother, friend and neighbor of countless military service members, I deeply, passionately and profoundly object to the erection of any architectural feature that disrupts the lovely and tranquil panoramic view that currently exists between the Lincoln Memorial and Arlington National Cemetery. Our Nation, our citizenry, and most importantly, our military dead and their loved ones, deserve better.

name: Betsey Ellerbroek
text: I strongly object to a monumental arch, or any other structure, being built on Memorial Circle. This is another effort by Trump to glorify himself. This project must be stopped at all costs! It is demeaning to all of our Veterans past and present and will be an abomination in our Capital city.

name: stephanie powell
text: The proposed arch is tasteless, overwhelms the area, and is one more example of how Washington is being destroyed. Please do not allow its construction - not even at a lower height - because once allowed, even at a lower height, they will go ahead and construct it the way they want anyway. Thank you for the opportunity to comment.

name: Jeff Brown
text: I strongly oppose the construction of the proposed Arch..its placement will impede the view of current memorials, and it will symbolize a degradation of our beautiful Capital area…it's classless and tacky..

name: Mary Geraghty
text: NO, No! No! Not only is the expense of it ridiculous but it serves no purpose. And it will detract from the thoughtfully planned landmarks already there.NO!

name: Francia Lindon
text: The proposed arch would be an ugly blot on the skyline. The proposed design looks like a cheap copy of one that belongs in Paris honoring fallen fighters of the revolution. Such a mass here would obliterate the entrance to Arlington cemetery, a place where we honor our fallen fighters. Please don't waste taxpayer money on something that's definitely not needed and an eyesore.

name: Suzanne DeFrancis
text: I write in opposition to Trump's proposed arch: As the mother of a U.S. Marine, who has friends buried at Arlington Cemetery, I would hate to see this massive and intrusive structure encroach upon the beauty and solemnity of this sacred ground. Our first thought driving across Memorial Bridge should be of the fallen. As a long-time Washingtonian, I have always been proud of this city with its beautiful vistas. As you drive into DC from the airport, you look across the river at the Lincoln memorial, the Washington monument, the Capitol. It's a quiet beauty. It doesn't shout. It's understated as befitting our democracy. We don't need an imposing arch, with royal flourishes, to taint our view. What is the purpose of this arch? The Trump administration says it is to commemorate the 250th anniversary of our country, hence it has to be 250 feet tall, taller than many monuments including the Lincoln Memorial, the Jefferson Memorial and the White House. They also say it's to honor our veterans, but Washington already has memorials to all the major wars we have fought. Trump has little support for his project. Polls show a majority of the public opposed and, at a federal design review hearing, it was reported that "100% of the comments were against the project." What was the process of approving it? The National World War II Memorial, spearheaded by the late Senator and wounded combat veteran Bob Dole, underwent a rigorous approval process. It took 11 years and required multiple acts of Congress, public hearings, a national design competition, and the involvement of several federal agencies before its 2004 dedication. One of the major criticisms was that it might interrupt the view between the Lincoln Memorial and the Washington Monument, just as Trump's arch would obstruct the view between the Lincoln memorial and Arlington National Cemetery. But Dole addressed this by making it lower. If it took all that to build the World War II Memorial honoring a generation of war heroes, we should at least follow a similar process for a proposed arch that is simply commemorative and appears to be a pet project of one man.

name: Frances Gerry
text: The Triumphal Arch will interfere with the existing commemorative works and does not protect public use. The Arch will intentionally disrupt visual and symbolic vistas. More is not better

name: Kerry Dalton
text: I am submitting my objection to the proposed Monumental Arch. Apart from the following objections raised by the National Trust, this project is an ill-conceived one that smacks of taxpayer waste and complete disregard for the dignity of the highest office of the land in order to prop up the ego of the current president. I agree with the National Trust that: "the location of the proposed Arch, at Memorial Circle, will interrupt the highly significant relationship between the Lincoln Memorial, across Arlington Memorial Bridge, to Arlington National Cemetery and Arlington House. One of the most symbolic landscape vistas in Washington, DC, the vista was designed to represent the post-Civil War reconciliation of the north and south of the United States. Arlington Memorial Bridge was intentionally designed with a low profile to respect the visual and symbolic vistas connecting the National Mall and National Cemetery. If constructed as planned at the proposed location, the new Triumphal Arch will obscure the intentional axial and aesthetic relationships between the Lincoln Memorial, Arlington Memorial Bridge, and Arlington House."

name: Sue Moynihan
text: My comments express my many concerns about this project. The location of the proposed Arch will interrupt the relationship between the Lincoln Memorial, across Arlington Memorial Bridge, to Arlington National Cemetery and Arlington House. This is one of the most symbolic landscape vistas in Washington, DC. The Arlington Memorial Bridge was intentionally designed with a low profile to respect the visual and symbolic vistas connecting the National Mall and National Cemetery. If constructed as planned at the proposed location, the new Triumphal Arch will obscure the intentional axial and aesthetic relationships between the Lincoln Memorial, Arlington Memorial Bridge, and Arlington House. Additionally, the unprecedented height and scale of the proposed Triumphal Arch will overwhelm the Lincoln Memorial, Arlington National Cemetery, and Arlington House. The proposed Arch would be double the size of the Lincoln Memorial, disrespecting this powerful and beloved monument. The Triumphal Arch is inconsistent with all planning decisions that have stewarded the National Mall as a unified composition characterized by long, open, and uninterrupted viewsheds, with a clear hierarchy of monumental elements, that culminates at its western end at the Lincoln Memorial. The location of the Arch, at the entrance to Arlington National Cemetery, is inconsistent with the solemn historic character of Arlington National Cemetery. The hallowed resting place of 400,000 veterans and their families, Arlington National Cemetery is a powerful reminder of American military sacrifice, selfless service, and national unity. Distinguished by the Tomb of the Unknowns, Memorial Avenue, and rolling hillsides of uniform rows of simple headstones, Arlington National Cemetery is a living memorial that honors thirty funeral services each day. The Arch, as proposed, would dominate Arlington National Cemetery, and be inconsistent with its hallowed character of solemn graves with powerful, unadorned white markers. I urge you to abandon these plans. This Arch is unnecessary and meaningless, but will have such a detrimental impact on vistas, monuments, and other aspects of this landscape that have been carefully and thoughtfully planned and provide so much meaning to Americans.

name: Kate McEnroe
text: I strongly object to the proposal for the Monumental Arch on the historical and aesthetic grounds raised by the National Trust for Historic Preservation. I further object to the concept of glorification of "victories" as the highest expression of the ideas of this country. In addition, as a taxpayer, I strongly object to this expenditure of public dollars. Even in cases where private donations have been promised, taxpayers are impacted.

name: Leona Papili
text: The proposed arch is a tacky monstrosity apparently designed by Mussolini's architect. It would have no meaning to the citizenry other than the shame and regret of despoiling deeply meaningful monuments.

name: Christeen Mix
text: The revised concept plans that have been submitted bring up concerns about the location, height, scale, and design of the proposed Triumphal Arch, the manner in which it interferes with existing commemorative works and fails to protect existing public uses and cultural resources. It seems highly inappropriate and disrespectful to our nation, our history, our values, our ideals, of the American people and our heritage. Thank You, Christeen Mix

name: Marsha Roberts
text: The so called Arch will destroy the view and meaning that was intended. The arch will be the biggest eyesore in DC. At this point, I NO longer visit DC. It has no significant meaning while this government allows the destruction of American History to continue. And let's not forgot the monetary cost of this ugly piece of architect just to appease a demented so call president that has no sense of right ir wrong.

name: Karen Rhodes

SACRILEGE !

name: Marie Havens
text: I strongly oppose this arch. Here are the reasons It detracts from the Lincoln Memorial. It is grossly out of scale and character with the surroundings. Imperial rather than democratic. And ugly to boot. It obscures the view of Arlington National Cemetery from the Mall. It frames the view of the former home of Robert E. Lee, a traitor to the U.S. It is a waste of taxpayer's money.

name: Emily Graeser
text: Please say NO to this totally unnecessary project which would impinge upon so much of historical and cultural importance just to satisfy one man's ego.

name: Nancy McCarthy
text: Simple comment…. Please … please… please stop the desecration of our beautiful capital! There is absolutely no need for an arch to impede or desecrate our sacred memorials.

name: Marcia Witt
text: Washington DC is a sacred place for the entire country. It is not a place for Donald Trump's personal pet projects to memorialize himself. It is appalling to think that this is even under consideration. There is no reason to desecrate the beauty, the symbolism, and the skyline. This is an outright demolition of the meaning behind the view from Arlington national Cemetery to the Lincoln Memorial. This needs to be shut down immediately. Hasn't there been enough destruction?

name: William Fiege
text: Hello, This Triumphal Arch does not fit with the other monuments in Washington, DC. It blocks the line of sight between Arlington Cemetery and the Lincoln Memorial, which has a highly significant meaning in connection with the ending of the Civil War, and unifying the country. In addition, it is too tall and overshadows the Lincoln Memorial, and competes with the Washington Monument. Buildings and monuments in Washington have to fit certain requirements, and this Arch does not. In addition, the Arch has not been approved by the National Park Service, nor has the project been approved by Congress. This Triumphal Arch does not belong in Washington DC or Virginia. Please do not approve it to be built. Thank you, Bill Fiege

name: Lou Duzac
text: This proposed monument is nothing more than an affront to the dignity of the Capital, and a token to the bottomless depravity of Donald Trump's ego. If built, it will be destroyed ceremoniously within the next administration by request of voters.

name: Nora Fischbach
text: The idea of an arch that will interfere with the beautiful monuments is not just a bad idea, it's a monumental waste of taxpayer dollars at a time when most Americans are suffering from inflation and loss of health care, food for the needy, and other vital services that have been cut. Frankly, it is an insult similar to "let them eat cake".

name: Jennifer Scanland
text: Absolutely not. Economic crisis for most Americans should be priority not continued construction and development projects.

name: Linette Lowe
text: I oppose the construction of this monumental arch. It would disrupt an intentional and meaningful viewscape and is an unnecessary and grotesque monument to the current President's ego. It has no place in our proudest national landscape.

name: Patricia Simmons
text: I am opposed to a proposed Monumental Arch at Memorial Circle on the George Washington Memorial Parkway, near Arlington National Cemetery and along the Potomac River. It is an unnecessary waste of money from the coffers that are already strained by war.

name: Phyllis Collord
text: I strongly oppose this arch for many reasons. The 2 most important are the fact that it will distract and take away from the grandeur of the Lincoln Memorial, a tribute to a president who had a great impact on our history and the future of our nation. Secondly, and more importantly, Arlington Cemetery is a place of respect and appreciation for the men/women who served our country (many who gave their own lives for our freedoms). The focus should be on those graves, on the Tomb of the Unknown soldier. A gaudy arch will take away from the solemnity and honor those buried there desire. An arch is unnecessary, a distraction and serves no purpose.

name: Beverly Pack

For Pete's Sake, someone needs to put common sense and loyalty back into our historical projects and existing monuments, buildings, national parks, etc!!!

name: Richard Hyman
text: I am categorically opposed to building the proposed arch, even if private money were used. It would be one more obstacle that obscures the current vista, and it is an unnecessary distraction. It would add nothing of value to the area.

name: Victoria Pellot

Also the dimensions of the arch will eclipse, the beautiful serene space that is the Arlington Cemetery. We do not need anything of that size entering into Arlington. name: Janet Thompson
text: I do not support the project of building an Arch in Washington DC. During this economically challenging time, this money should be used to support people instead of glorifying a racist agenda. name: Nancy Cuffman
text: I am appalled to see these eyesore structures that the current administration has decided to waste taxpayer money on. name: Lydia Lutt
text: This proposed project is a disgrace.

name: Karen Cole
text: I am the daughter of a Major of Marines and I laid my Dad to rest in Arlington three years ago. I have a long history with Washington DC and Arlington and am greatly saddened by the destruction of many historical and beloved landmarks at the hands of the current occupant of the White House. Our country is in dire need of many things - universal healthcare, support for our aging population, relief from inflation - and an ugly Arch that will disrupt the flow of the capital should not be a priority where our tax dollars are concerned.

name: Denise Kirchner
text: This arch would be a travesty and would disrupt a carefully planned vista. It is in terrible taste.

name: Jessie Clark

name: Ann Dixon
text: The proposed arch is a desecration to the city and the historical significance of the view to Arlington. Why are you wasting taxpayer money on this boondoggle that will be taken down after this administration is over?

text: This is another absolutely disgusting and wasteful vanity project!! Please help stop it, especially as it obstructs the view of Arlington, which is sacred to so many. name: Frances Coose
text: NO Arch. Period. The proposed arch is tOOOOOOOO big and looks obscene on these sacred grounds. A complete waste of taxpayer $$$$. JUST SAY NO!!!!!!!!!!!!!

name: Virginia Bader
text: Have we not learned enough about wasting tax payer dollars on vanity projects for one single American? Please. Stop this abhorrent misuse of the office of the Presidency. We need to stand up and say no before another hammer falls.

name: Scott Sipler
text: This is as ridiculous as it is unprecedented. Do not build this arch.

name: Tom Wahl
text: Please do not approve the New Monumental Arch. It obscures the solemn view of Arlington Cemetery. It is nothing more than a vanity project. It does not belong.

name: Nancy Matheny
text: The proposed new Monumental Arch interferes with this historic and sacred space, does not reflect American values, and will cost a boatload of money that can be put to better use.

name: sara holtz
text: Do not build the arch. It's a monstrosity and waste of taxpayer money. It ruins the view. No one wants this arch

name: Amy Dagnall
text: It breaks my heart that a large arch, with no significance to our country will change the view of so many meaningful memorials and sights. My nephew is buried at Arlington National Cemetery and someday my Retired Naval Officer and myself will be there, too. The bridge will be overshadowed as will the house on the hill of the Cemetery. It makes no sense that one person can make these decisions without expert insight and observations of the effects on the rest of iconic city views as well as the historic preservation approval. Please do not let this be built.

name: Holly Perry
text: I am opposed to the addition of a vanity project arch which destroys the sight lines of the mall and the view towards Arlington Cemetery. Such major changes to the traditional landscape and its concomitant impact on surrounding buildings and open space need to be approved by a nonpartisan committee or by Congress or by both. It should not be left to a single individual to alter public spaces for legacy or aggrandizement purposes.

name: Margaret Bostrom
text: I lived in northern VA and DC for nearly 3 decades. I can't count the number of times I was at the location of the proposed arch. The current view is awe-inspiring, not just visually but also the history and meaning. Please do not build this proposed monstrosity.

name: James Shaw
text: This arch proposal is an obscene miscarriage of presidential authority. It must be stopped!

name: Toni Brooks
text: I find it deeply frustrating that money is being spent on building a gold arch in Washington when so many citizens are struggling with basic needs. At a time when people are dealing with high housing costs, food insecurity, medical bills, homelessness, and underfunded community services, public money should be directed toward helping the people — not creating flashy monuments. Leadership should be measured by how well it takes care of its citizens, not by how much gold it can put on display.

name: Kathlynne M Altmann
text: Please stop the madness. Why does Mr. Trump think he can do whatever he pleases without congressional approval? This is sacred ground. The arch is just another piece of property made by himself to honor himself. This is not right. How do we all just stand by and watch this happen? Please honor our veterans by not allowing this arch to be built.

name: Jennifer Morris
text: Do not allow this structure to be built. Changes to the historical monuments/ settings should not be allowed at the whim of the president. It's important to maintain the vision of those who created it. It's too late for the East Wing and reflecting pool. Please stop him.

name: Laura London
text: I no longer have faith that the Will of the People matters to this administration (ie that stupid tax-payer funded ballroom), but I strongly oppose the Arch and its location. It's simply disrespectful. We don't need an Arch. We certainly don't need to frame Confederate gravesites.

name: Lynette Doele
text: I OPPOSE TRUMP'S grotesque arch. It is an architectural eye sore that impedes the view of Arlington cemetery from the Lincoln memorial. It also would also be a disturbing, continual reminder of how a corrupt con man consumed with a bad case of megalomania sought to give himself a monument to his own ego. NO TAXPAYER MONEY FOR THIS!

text: This is a vanity project with no architectural merit. It will disrupt the visual lines of the area, and dominate in an artistically offensive way, everything around it. It is an enormous proposed waste of money for something that isn't even relevant to our history. Please reject it. If you want to build something, hire real landscape architects and artists who have the vision and courage to dream up something wonderful and build something beautiful and meaningful that works in harmony with everything around it and speaks to a noble cause. This giant arch is simply a monstrosity concocted to assuage an leaders ego and communicate power.

name: Karen Bartos
text: I DO NOT WANT THIS ARCH! It is a waste of my tax dollars. Stop it, please!

name: Margaret (Peggy) Russo
text: Regarding the proposed Monumental Arch at the Arlington Cemetery Traffic Circle: I have lived in Northern Virginia for the last 40 years. My family and I have attended numerous burial services for friends and family at Arlington Cemetery over the years. My dad served in WWII and both of my parents are interred there, so I am distressed at the idea of the addition of a Monumental Arch on the traffic circle leading to Arlington Cemetery. There is no need for something that large to be constructed in that area. The drive into the cemetery is simple, solemn, and respectful, and prepares visitors for the grounds they are about to enter. The sheer size of the proposed arch would cause it to obscure the gate to Arlington Cemetery, and the amount of tourist traffic just to view the arch could add to the already congested traffic circle. There are 20-30 burial services per day on the cemetery grounds, in addition to the already heavy commuter and tourist traffic in that area. The traffic circle at Memorial Bridge, continuously busy, requires focus to navigate the already large number of vehicles passing through there, to and from D.C. The approach from the George Washington Parkway runs along the Potomac River, with a view of the Lincoln Memorial, Memorial Bridge, and in spring, the beautiful cherry blossom trees are visible across the river. This arch, because of its proposed scale, location, and design would become the main attraction, and thus detract from the historic and serene entry into Arlington Cemetery, as well as from Memorial Bridge and the Lincoln Memorial. Why would it need to be erected there? Arlington Cemetery should remain the focus; a Monumental Arch should not be the focus there. Put it somewhere else, please.

name: Gail Roberts
text: This archive as well as other destructions of our nation's monuments, is a travesty. To allow the destruction is a slap in the face to all who served and all those who died and all of us who love this Country.

name: Neil Bergal
text: I am a retired Gulf War Veteran. I have been to Washington DC many times in the last 50 years. I have seen the road from both ends which lead to the Arch project. This is a very disturbing project. I object very strongly. The view from and to Arington National Cemetery was planned as to be an uninterrupted line of sight. An honor to the fallen. So we never forget the cost. This Arch has all the earmarking of a vanity project for the president. Again, I say I object to this project.

name: Carol ONeill
text: Hello, I respectfully submit that I find this arch to be an atrocious addition to the historical and deeply valued monument landscape. It serves no purpose other than to continue the egotistic endeavors of the current president. Washington, D.C. is not supposed to be a golden, guilded, casino-like destination; rather one that preserves history.

name: Emily Brandt

Funds should not be allocated for such a ridiculous "eye sore" when there's REAL problems that could be solved with that kind of money. We need to do better.

Under no circumstances should our tax dollars be spent for this vanity project. Please do not allow this project to move forward.

name: LInda Nelsen

name: Andrew Reynolds
text: To whom it may concern, The proposed 'commemorative arch' does nothing to mark America's founding, nor does it foster any aspect of our nations many accomplishments. It does nothing beyond satisfying Donald Trump's desire to commemorate and glorify himself. Do not allow it's construction. Do not allow the further desecration of DC for the sake of satisfying one man's ego. Sincerely Andrew Reynolds

name: Julia Volandf

name: Phyllis LeRoy
text: As a constituent of the United States, I think that there are many and better ways to save the taxpayers dollars then an arch it's not necessary thank you!

name: Cleo Haler
text: I object to this "New Monumental Arch". It is not necessary to have a Monumental Arch to honor Trump, to be paid for by U.S Citizens. I pay taxes, Trump does not. If he wants an arch, he should put it on one of his golf courses and pay for it himself.

name: Rebecca Kendall
text: I urgently request that you disallow the planned large arch near the Arlington Bridge. name: Laura Georgi
text: No to Trump's Arch. This is a stupid waste of taxpayers' money and would detract from the existing monuments. The arch is totally the wrong aesthetic for a democratic republic. name: Judy Ulrich
text: Please do not let this be built. I've been to Washington D. C. Many times and recognized the importance of a clear and open view toward Arlington Cemetery. Also, the arch will be the biggest in the world. Big does not make something beautiful. Thank you for considering my thoughts.

name: Emily Novakowski
text: We definitely don't need an arch to honor a president who is a convicted felon. It is disgraceful especially leading into an honorable place like Arlington National Cemetary. It dishonors all those that sacrificed their lives for our country. I am appalled that anything like this would even be considered. Emily Novakowski Pittston, PA

name: Maria Lichter
text: This arch would diminish the significance of Arlington Cemetery and detract from the area's beauty. In simpler terms, it's absurd. Thank you.

name: Ann Silberlicht
text: I am commenting on the proposal by the Executive Office of the President and the U.S. Department of the Interior to construct a new Triumphal Arch at Memorial Circle on the George Washington Memorial Parkway. Under the Commemorative Works Act such works should "not interfere with, or encroach on, an existing commemorative work," and "to the maximum extent practicable, it protects open space, existing public use, and cultural and natural resources." 40 U.S.C. § 8905(b)(2). Furthermore this project has not been approved by Congress. I am concerned about the location, height, scale, and design of the proposed Triumphal Arch. It interferes with existing commemorative works and fails to protect existing public uses and cultural resources. The 68-foot-high sculpture at the top of the proposed Arch has not been removed or reduced, contrary to the Commissioners' recommendation. The location of the proposed Arch, at Memorial Circle, will interrupt the highly significant relationship between the Lincoln Memorial, across Arlington Memorial Bridge, to Arlington National Cemetery and Arlington House. If constructed as planned at the proposed location, the new Triumphal Arch will obscure the intentional aesthetic relationships between the Lincoln Memorial, Arlington Memorial Bridge, and Arlington House. I am concerned about the unprecedented height and scale of the proposed Triumphal Arch, which will overwhelm the Lincoln Memorial, Arlington National Cemetery, and Arlington House. The proposed Arch would be double the size of the Lincoln Memorial and would risk disrespecting this powerful and beloved monument. It will disrupt the hierarchy of monumental elements, that culminates at its western end at the Lincoln Memorial. The Arch would be disrespectful to our fallen warriors and their families. The proposed location of the Arch, at the entrance to Arlington National Cemetery, is inconsistent with the solemn historic character of Arlington National Cemetery. The Arch, as proposed, would dominate Arlington National Cemetery, and be inconsistent with its hallowed character of solemn graves with powerful, unadorned white markers. Review of the proposal under Section 106 of the National Historic Preservation Act has not yet been initiated. The statute mandates that the review process be completed "prior to" approval of the project. 54 U.S.C. § 306108. The proposed plans will be improved in response to the collaborative review and comments from the expert professional staff of the involved agencies, including the Commission's own staff. I urge the Commission members to defer any decision in order to be informed by the Section 106 process. Adding a new monument to our Capitol landscape should only be done after thorough consideration by the public, Congress, and experts, not at the whim of the ego of a current president.

name: Nancy Pesti
text: The proposed Monumental Arch — the scale, location, and design — are totally wrong for the site. It's aesthetically unappealing. The Arch will dwarf the Lincoln Memorial and disrupt the long, open, and uninterrupted views, overwhelming the entry to Arlington National Cemetery—the hallowed resting place of 400,000 veterans and their families and a powerful reminder of American military sacrifice, selfless service, and national unity, all within sight of the monumental core of the Nation's Capital.

name: Pamela Pramuka
text: NO ARCH! No! No! No! no! It's a hideous monument to a hideous person. No living president should have a garish, low-class display of grandiosity. Had this gone through proper channels I have no doubt that it would have been shut down. It's presence would deface our capital city and be a reminder of the most corrupt president and regime we've ever had. NO!

name: Mary Worzala
text: I am completely opposed to the construction of the Monumental Arch. The Arch will tower over other monuments in the vicinity and obstruct the view of Arlington National Cemetery. Arlington Cemetery is hallowed ground, the burial place for our bravest citizens who gave their lives in service to our country. Washington DC has enough monuments and does not need to build this Arch. It is both costly and unnecessary.

name: Eileen Nikopoulos
text: I am deeply concerned and against the construction of the new monument. First im against the unprecedented height and scale of the proposed Triumphal Arch, which will overwhelm the Lincoln Memorial, Arlington National Cemetery, and Arlington House. The proposed Arch would be double the size of the Lincoln Memorial and would risk disrespecting this powerful and beloved monument. As such, the Triumphal Arch is inconsistent with the McMillan Plan and subsequent planning decisions that have stewarded the National Mall as a unified composition characterized by long, open, and uninterrupted viewsheds, with a clear hierarchy of monumental elements, that culminates at its western end at the Lincoln Memorial. In addition, the proposed location of the Arch, at the entrance to Arlington National Cemetery, is inconsistent with the solemn historic character of Arlington National Cemetery. The hallowed resting place of 400,000 veterans and their families, Arlington National Cemetery is a powerful reminder of American military sacrifice, selfless service, and national unity, all within sight of the monumental core of the Nation's Capital. Distinguished by the Tomb of the Unknowns, Memorial Avenue, and rolling hillsides of uniform rows of simple headstones, Arlington National Cemetery is a living memorial that honors thirty funeral services each day. The Arch, as proposed, would dominate Arlington National Cemetery, and be inconsistent with its hallowed character of solemn graves with powerful, unadorned white markers.

name: Ann Berger
text: This Arch will obstruct the view of Arlington. That alone is reason to reject it. We ALL know the reality of why this is being done - it's another vanity project to feed the insatiable ego of one man. A man who has lied, cheated and stolen from the American people. Do not allow this to happen this way - fast and loose without going through the normal channels. How much is this going to cost us?? If the government doesn't have money to feed its citizens it doesn't have the $$ to put this ugly, gaudy, ill conceived arch up to glorify a truly vile human being. To those that claim otherwise say "quiet piggy!" to them!!!!

name: Barbara Sampath
text: I am totally against building the Monumental Arch at Memorial Circle on the George Washington Memorial Parkway, near Arlington National Cemetery and along the Potomac River. The area has been already ruined by destruction of the White House east wing, the paving over of the rose garden grass, and starting building of an obscene unneeded ballroom . The Oval Office looks like the inside of a Hobby Lobby. Stop this nonsense. Do not build this ugly arch!

name: Anita Cola

I feel that it is very Insulting and disrespectful to veterans who sacrificed so that we maintain a democracy. It is shameful that this project had even gotten this far. Additionally, the spending by this administration has been and continues to be astronomical. Stop the fiscal irresponsibility now!

name: Barbara Carleton
text: In addition to disrupting the purposeful layout toward Arlington, it is a huge and expensive structure which is being imposed on the public by one person. As a member of the public I am shocked and disturbed major monument and construction to the nation's capitol was not announced or described in the campaign nor was it proposed and considered by Congress to satisfy our core values of 'representative democracy.' It will forever be known as a vanity structure like the dictators of Europe constructed -- not a beloved era of U.S. citizens. Ideas like this out of the blue render concerns about national debit, federal spending as trivial instead of the gross irresponsibility it is. I'll change my mind only if Congress votes for it and majority passes it.

name: Dennis Cialini

It represents unbridled power, greed and ego and belittles the REAL memorials and monuments nearby like the Lincoln Memorial and Arlington National Cemetery. Please do everything in your power to deny the construction of the Monumental Arch. Present and future Americans will thank you for it.

name: Caroline Hack
text: I do not support this arch. The fact that it is even being considered is outrageous. It will dishonor those buried at Arlington. It will be an eyesore, which will need to be removed once this corrupt administration is removed from office. There is no reason for it to be3 built and it will just detract from the beauty of our nation.

name: Perry C Lyons
text: Hello all. I wish to have my thoughts recorded as a Negative vote on this arch. It will ruin most all of the beautiful sights around the mall with its unsightly gaudyness. THANK YOU!

name: Karen Marler
text: I am vehemently opposed to building the national arch, mostly because I feel this monstrosity will take away the peaceful beauty of Arlington National Cemetery. We do not need an arch fighting with all the national treasures in that area. It will NOT add to the ambience of the area, but will detract from its tranquility. The focus of that area should be the cemetery and those who fought for our country; not a big ugly arch.

Visiting Arlington National Cemetery is a sobering event and to see the Lincoln Memorial from General Lee's former property is such a historic moment for anyone visiting and of vice versa. There is absolutely no reason to mess with the significance of that view. The proposed arch is way too big and too self centered. Please do not allow this assault on history. Thank you

name: Cathryn Newhouse
text: I strongly object to this. The size of the structure alone is outlandish. It disrupts the beauty & view of the area. It appears that the majority of the American public do not want this. It is reminiscent of structures that dictators or other world leaders have installed for their vanity. It is just simply hideous. And frankly, I do not want one cent my tax dollars to be spent on this monstrosity. The cost of that arch, like that of the ballroom, could go a long way to helping the American citizens, many of whom are in a world of hurt right now.

name: Mary Osin
text: I just buried my husband at Arlington. It was a beautiful, meaningful experience. The presence of an overpowering arch would demean the deaths of the 700,000. Civil War vetereans who died to keep the country together. I cannot fully express the fury with which every one I meet feel about this. However, a more modest design might be considered more acceptable. Mary Sue Osin

The disruption to the serenity and wonder of the area is irresponsible. The view of Arlington and the Patriots interred there is unacceptable. The current administration has caused enough damage and disruption already. Please do not allow this project to continue. Thank you for your time.

name: Joan Morrissey Grace
text: This Arch should not be built. It will be an insult to the land where our fallen soldiers are laid to rest. The beautiful sightline from the gentle rolling hills to the Lincoln memorial wil be blighted by this enormous unsightly stone embodiment of our narsisistic president. Let us celebrate all that is historically important in our great nation's capital, without the eyesore of thi arch. Thank you

name: Karen Gugich
text: I am against the Arch project.

name: Kathleen Thier
text: Please reject this proposal for the Arch as it undermines the original intent of the existing monuments and landscape of this area. It also appears that it is not following the guidelines and process that is in place for such a project.

name: debra unverdruss
text: The location of the proposed Arch will interrupt the highly significant relationship between the Lincoln Memorial, across Arlington Memorial Bridge, to Arlington National Cemetery and Arlington House. One of the most symbolic landscapes in Washington, D.C., the vista was designed to represent the post-Civil War reconciliation of the north and south of the United States. It is because this viewshed carries so much meaning to the country the proposed Monumental Arch, whose scale, location, and design will disrupt this important visual and symbolic vista. In addition, the Arch will dwarf the Lincoln Memorial and disrupt the long, open, and uninterrupted viewsheds, overwhelming the entry to Arlington National Cemetery—the hallowed resting place of 400,000 veterans and their families and a powerful reminder of American military sacrifice, selfless service, and national unity, all within sight of the monumental core of the Nation's Capital. For all of the reasons above, please do not agree to the building of this arch.

name: Mari Hannah
text: Where is the permission from Congress? This is my tax dollars going to a vanity project to appease Dear Leader. It is a complete disrespect to the soldiers buried in Arlington Cemetery as visitors will be able to see that monstrosity looming over the trees. No. No. No.

name: Melody Rose Morton
text: Please do not allow this arch to be constructed. It is a vanity project that will destroy the existing monuments site lines. It is a waste of taxpayer money and I oppose it.

name: Judith Langham
text: I object to any construction that draws attention away from the beautiful entrance to the National Cemetery. This is a sacred and respected place of reflection not a "wow look at this" tourist attraction. Please stop. Reserve those funds for the maintenance of our existing parks and memorials.

name: Lisa Altenbach
text: The arch is costing the country millions and with no discernable benefit to the people. It will ruin the line of view of Arlington cemetery and diminish the Lincoln memorial. I do not want my tax dollars going to this.

name: Karen Solheim
text: Here are three reasons the proposed arch should definitely not be built: 1. It would block famous views in Washington. A group of veterans and a historian have already sued in court to stop construction, arguing that the arch would block the view between the Lincoln Memorial and Arlington National Cemetery. At 250 feet tall — more than twice the height of the Lincoln Memorial — it would dramatically change the look of one of America's most treasured landscapes. 2. It copies a French monument instead of creating something original. The design looks very similar to the Arc de Triomphe in Paris, which is actually where Trump got the idea after visiting France in 2017. Using a bigger version of a French landmark as America's main symbol for its 250th birthday raises the question of whether the arch truly represents American identity — or is just a competition to out-do Paris. 3. Even architects who support the project think it's too big. The architect who had been working on Trump's proposed White House ballroom spoke out against the arch's height at a government review hearing, suggesting that the statues on top — which add 84 feet to the structure — should be removed. When designers working within the administration itself have doubts about the size, it suggests the project is more focused on making a big impression than on good design. 4. This is a needless expense at a time when crucial services are being cut from the federal budget. Instead of unnecessary spending on vanity projects in Washington DC, taxpayer money should restore support for medical insurance coverage, public radio and television, and education.

name: Sheri Crotty
text: This planned monstrosity obscuring the Arlington is disrespectful and the OPPOSITE of what our country stands for. First of all, nothing should be taller or bigger than any other national monument, and obscuring our the place where we honor those who fought for our freedom is heartbreakingly rude. PLEASE, DO NOT construct such a thing anywhere in our nation's city!!

name: Nan Thaler
text: The location, scale, and, design of the proposed Arch will interrupt the highly significant relationship between the Lincoln Memorial, across Arlington Memorial Bridge, to Arlington National Cemetery and Arlington House. In addition, it appears inappropriate to construct a monument to a living president who has not finished his term. A vanity project such as this sets a bad precedent for use of public monies.

name: Linda Johnson
text: Don't build it at all! This is another monumental ego project from Donald Trump, who appreciates nothing about history or even aesthetics. Stop him now!

name: Joan Magnuson
text: I am opposed to the gaudy and disgusting Monumental Arch. This monumental eyesore will overshadow Arlington National Cemetery and the monuments to good presidents, who actually did positive things for our country. Our current president is using the office to enrich himself and his family, while making life monumentally more difficult for average Americans. The only monument to him should be a urinal on his gravestone.

name: Ann Boulden
text: I am writing to oppose the construction of a monumental arch between the Lincoln Memorial and Arlington Cemetery. The purpose of the arch is unclear. It appears to be the aggrandizement of a living President and that is not acceptable in America. The design of the arch is terrible. It is far too large. It will block the view from Arlington and diminish it. This is America. Triumphal arches are not part of our culture. We are not Paris or Berlin or Rome. name: Susan Loch
text: I would like to register my strong opposition to the large arch proposed to be on the traffic circle in front of Arlington Cemetery. It is unnecessary, out of place and ridiculously expensive in a time when other basic citizen needs are being cut. The arch will destroy the view from and into the Cemetery. It's an eyesore. It will disrupt traffic. its design is gaudy and looks like something that would be built in the 1800's, not in 2026. Thank you for your consideration. Susan Koch

name: Kathy Anderson
text: I am imploring you to scrap the idea of this disrespectful arch! It will impede the view of Arlington National Cemetery & all that it stands for! It is just another thing Trump wants to stamp his name on. This arch is a travesty & a dishonor to those buried at Arlington.

name: Mary Lee
text: I am opposed to this project. I visited Washington DC in 2011 with a group of WWII veterans including my father. It was an Honor Flight to honor their service. We visited the World War II memorial, the Korean War memorial, and many other places on our single-day visit. I was privileged and proud to join those veterans. Our final stop of that day was Arlington. I still feel overwhelmed when I remember all of those headstones, going on for what seemed like forever. Imagining all of those lives of service. This arch is ugly, obtrusive and unnecessary. It is a dishonor to all who have served and their families. It should be rejected immediately.

name: Cathy Weiss
text: We do not need or want the arch! Waste of our tax dollars!

name: Margaret Wierzbicki
text: I share as a citizen all of the concerns and do not understand the need for this overly large arch that will disrupt the beauty of the historic monuments that are already there.

name: Dorothy Wiggins
text: At this time of high inflation, I feel adding a new monument to a living president is a waste of taxpayer dollars. Most monuments are erected posthumously to honor superior meritorious achievements or bravery in service to the American citizenry. Neither is the case yet proven for Donald Trump. Rather than spend money to honor his unproven service, his abuses of our present memorials, including the White House, Reflecting pool, Kennedy Center should be restored. Further destruction of property of the public or National Park service must not be permitted. In fact, fines should be imposed upon Donald Trump personally to restore property he has destroyed or defaced in Washington DC.

name: NANCY Chatteinier
text: Mr. Rodney Mims Cook, Jr., Chair U.S. Commission of Fine Arts 401 F Street, NW, Suite 312 Washington, DC 20001 Re: CFA 21/MAY/26-1 Memorial Circle, George Washington Memorial Parkway, Washington, DC. New Monumental Arch. Revised Concept. The proposed Arch would be double the size of the Lincoln Memorial and would risk disrespecting this powerful and beloved monument. Distinguished by the Tomb of the Unknowns, Memorial Avenue, and rolling hillsides of uniform rows of simple headstones, Arlington National Cemetery is a living memorial that honors thirty funeral services each day. The Arch, as proposed, would dominate Arlington National Cemetery, and be inconsistent with its hallowed character of solemn graves with powerful, unadorned white markers. This disrespectful monument is a disgrace and slap on the face to our veterans and their families. I respectfully request this project be shut down. Thank you for your time and consideration. Nancy Chatteinier, PhD nchatteinier@hotmail.com

name: Amy White
text: This comment is to State my objection to the proposed triumphal Arch which will block views of Arlington national cemetery from Washington DC. The views of Arlington are planned to always remind our leaders of the consequences of their actions regarding our military. Blocking them with this neo-Nazi edifice to glorify one person is obscene. Let Arlington remain ever visible in our nation's capital so we remember the sacrifice of the thousands who lie there. Signed, a former military wife who trailed around the world after her spouse. Amy I White.

name: Mary Ranta
text: I am appalled at the prospect that the Monumental Arch construction would be approved. The location of the proposed Arch will interrupt the highly significant relationship between the Lincoln Memorial, across Arlington Memorial Bridge, to Arlington National Cemetery and Arlington House. One of the most symbolic landscapes in Washington, D.C., the vista was designed to represent the post-Civil War reconciliation of the north and south of the United States. Please don't allow the desecration of this important landscape.

name: Megan Kirin
text: I strongly oppose the Arch project. Public spaces and memorial grounds should serve the broader public interest, not be used to elevate or commemorate a sitting political figure. Establishing what is effectively a personal monument under these circumstances raises serious concerns about the appropriate use of power and public resources. This proposal is especially troubling given its impact on existing and future memorials. Spaces intended to honor fallen service members and other national heroes carry deep meaning for many Americans. Any action that would limit, overshadow, or displace those tributes undermines the purpose of such sites and disrespects those they are meant to honor. Government decisions about public land and monuments should be guided by principles of fairness, historical perspective, and broad consensus—not personal legacy-building. I urge decision-makers to reject this proposal and prioritize projects that genuinely serve the public and preserve the integrity of our shared spaces.

name: Mary Stark
text: I do NOT support the proposed monumental arch. There should be no monuments to living presidents. There should be nothing to impede the view of Arlington National Cemetery and the heroes buried there. Please STOP this project.

name: Kelly Taylor
text: The idea of the arch is not a bad one, but the proposed size is too large. It will look silly. Please cut the size down to be proportional with surrounding structures so it doesn't look ridiculous, or kindly scrap the project.

name: Bill Doerner
text: Having family buried in Arlington National Cemetery I have visited many times. I feel that this proposed arch is a inappropriate, unnecessary and disruptive addition to the grand view from the cemetery across the river to DC. This is simply another inappropriate act by a uncontrolled narcissist who has already done considerable damage to the the historical and cultural sites of Washington DC, including the White House, the Kennedy Center and who knows how many other more minor locations. i would like my opinion known that i am opposed to the construction of the "Monumental Arch".

name: Mary Bullard
text: I am a Canadian born US citizen-retired librarian/teacher who has enjoyed leading students to DC, attending Book Festivals, and workshops at Library of Congress. The monument of Lincoln, the reflecting pool, and Arlington Cemetery: These historic monuments are a visual history not just of our past but how we have solved problems and come together. Vanity projects have NO place in DC… it is space that belongs to ALL of the nation. No Arch, no Ballroom, no painted blue reflecting pool. And beyond the arch…no images of our current leader hanging on buildings.

name: Susan Fuller

name: Russell Bonanno
text: Please see attached document. Attachment

name: Kimberly Geno
text: As a veteran of 30 years with two overseas deployments for Iraqi Freedom I am absolutely appalled that any president should want to disrupt what was a deliberately designed tribute in our nation's capital. These constant projects to fit one man's idea of splendor are not representing the needs or desires of the general public. This is the United States of America - we don't need to copy every monument and parade that other nations have to be great. Our greatness came from our unity and strength. name: Laura Ray

name: Teresa Taylor
text: This arch is a travesty and has no place in our nation's capitol. Trump has done absolutely nothing to make this country better for anyone but his billionaire friends and his family. He has no concept of honor, and should not be able to destroy historical buildings or build monuments that no one approved of.

name: Joel Kershner
text: I strongly object to the monumental arch that has been proposed for the following reasons: The location of the proposed Arch, at Memorial Circle, would interrupt the relationship between the Lincoln Memorial, across Arlington Memorial Bridge, and Arlington National Cemetery. name: Denise Urban
text: Having visited DC numerous times and having spent time at both Arlington National Cemetery and the Lincoln Memorial, placing a giant monument in between those locations is offensive to those interred there and is ignorant of the intentional design of that space and DC overall. The Civil War was a crucial inflection point in our history. The intent behind the site lines is to help us remember the challenging path of our history and the challenges ahead. It also puts first and foremost the sacrifice of our military to protect our freedoms in front of visitors and residents with uninterrupted site lines from the bustling activity in DC proper. When compared with the intent of other significant markers in DC, this feels like a self promotion with little recognition of the significance of the surrounding areas I also question the appropriateness of spending tax dollars on anything of this nature when people can't access food, housing or healthcare.

name: Ruth Stoeckel

Shame on anyone who thinks this is a good idea.

name: Peggy Schaff

name: Jenele Myers
text: Good evening, I cannot possibly express my disgust for this planned "arch" loudly, emphatically or often enough. It's no secret that this president ONLY thinks of himself, but this hideous structure is so out of place, it's almost laughable. The "before" and "after" photos of this location are so shocking, I actually had to catch my breath. I was born long after WWII but from my history lessons, all I see is flashes of Nazi "art" when that arch appears in the "after" photo. The fact that it blocks out the view of the historical burial ground of fallen soldiers is the insulting icing on the gaudy, tacky cake. Please, for the love of God and country, make this ludicrous atrocity go away.

name: Kathleen McKinley
text: I am appalled and disgusted that President Trump is planning to build an arch in honor of himself in front of the entrance to Arlington National Cemetery. It will obscure the current view that one has of that sacred place where so many of our nations veterans are buried. I strongly object to building this monument to a president who has done nothing but cause harm to our country and it's people.

name: Heather McMahon
text: As an architectural historian, I am well versed in the history of previous attempts to monumentalize Washington, DC as the seat of the nation's capital, from Pierre L'Enfant's Baroque master-plan that laid out grand avenues and rond-ponts for the express purpose of holding national memorials to the McMillan Commission's 1902 revision of L'Enfant's Mall as a collection of monumental edifices and objects. DC is a city for memorialization, I do not deny that. I also support erecting something to commemorate the U.S. Semiquincentennial, marking the 250th anniversary of the country. However, as a historic preservationist, I have concerns that this proposed structure would overshadow the 99-foot-tall Lincoln Memorial as well as disrupt the historic views of Arlington House. That visual connection is symbolic and loaded with meaning; it should not be tampered with. To do so would be to make a political statement about race relations in this nation as well as the most devastating internal war we have ever experienced as a nation. Is that the intention of this site design proposal? As for the form, I also question whether a triumphal arch, which originated in imperial Rome and suggests the conquering of nations, is the correct form for a memorial that is supposed to celebrate 250 years of representative democracy. The quickness with which this project is being sped through the review process also undermines the very foundations of our democratic process. I hope you will listen to and hear these comments and truly and sincerely incorporate them into your decision-making process. Thank you, Heather McMahon, Architectural Historian heather-mcmahon.com heathermcmahon.archhistory@gmail.com (202) 596-5532

name: Heather Stacy
text: I am strongly opposed to this blatant monument to one person. He is not a king nor a dictator. We do not erect "monuments" like this. This will be money completely wasted. I cant believe this is even a discussion. Millions of Americans are hurting financially right now and this is a slap in the face. Truly disgusting. I hope this project never moves forward.

name: s Leighton
text: The arch would frame Robert E. Lee's home, and would detract from other nearby historic sites. Hitler also wanted an arch.

name: Rebecca Tackett
text: I object to the construction of a massive arch that will permanently alter the historic planned view shed that already exists. name: Richard Gould-Saltman
text: To whom it may concern: I am writing to urge you to oppose the proposal for a Triumphal Arch at D.C.'s memorial Circle for several reasons. Washington, D.C. is an inspiring place with significant historically important memorials and vistas, centered on the National Mall. This project appears to be a personal vanity project of the president, not something that reflects any significant historical event (see 40 USCA § 8902(1). It bears no logical relationship to the nation's semiquincentennial. The proposed height and location of the proposed arch would upset the carefully curated layout, including the views of the Lincoln Memorial, the Arlington Memorial Bridge, and Arlington House. In my opinion, it would also desecrate the solemnity of the Arlington Cemetery as a hallowed place of repose for those military members and their families. I also point out that Section 106 requires that the proposal cannot be approved prior to completion of the review process mandated by the National Historic Preservation Act of 1966. See 54 U.S.C. §306108 and 36 CFR Part 800. To my knowledge, that review process has not even started, let alone been completed. The Commemorative Works Act, 40 U.S.C. §§ 8901–8909, requires Congressional approval, see 40 U.S.C. § 8903, which has not occurred. The CWA requires that future commemorative works "reflect a consensus of the lasting national significance of the subjects involved. " See 40 U.S.C. § 8901(4)(B). No such consensus has been shown, and indeed, there has been widespread expert and public opposition to the project. The timing of the project does not comply with the waiting periods prescribed by the CWA, specifically 40 USCA § 8903(b) and (c): "10 years after the officially designated end of such war or conflict" for military commemorative works and "after the 25th anniversary of the event, death of the individual, or death of the last surviving member of the group" for works "commemorating an event, individual, or group of individuals." The fact that the Trump-appointed Commission of Fine Arts has approved the proposal should carry little weight, because it has failed to follow the requirements of 40 U.S.C. § 8905(2): "A commemorative work shall be located so that-- (A) it does not interfere with, or encroach on, an existing commemorative work; and (B) to the maximum extent practicable, it protects open space, existing public use, and cultural and natural resources." Please follow the existing laws and the expressed will of the people to deny approval of the proposed triumphal arch.
