text: Respectfully and frankly, I find the proposed arch disrespectful to the fallen and those we pay tribute to. Whether its placement is as proposed, or anywhere in DC, it would be a mockery to the many memorials and solemn resting place of those who courageously defended this country. It is tremendously out of scale, gaudy, and a waste of funding. My first visit to DC was as an adult, and I distinctly recall being impressed with all the greenbelts and parks. It is difficult to envision a monstrous arch adding positive value to our nation's capitol.

name: Jennifer Reingold
text: This is an affront to anyone who has ever a) lived in Washington b) studied architecture or history c) walks upright (actually on all fours as well). It is gauche, wrong for the space, and representative of a shameful era in US history.

name: Patricia O'Connor
text: I oppose.the construction of the monumental arch. It is a monumental expense and a disruption of the architectural symbolism for which Washington DC is famous. This is an unnecessary, ego-driven project. The money could be better spent on education, Healthcare, or anything else that would serve the people. Please stop the arch.

name: Marge Grie
text: The USA and the World does Not need any more monuments to tRump. Because that's what it is. The current view from Lincoln to the cemetery Must Not Be Obscured. It is sacred and must remain so. There has been so much desecration to our country by tRump. We The People deserve the view as it is and as it was designed. Please find your spines and say NO! to this desecration.

name: Carolyn Jones
text: Please stop this proposed TACKY TRASHY arch to dictator Trump. The lovely vista that defines Washington DC toward & back from Arlington would forever be damaged. It demeans our war dead. You can't buy CLASS as Trump demonstrates.

name: Matt Oerding
text: As an American and veteran I absolutely am against the idea of a triumphant arch. America was founded on the ideas of liberty and freedom, not the conquest of a king or empire. This is a waste of taxpayer money and should not move forward.

name: Deborah Burke
text: Absolutely not! Washington DC should represent all Americans in the classic and clean style it always has. One man's tacky, gold-plated taste should not be allowed to change the simple beauty of our capital. This is the behavior of an egotistical dictator. DC should reflect America, not trump. (And his having complete say over who serves on the Arch board proves that Trump alone is in charge)

name: Anna cupito
text: As a longtime resident of the District of Columbia, I'm absolutely appalled at the proposed "monumental arch." It's a ghastly vanity project being foisted onto the taxpayers, and I welcome the opportunity to offer public comment before actual construction begins. After the destruction of the East Wing, we saw how little this administration values basic rules and norms, and it's important that all comments are thoroughly reviewed in this instance. As any visitor to the area can see, there is a visually significant relationship between the Lincoln Memorial, across Arlington Memorial Bridge, to Arlington National Cemetery and Arlington House. One of the most symbolic landscapes in Washington, D.C., the vista was designed to represent the post-Civil War reconciliation of the north and south of the United States. In addition, the Arch will dwarf the Lincoln Memorial and disrupt the long, open, and uninterrupted viewsheds, overwhelming the entry to Arlington National Cemetery—the hallowed resting place of 400,000 veterans and their families and a powerful reminder of American military sacrifice, selfless service, and national unity, all within sight of the monumental core of the Nation's Capital. This Arc de Trump is an insult to this national monument and cannot be approved.

name: Lilian Mullane
text: I am opposed to any monument to a living president. These are meant to be memorials to great presidents, not every president merits one in DC. Please respect the values these memorials stand for and prevent this ego demonstration.

name: Holly Quick
text: I am opposed to the new monumental arch proposal. The arch would be too big, out of proportion with the other structures in the area. Most concerning, it would block the view of Arlington National Cemetery, a site sacred to many. The arch as proposed is out of scale for Memorial Circle, and should not be built.

name: Lisa Coolidge
text: Building this arch would annihilate the historic importance of the view between the Lincoln Memorial and Arlington National Cemetery. It is, also, highly disrespectful of the veterans and others buried there.

name: Pamela Cole
text: NO! NO! NO! NO! NO! Everything about this is insulting, disgusting, and wasteful! We need NO MORE reminders of Trump in this city, and the cost to tax-payers is WASTE, FRAUD, and ABUSE!!! If you build it, we will tear it down to the ground the minute the man is gone, so don't waste our taxes!

name: Barbaara Brunson
text: To: National Capital Planning Commission I strongly oppose CFA 21/MAY/26-1, the Revised Concept for a New Monumental Arch at Memorial Circle on the George Washington Memorial Parkway. I write as a daughter, daughter‐in‐law, and spouse of veterans interred at Arlington National Cemetery; my family's connection to ANC gives me a personal stake in preserving its dignity, context, and historic character that honors those who served. Objections: Legal: The proposal appears to violate the Commemorative Works Act—no documented consultation with the National Capital Memorial Advisory Commission or congressional authorization is shown. Historic harm: The arch would intrude on a nationally significant designed landscape, disrupt key sightlines and axial relationships, and diminish ANC's contemplative setting. Safety: Memorial Circle is a high‐traffic convergence with complex merges, weaves, and multiple pedestrian/bicycle crossings; blocking sightlines will worsen congestion and increase safety risks for drivers, cyclists, pedestrians, and funeral processions. Alternatives and mitigation lacking: The Revised Concept provides no thorough alternatives analysis, cumulative‐effects evaluation, or enforceable mitigation and stewardship commitments. Requested actions: Deny approval in its current form. Require documented compliance with the Commemorative Works Act (NCMA Commission consultation and congressional approval as applicable). Require an independent, comprehensive traffic and safety study addressing sightlines, merge/weave operations, pedestrian/bicycle crossings, and funeral procession impacts. Require a full alternatives analysis prioritizing avoidance (alternate sites, reduced scale, or non‐intrusive interpretive options) and a rigorous historic‐preservation impact assessment in consultation with preservation authorities. If pursued, any commemorative work must preserve unobstructed views to/from ANC and include enforceable mitigation and long‐term stewardship. Sincerely, Barbara Brunson Norfolk, VA Attachment

name: Donna Truman
text: No to the Arch, it's inappropriate, it's too big, it's too ugly, and we have NO MONEY!!!!!!!!!

name: Sharon Seymour
text: I absolutely oppose construction of this obtrusive, monstrous mistake. I'm puzzled that it is even being considered. It is not a contribution, but an insult to the people of this nation and to our history. I do not want my money spent this way.

name: Lora Sharkey
text: To the Members of the National Planning Commission Comments regarding NCPC File Number: 8778 As an American taxpayer I must express my opposition to any actions to install an arch or any other commemorative works that does not follow the prescribed process for approval. At this time the president of the United States has stated he will have a commemorative arch installed on federal property without seeking approval from Congress which is required under the Commemorative Works Act. Additionally, I feel the construction of an arch at the Memorial Circle on the George Washington Memorial Parkway, would be a distraction to the Arlington National Cemetery entrance. The National Cemetery has a purposeful, dignified, solemn landscape that should be protected from structures of unusual height, adornment and lighting. Respectfully, Lora Sharkey 432 Cades Trail Southport, NC 28461

name: Lori Richatdson
text: I think the Arch is not only ridiculous, it would destroy the view of Arlington Cemetery! Nothing should ever destroy the final resting place of our service members that died!

name: Jerry Sessions
text: I do not believe now is the time to build an arch. Especially this proposed monumental arch. With our national debt soaring and Americans under stress economically, an arch does not reduce the debt or help Americans financially. This new monumental arch would seem to reflect the decline of America under the current administration and not be a reflection of the America our founding fathers envisioned. The timing is wrong and the arch is not what we the people want. Please reject the proposed arch.

name: Reese Brooks
text: The arch looks tacky, ugly, and un-American. Even if by some miracle it is built it will be torn down within a year.

name: Jean Gioffre
text: With the division in our country; high prices on food, gasoline and other essentials; the war in Iran with its massive cost; the allegations about this administrations IRS and financial fraud; AND the Epstein files - this is not the time to consider building a monumental arch. Its only purpose is to assuage the President's ego and distract the public's attention from far more important issues. It will negatively and irrevocably impact the honorable and historic landscape that already exists. It's a fool's errand. Thank you.

name: Maury Niebur
text: NO! the Arch serves no purpose other than to massage the ego of the current occupant of 1600 Pennsylvania Ave. it would.violate the "view" prescriptions laid out in the design of the city and forever cast a pall over Arlinton Maternal cemetery. My father and mother are buried there, and they will both be rolling over in their graves if this atrocity gets built. So .... NO!

name: Jacqueline Patterson
text: I am writing to strongly oppose the proposed arch near the Lincoln Memorial. The open visual approach to the memorial is one of the most powerful and symbolic public spaces in the United States. Any large new structure placed within that sightline risks diminishing both the solemnity and emotional impact of the memorial itself. The Lincoln Memorial was intentionally designed as a place of reflection, dignity, and national unity. Its setting — especially the unobstructed views across the National Mall — is part of the memorial's meaning. Introducing a monumental arch into this historic landscape would interrupt the visual balance and alter a carefully preserved civic space that belongs to all Americans. This proposal appears to prioritize spectacle over preservation. The power of the memorial comes not only from the statue of Abraham Lincoln, but from the experience of approaching it through an open and uncluttered landscape. Adding another dominant architectural feature nearby would compete for attention and reduce the sense of reverence visitors feel. The National Mall is one of the country's most historically and symbolically important public spaces. Changes to it should be approached with extreme caution and respect for the original design intent. Once a major visual intrusion is added, the damage to the character of the site cannot easily be undone. In addition, the cost for a totally unnecessary monument will likely be borne by the very citizens who find it abhorrent.

name: Marsha Adkins
text: The height of buildings act of 1910 limits the height of all buildings within Washington, DC to be no greater than 130' + 20' for a penthouse. Clearly, the arch, at 250' is illegal. The proposed placement of this arch is also problematic, in that it blocks the view and symbolic entrance to Arlington National Cemetery. The Arlington Memorial Bridge was meant as a unification of North and South after the Civil War. The arch is a huge divider between the Lincoln Memorial, which it dwarfs, and the solemn graves of 400,000 men and women who gave their lives for our country. A better location for the arch might be at the entrance to the city, along I-95, either in Maryland or Virginia.

name: Vicki Devine
text: Please for the love of God stop this abomination! It's complete disrepect for our fallen soldiers, since it blocks views between the graves and the Lincoln Memorial, all for an egomaniac that thinks he can build anything in D.C. without approvals or consequences. And he is a draft dodger, so there is that.

name: Christie Abraham
text: The arch will be another detractor. We already have too many. Trump has been allowed to run roughshod over the changes to the White House grounds. He destroyed the Rose Garden, ruined the Kennedy Center, the reflecting pool, ad nauseam. Please stop him.

name: Barbara Gugliotti
text: I am adamantly opposed to the proposed Arc de Trump for the following reasons: 1. It is not compatible with the existing monumental or other architecture in our Nation's Capital. 2. The location of this arch is a desecration of Arlington National Cemetery and of utmost disrespect to those buried there and their families. 3. No other living President has constructed a monument in self-praise. National monuments are a way for grateful citizens to pay tribute to the legacies of and remember honored leaders. Trump is still living; his legacy is yet to be determined. 4. It is embarrassing that, like a male dog urinating to mark territory, Trump is putting his name and likeness on everything in our Nation's Capital. The White House and other significant elements of Washington, D.C. belong to the people of the United States of America, not Donald J. Trump.

name: Brody Willis
text: The "Monumental Arch" is an aesthetic and functional excresence whose only purpose is to be bigger than anything of its kind, and is meant only to glorify one person, not our country or the fallen heroes resting in Arlington Cemetery. As a taxpayer and a combat veteran, I vehemently oppose this useless, worthless totem of vanity. I would rather have universal health care, student debt relief, and higher taxes on the rich. The answer is NO.

name: Cathy Blankenstein
text: This will be a desecration of the views and solemn sentiment that frame Arlington national cemetery. Our veterans deserve better. Vote no on this monstrosity. It is unnecessary and just another distraction for Trump and his endless vanity projects.

name: Steven Douglas
text: The Monumental Arch Project would be a monumental mistake. It is grossly out of scale and the proposed adornments are also too large and ostentatious. It looks like something from Berlin during the 1930's. Existing sight lines to Arlington Cemetery and other historic sites would be disrupted. Please do not approve the monument.

name: Diana Vaniotis
text: My visit to DC a few years ago included the many historical monuments that chronicle our history. Looking back at photos I am struck by both the majesty & modesty that defines a government that is of the people. The proposed arch is out of scale, grotesque & gaudy. It is a monument to one man's insatiable thirst for self promotion & adoration. Not to mention the likely corrupted misuse of taxpayer money. It is an abomination and needs to be abandoned completely. NO to monumentally corrupt arch.

name: Dana Pietromonaco
text: This arch is not in keeping with the scale, scope, or intentions of our national monument. It obscures and detracts rather than highlights. It becomes a monument unto itself and the person who installs it. It is not for the people. And the people can not afford to pay for this massive monstrosity! No money for arches for arches for the dead while we have living people dying of hunger and disease.

name: Matt Morgan
text: What, he's Napoleon now? Or Caesar? Give us a fucking break. No fucking arch.

name: Kathleen Hintz
text: I am appalled as well as absolutely opposed to the proposed monumental arch. I have read hundreds of comments about this project, none of them favorable, and most more articulate than I can hope to provide. Please do what you can to put a stop to this monstrous monstrosity. It is nothing more than one more effort by Donald Trump to leave a stain on our country. Make our voices heard and I'll pray that those in charge are listening.

name: Thomas Tews
text: This project is a waste of time and money. The country has other needs. There is no practical justification for this project that should allow it to proceed. Let's focus more on the American people and less on vanity projects.

name: Melanie Richardson
text: Don't need anything from blocking the view of what's important Arlington Cemetery

name: Joanne Fuchs
text: I am against the Monumental Arch for a number of reasons, most of which is the symbolism it projects. Arches are about power and military victory. The US is a democracy and thus should focus on peace, not war. The arch is also too large, too ornate, and destroys the esthetics of the mall. It doesn't belong anywhere near the mall. It is also not the time to spend that kind of money. An arch would not represent the spirit of the US. DO NOT BUILD IT ANYWHERE.

name: Joyce CRAIN
text: This is ridiculous!!! PRESERVE OUR SPACES, OUR HISTORY,OUR SCENIC MEANINGFUL VIEWS. Joyce Crain

name: Carol Conklin
text: I am opposed to the proposed Arch. I am concerned with the location, height, scale, and design of the proposed Arch, the manner in which it interferes with existing commemorative works and fails to protect existing public uses and cultural resources. The location of the proposed Arch, at Memorial Circle, will interrupt the highly significant relationship between the Lincoln Memorial, across Arlington Memorial Bridge, to Arlington National Cemetery and Arlington House. The unprecedented height and scale of the proposed Arch, which will overwhelm the Lincoln Memorial, Arlington National Cemetery, and Arlington House, is unacceptable. The proposed Arch would be double the size of the Lincoln Memorial and would risk disrespecting this powerful and beloved monument. The proposed location of the Arch, at the entrance to Arlington National Cemetery, is inconsistent with the solemn historic character of Arlington National Cemetery, and is an insult to the families and loved ones visiting the Cemetery.

name: Michael Solomon
text: Dear National Capital Planning Commission, My name is Michael Solomon and I'm writing to express my disappointment in the Monumental Arch proposed by President Trump. This project unabashadely serves no purpose other than to inflate the ego of the proposer. In the setting of legitimate memorials to Lincoln, Jefferson, Washington and most importantly the Arlington Cemetery, this proposal is obtusely out of place. None of the aforementioned memorials were proposed by their namesakes. This alone should be reason enough to reject this arch proposal. Further, the scale, style, and compatibility with the thoughtful arrangement of the existing memorials clearly reflects how inappropriate this proposal is. History will judge these days as the lowest in American history, with backwards missteps and callous disregard for responsibilities that comes with authority. Let's not further memorialize this period with a gaudy arch. Thank you for your consideration, Michael Solomon

name: Lorraine A
text: This proposed "monumental arch" would be a stain on the historical landscape of DC and added to the other defacements already taking place for no decent reason. I oppose this arch.

name: Kyle Rogers
text: This project is simply idiotic.

name: Rick Aragon
text: Esteemed Commission Members, I support a monument to celebrate the semiquincentennial of our nation's founding. I do not see an issue with a triumphal arch being that monument. However, I believe that the size of the proposed arch is far too massive for the location. I urge that the arch be scaled down to better fit the other monuments. I also encourage that the arch should not have a figure above it. Thank you for your time.

name: Tracy Cornish
text: I am writing to lodge my objection to the proposed arch. I share the same concerns and the National Trust. In addition, in a country that is currently struggling with basic necessities like groceries, gas, shelter, healthcare and education, this vanity project is deeply disrespectful. We the people oppose this, the ballroom, the lack of transparency and the corruption of this government.

name: Michael M
text: It would be a national disgrace for this government to obstruct and destroy the Lincoln Memorial and Arlington vistas by building this arch at the behest of vain man. What an absolute abomination. If this goes through it debases every person who made it happen or did not stand in its way. It debases our great nation. Know this: Whatever this man erects to flatter himself, we will tear it down.

name: Jeanie Lemens
text: No to Trumps Arch. He is spending millions of our money on vanity projects without getting preapproval in many cases. We have other more important needs in our country. Food, Healthcare, Housing, Medicaid, Medicare and Social Security to name a few. A vanity Arch is not one of them. We are trillions of dollars in debt and are going another 2 Trillion just this year alone. So no. No Arch!!!!

name: Patrick Chapman
text: I am adamantly opposed to the proposed arch. Not only does it not fit into the existing, historical architectural design of the surroundings, it will alter the approach to Arlington National Cemetery, where both of my parents are interred. Please reject this monstrosity.

name: Ginger Vollmar
text: The proposed new monumental arch is a horrible idea. It is in a bad location (interfering with the views that are now there), it is much too high, is too large in scale, and the design of the Arch is over the top with its gaudiness. Also, the manner in which it interferes with existing commemorative works and fails to protect existing public uses and cultural resources is very disturbing. Please stop this project from moving forward. Ginger Vollmar

name: Susan Freiband
text: I don't think that the construction of a Monumental Arch at Memorial Circle is a good idea. The proposed Arch does not fit the aesthetics of the space. It is ostentatious and arrogant, not fitting the character of the place where it is supposed to stand. It will provide an unnecessary distraction, disrupt the flow of traffic and transportation through the area.

name: Ginny Waters
text: I am completely opposed to the construction of this arch. Its projected size is grossly out of proportion to the adjacent natural and manmade features, and its trite, vaguely militaristic design sends precisely the wrong message. The arch is a mere vanity project commemorating nothing. It means nothing. It would be a blot on the landscape and a waste of time and materials. Please DO NOT allow this arch to be built.

name: Mary Lou Cochrane
text: Arlington National Cemetery and the view to Arlington National Cemetery should not be desecrated by the building of this offensive arch. My husband served in Vietnam and my father served in Italy during WW II. They and other veterans who gave their lives for our country should not have their service treated with such disrespect by the construction of this monster arch.

name: Stephen Folkemer
text: Trump's ego assuaging arch proposal is a brutal insult to our veterans. Stop this grotesque proposal now!

name: Cathy Poyser
text: Stop! We should NOT be spending money to build an Arch that isn't necessary and is really only important to one person! We have people in this country who can't afford, food, housing, gas, who are living on the street and we're seriously considering this vanity project?! When is this going to stop?! He's already been allowed to destroy a portion of the White House. THE WHITE HOUSE, for goodness sake. Please do not allow him to destroy the current view of Arlington, which is sacred ground. Just STOP!

name: John Buzzell
text: Trump's erection of a monument to his ego is obscene and pushing into the realm of the perverted. Squandering and looting $billions of OUR tax dollars for this low-rent copy of Moscow's Triumphal Gate, is horrific - even more so in America's current state of disarray. When are we going to say "enough!"?

name: Janet Driver
text: The proposed Monumental Arch will obscure the intentional axial and aesthetic relationships between the Lincoln Memorial, Arlington Memorial Bridge, and Arlington House. This is not acceptable and expressly against the intentions of the post Civil War era memorialization committees that decided against a winner takes all approach to our national commemoration of our history and choosing to ensure designs that show a healing of the country rather than a divide. The proposed Arch is the embodiment of obstruction and distain for the common citizenry. Its sole intention is to flex Presidential power and turn it into real estate development by and for one man only - Donald J. Trump. It is neither his place to commemorate himself in this way nor is it conducive to national unity. If this Arch is built, I would expect it to be a source of national embarrassment and be subject to demolition by the citizenry at the first possible opportunity. It will only bring more division and protest to an already stressed capital city.

name: Sally Nichols
text: I strongly oppose the construction of an arch in DC area. Any monument should be a celebration of an extraordinary event meaningful to the majority of Americans. This arch is purely a vanity project stroking the demented ego of one man. It is monumental only in the waste and abuse of taxpayers money. We need no monument to the worst president in American history. If built, I and others will gladly contribute to destroy it.

name: Colleen Manzer
text: Please, please stop this oversized, monstrosity from becoming a reality. It looks like something made for Las Vegas. It has no real meaning behind it, beyond Trump celebrating himself. DC is a beautiful city, monuments have thoughtfully been installed and are cherished by Americans. This does not enhance the monuments or celebrate anything of value to our nation.

name: Carole Woomer
text: I am against the proposed arch in Washington for the following reasons: The location of the proposed Arch will interrupt the highly significant relationship between the Lincoln Memorial, across Arlington Memorial One of the most symbolic landscapes in Washington, D.C., the vista was designed to represent the post-Civil War reconciliation of the north and south of the United States. The scale, location, and design will disrupt this important visual and symbolic vista. In addition, the Arch will dwarf the Lincoln Memorial and disrupt the long, open, and uninterrupted viewsheds, overwhelming the entry to Arlington National Cemetery—the hallowed resting place of 400,000 veterans and their families and a powerful reminder of American military sacrifice, selfless service, and national unity.

name: Kimberly Baker
text: I ask that you not approve the plan for the new monumental arch in Washington, DC. The arch disrupts the continuity of the Lincoln Memorial and Arlington National Cemetery, which when considered together, communicate a powerful message of the reintegration of the North and the South following the Civil War. The vast size of the arch also overwhelms and blocks the view of important monuments throughout that area of DC. And the style is in stark contrast to the design of monuments and federal building in the area, which were intentionally designed not to be ornate or grandiose in order to express more clearly the vision of the United States as "We, the People," rather than one of conquest and elitism. Please oppose this proposed arch.

name: Susan Fortney
text: This proposed arch does not belong in our nation's capitol. It will disrupt the symbolic landscape of the Lincoln Memorial and Arlington National Cemetery. It is a gross waste of taxpayers' money, especially at a time when ordinary people are struggling to make ends meet.

name: William Keys
text: The location of the proposed Arch, at Memorial Circle, will interrupt the highly significant relationship between the Lincoln Memorial, across Arlington Memorial Bridge, to Arlington National Cemetery and Arlington House. One of the most symbolic landscape vistas in Washington, DC, the vista was designed to represent the post-Civil War reconciliation of the north and south of the United States. Arlington Memorial Bridge was intentionally designed with a low profile to respect the visual and symbolic vistas connecting the National Mall and National Cemetery. If constructed as planned at the proposed location, the new Triumphal Arch will obscure the intentional axial and aesthetic relationships between the Lincoln Memorial, Arlington Memorial Bridge, and Arlington House. In addition, the proposed location of the Arch, at the entrance to Arlington National Cemetery, is inconsistent with the solemn historic character of Arlington National Cemetery. The hallowed resting place of 400,000 veterans and their families, Arlington National Cemetery is a powerful reminder of American military sacrifice, selfless service, and national unity, all within sight of the monumental core of the Nation's Capital. Distinguished by the Tomb of the Unknowns, Memorial Avenue, and rolling hillsides of uniform rows of simple headstones, Arlington National Cemetery is a living memorial that honors thirty funeral services each day. The Arch, as proposed, would dominate Arlington National Cemetery, and be inconsistent with its hallowed character of solemn graves with powerful, unadorned white markers.

name: Linda Barnett
text: I entreat you to oppose the erection of this Arch. It is not at all consistent with the monuments already in place, and it is gaudy. It will be a smudge on the landscape in that treasured area.

name: judy horning
text: To whom it may concern, I am against building a monumental arch. Ours is not a country that needs to prove our greatness with decorations like this. Our greatness is in our constitution and rule of law. It is belittling of all our other memorials to construct an arch to celebrate war and killing. Our other monuments celebrate the honor and sacrifices of fallen soldiers. This arch is not a celebration of our ideals. It is ill thought out and unattractive and an embarrassment. Please do not approve it at all.

name: Cynthia van Duin
text: I am writing to oppose this new Monumental Arch. It is completely opaque as to what this arch I supposed to honor or add to our historic capital. Furthermore it will destroy the impressive and serious atmosphere of Arlington Cemetery and block the view of one of our most important monuments, the Lincoln Memorial. The visual connection of Arlington Cemetery and the Lincoln Memorial emphasizes their historical connection as the Cemetery began as a resting place for veterans killed in the Civil War. Put a stop to this ridiculous project.

name: Virginia Connelly
text: I implore you to reconsider plans for the "Victory Arch" in Washington, especially its placement (actually misplacement) on the Virginia side of Memorial Bridge. I grew up near Washington and have always loved this truly beautiful bridge and the perfection of its setting. It gracefully and meaningfully links the beloved Lincoln Memorial with the hallowed grounds of Arlington cemetery. To disturb this elegant historical setting confounds all common sense and good taste. Please, please consider placing the arch somewhere else, where it can be the center of attention, if it has to be built at all.

name: Natalie Heilman
text: The arch is just another gaudy project to destroy our country. It is tacky and doesn't need to exist. Furthermore, our government is not spending money to take care of its citizens. Healthcare, education, and basic human rights should be the focus. We do not need another vanity project funded by American taxpayers.

name: Greg Dixon
text: I feel like this project is an abomination in and of itself. It is totally unnecessary and garish, not fitting into any of the tasteful architecture around it. The sight line affecting Arlington Cemetery alone makes the project particularly ill advised. To summarize, it is an unnecessary, unappealing waste

name: Freida Garrison
text: Please do not build this arch. It would only disrupt the hallow landscape that flows together and honors our fallen heroes.

name: Stephanie Seacord
text: As an American citizen and taxpayer I am appalled by this Administration's constant disregard for the laws and regulations put in place to safeguard our collective national treasures, including the historic and cultural assets of the District of Columbia. I am equally disgusted by the Commission's decision on this project. By approving the Monumental Arch on May 21, the Commission and its individual members have abandoned the responsibility you were given to ensure that any works in your jurisdiction do not "interfere with, or encroach on, an existing commemorative work and to the maximum extent practicable, protect open space, existing public use, and cultural and natural resources." We may restore our nation, eventually, but what you are enabling will cause damage that can never be repaired. We as a republic, and you as public servants, are better than this.

name: Adam Rothman
text: The Triumphal Arch proposed for Memorial Circle is ill-advised. It would block the sightlines from the Lincoln Memorial to Arlington National Cemetery and along the Potomac, and disrupt the historic integrity and coherence of the commemorative axis running from the Lincoln Memorial across Arlington Memorial Bridge to Arlington National Cemetery. The area is meant to be a space for solemn reflection on the great sacrifices that Americans have endured in the name of freedom and democracy, not gaudy triumphalism.

name: Devon Rehse
text: This project is very concerning and totally unnecessary. It will disrupt the expansive and purposeful view and dwarf the Lincoln Memorial as well as the sanctity of Arlington National Cemetery. These projects that proceed at a whim without forethought or care what the citizens of the United States want for their capital is alarming and must come to a stop immediately. Millions of dollars are being spent unnecessarily, dollars that come from my pocket!

name: Renee Searfoss
text: Under no circumstances should this monstrosity be built. Any person and company who participates in any way in pushing this project forward or working on it should lose their jobs, any and all current and future contracts, public or private. Any government official or employee involved in this corruption should be removed from their position and barred from any government position at any level.

name: Mary Braatz
text: I strongly oppose the construction of the new monumental arch. It will be too big and it will obstruct the Lincoln Memorial and the entrance to Arlington National Cemetery. There is no reason for its construction and it is a waste of taxpayer money.

name: Judy Shulman
text: I object to the proposed location of the Arch. The location of the proposed Arch will interrupt the highly significant relationship between the Lincoln Memorial, across Arlington Memorial Bridge, to Arlington National Cemetery and Arlington House. One of the most symbolic landscapes in Washington, D.C., the vista was designed to represent the post-Civil War reconciliation of the north and south of the United States. It is because this viewshed carries so much meaning to the country that the National Trust has raised concerns about the proposed Monumental Arch, whose scale, location, and design will disrupt this important visual and symbolic vista. The Arch will dwarf the Lincoln Memorial and disrupt the long, open, and uninterrupted viewsheds, overwhelming the entry to Arlington National Cemetery—the hallowed resting place of 400,000 veterans and their families and a powerful reminder of American military sacrifice, selfless service, and national unity, all within sight of the monumental core

name: Brett Aresco
text: This arch is an unnecessary and expensive eyesore, a tribute to the large ego of a man so small as to be insignificant. History will remember this president only for cruelty and incompetence, so please don't force any more reminders of his tenure on the American people.

name: Janet Bourne

I am very familiar with the historic plan for the city, which works beautifully--the vantage points between distinguished monuments, the care not to overcrowd public areas, the decorous attention to detailing. The current president has removed all trained professionals from the arts commission and is trying to turn our capitol into Pyongyang! The so-called Monumental Arch is a travesty. Badly designed, clumsy and ahistorical, and just plain ugly. It will destroy internal relationships between our central monuments and utterly eliminate the human scale of tourist and official areas. It will obstruct already problematic traffic. It is also a phenomenal waste of money, at a moment when virtually no funds are being spent to help anyone who isn't a millionaire. This project is unconscionable. And please take down those horrible giant banners of his face. we're still, nominally, a democracy! Dr. Elizabeth A. Brown, Ph.D.

It's not needed, wanted -- and an incredibly poor use of our tax monies. How about paying down the debt if you've got so much money to blow on unneeded idolatry.

The funds for the arch can help maintain and restore other historic monuments and fountains in our nation's capitol!

name: CHRIS FULMER
text: Respectfully, I request you vote NO on this arch. There are myriad reasons, but I will touch on just a few: No review. Projects such as this take YEARS of review, architectural analysis, traffic studies, public need, costs and budget, and more. This process is being completely bypassed. This is a vanity project: No one asked for this arch, except Trump, who wants it to commemorate himself. No president has ever considered something this egregious before. Disrespect to Arlington: The aspect and perspective of the National Cemetery has been planned and makes the hillside with the view of Arlington House and the rows of headstones central to those looking across the river. It bears the names of hundreds of fallen military men and houses the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier. It stands as a memorial to those who served and died — not as a tribute to a sitting political figure. If there were discussion of building a meaningful memorial honoring the dead and missing from Vietnam, Korea, and other wars fought by Americans, I could understand that — assuming our fiscal reality actually supported such spending. name: John Ayers
text: The proposed triumphal arch at Memorial Circle is a direct assault on one of Washington's most carefully designed civic sequences and the country's most hallowed ground. The Lincoln Memorial, Arlington Memorial Bridge, Memorial Circle, Memorial Avenue, Arlington National Cemetery, and Arlington House form one ceremonial approach held together in one sight line. The McMillan Commission explained that Washington was planned with careful attention to "reciprocal relations" among public buildings and that "vistas and axes" were part of what made the capital "a magnificent and consistent work of art." The point was not simply to build monuments, but to protect the relationships among them and preserve the capital's visual order. The National Park Service recognizes Arlington Memorial Bridge as the "ceremonial entrance to Arlington National Cemetery," and a 2022 NPS viewshed analysis confirmed that the reciprocal view between the Lincoln Memorial and Arlington House remains an intact and protected feature of the cultural landscape. Any arch, triumphal or otherwise, will interrupt the sequence and commandeer the Lincoln-to-Arlington axis, converting the ceremonial entrance to Arlington from a passage of reconciliation, sacrifice, and reverence into a visually intrusive focal object. Frederick Law Olmsted Jr. warned that nothing suffers more from "vulgarity, ignorance, and pretentiousness" than the modern cemetery, and that such places should be entered with "respect and peace, as into a church or sacred place." Reverence does not begin only after one passes through Arlington's gates. The Lincoln Memorial, Memorial Bridge, Memorial Circle, and Memorial Avenue are part of the experience of entering Arlington Cemetery. The Arlington axis is something rarer than a monumental vista. It is a ceremonial approach in which every element — the cemetery founded on Lee's confiscated land in 1864, the house he left to fight against the Union Lincoln preserved, the bridge completed as an act of national reconciliation, and the avenue named for the fallen — belongs to the same chapter of American history. The McMillan Commission did not invent that meaning. It recognized it, gave it form, and protected it. Any arch placed on that axis would interrupt that sequence and commandeer one of the capital's most carefully preserved commemorative landscapes. The McMillan Report is unambiguous. The National Park Service's own treatment of the Lincoln-to-Arlington corridor is equally clear. In light of that history, approval of this proposal is difficult to comprehend. Attachment

name: Elizabeth Morton
text: Dear Commissioners, I am writing to urge the National Capital Planning Commission to reject the proposed New Monumental Arch — or, at minimum, to decline to advance or endorse the concept until the Section 106 review is complete. I am a Washington, DC resident with a Master's (UNC) and PhD (MIT) in City Planning focused on civic design and preservation. I have served on several public art commissions and am a former member of the Arlington Planning Commission. The proposed design and location are significant departures from the founding planning principles and protected viewsheds that make Washington a world-class capital. The arch would disrupt the deliberately low-scale, reflective axis linking the Lincoln Memorial, Arlington Memorial Bridge, and Arlington House. It would also distort the established monumental hierarchy — inserting a wildly out-of-scale, gilded tribute to one man that overshadows our most cherished commemorative works (notably the Lincoln Memorial) and severely degrades the dignified respectful character of Arlington National Cemetery. Beyond its deviations from the McMillan Plan and the Commemorative Works Act, the proposal is plainly out of conformance with the Federal Urban Design Element of the Comprehensive Plan for the National Capital: Federal Elements. That Element, adopted in 2016, makes preservation of Washington's low, horizontal skyline and its symbolic view corridors a national interest, and directs that the "physical preeminence and visual hierarchy" of the city's most significant civic structures — the White House, U.S. Capitol, and Washington Monument — be preserved. The Element further recognizes the Arlington Memorial Bridge as a ceremonial "Capital Gateway." A 250-foot gilded arch astride that gateway and the axis it anchors does the opposite of what these policies require. Apparently the Section 106 consultation has not been completed. Section 106 requires that effects on historic properties be considered "prior to" approval (54 U.S.C. § 306108; 36 CFR § 800.1(c)), and acting before that process concludes risks foreclosing meaningful and transparent consultation. Consistent with longstanding precedent, the Commission should wait for the review to finish before advancing this seriously flawed proposal. Thank you for the opportunity to comment. Elizabeth Morton

Nothing about this monument enhances the sanctity of the area in which it wishes to be built. PLEASE vote it down.

name: Cynthia PUGLIA
text: Arlington should honor sacrifice, not serve as a backdrop for a vanity project. Our fallen heroes deserve dignity and reflection - not a towering monument built to glorify a draft dodging bone spur politician. Arlington is scared ground, not a stage for someone's ego!

name: Douglas Hancher
text: The proposed Trump Arch is wholly inappropriate in concept, scale, and appearance. It will be a blight and eyesore that compromises the vistas and character of D.C. -- Douglas G Hancher, CDR, Usn (ret.), P.E.

name: Ellen Jahos
text: I am vehemently against the construction of a so-called, "Triumphal Arch." What "triumph" warrants building this gaudy, self-serving structure, a structure the citizens of this country did not ask for? If the current president wants an arch so he can boast that the US has the biggest arch in the world, then that in itself is proof that he hasn't studied history, and doesn't understand what America stands for. The fact that it will be an overwhelmingly negative alteration of our capitol's landscape should be foremost in decision makers' minds. Even more disgraceful than the arch itself is the decision to block a clear view to the entrance of one of the most sacred places in our country - Arlington National Cemetery. What kind of blind, selfishness would allow the scarring of our Capitol's landscape? What kind of people would knowingly approve the building of a structure that obscures the resting place of those that gave their lives so that we may all live free? It is time for you to listen to the people of this country. The destruction of the East wing of the White House has already shocked and sickened the citizenry. Don't let another vanity project disgrace our country's Capitol.

name: Lisle Hannah
text: I believe the proposed monumental arch will significantly diminish established views, dwarf the magnificent Lincoln Memorial and cause traffic issues. An arch of this size does not belong in this location and I urge serious consideration.

name: Jacklyn Ulinski
text: THe proposed arch named aftervone man does not belong at the entrance of Arlington Cemetery. Arlington is a sacred place where our service members and honored representatives and Presidents lie in rest. This is not a place to have an arch dedicated to a non-service man This arch becomes a block for the view to the entrance and forever changes how we see Arlington. Visiting there for my uncle and visiting the President's grave site is something we can cherish. Changes to the monuments and design and structure in Washington must be changed and agreed by Historical committees and Congress. Not just one man.

name: Margaret Yacovissi
text: Washington DC is a beautiful city filled with fine architecture laid out in symbolic lines. The connection of the Lincoln Memorial across the Potomac to Arlington National Cemetery echoes the beauty of the reconnection and reconciliation after our Civil War in the 1860s. Considering the current state of civil rights in the USA, it would be especially disrespectful to change that vista to glorify our narcissistic president. A person of character doesn't need to build monuments to himself. He can be confident of recognition after his passing. Since Trump can't be sure he will be remembered after he's gone, he wants to litter the DC landscape with anything that will boost his ego. HIs regime is not a triumph. He should not have the right to spend money on frivolous things at public expense. He must be made to follow all appropriate guidelines for historical and architectural review in his proposal and it should be rejected in favor of preserving some part of the dignity of our national city. Please vote against this poorly sited and undeserved arch.

name: Susan Babbitt
text: The comments submitted by the National Trust for Historic Preservation give such a full and sensible account of the procedural and aesthetic problems with this proposal, that I can add only that they deserve attention and approval.

name: Alexandra Nelson
text: Do not build this monstrosity.

name: Eleanor McGrath
text: I object to the arch for a number of reasons: it is inappropriate, it obscures the view of Arlington National Cemetery, and it's ugly.

name: Dave Long
text: Considering the plethora of much more urgent issues facing citizens and our country, spending time and funds on such a project ignores or diminishes their importance. Please consider putting this very vain project to bed.

name: Marina Salazar
text: I am opposed to this garish arch — it has no relevance or place among our monuments.

name: Rebecca Bolen
text: There's only one person who wants this. It's ugly and doesn't match anything in DC. We don't build monuments for egomaniacal whims. For the love of God, have a spine. Tell him no.

name: Michele Homan-Schultz
text: I strongly object to seeing a monstrosity of an arch interrupt the views of our cherished monuments to men that contributed to the good of our country. I emphatically object to ANY monument to a living, egotistical, grifter. Please do not allow this huge, gaudy, self serving arch to be constructed on our serene national land.

name: Michael Brown
text: The White House now looks like a crummy motel and the the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool is going to be the color of toilet cleaner. Any and all projects under Donald Trump's direction need to be stopped not only due to ridiculous costs but for an appreciation of good aesthetics. Somebody give him a LEGO set to play with so he stops ruining our lovely capital.

name: Linda Seaquist
text: Do not break the line of sight work a new arch. We do not need an irrelevant monument added to our already revered monuments.

name: Christina Vanderwall
text: I strongly object to consideration or approval for construction of this rogue monument. No proper procedures were followed. No hearings. No design review. No legal financing process. So, no no no no. I write this even though submitting this email may result in my being put on some nefarious action list by the current President or his acolytes.

name: Jeanne Connelly
text: I am adamantly opposed to the monumental arch at Memorial Circle. The scale of this proposed arch is completely out of line with nearby monuments and vistas. It would overwhelm the Lincoln Memorial, block the important vistas of Arlington Cemetery and cause traffic tie-ups at the Circle. The circle currently provides a beautiful entrance and view toward Arlington Cemetery and should not be desecrated with the Trump Arch. This proposal should not even be considered until it has gone through the Congressional review process and has been proposed with the passage of legislation. Please don't ignore the will of the people!

name: John Henderson
text: This proposed arch is a ghastly travesty and must be stopped. On my first visit to Washington DC with my family as a 6 year old in 1968, we made a point of visiting the Lincoln Memorial as the sun was setting to gaze at the Washington Monument as its lights came up in the Reflecting Pool. We turned to see the glow of Arlington Mansion and could faintly make out the eternal flame of JFK's tomb in the wooded darkness. Just two months later, RFK would join his brother on that hillside. The sanctity of these hallowed memorials was palpable to me as a small boy and the impression so indelible, that evening is alive to me nearly 60 years later. I was too young to understand the intentional juxtaposition of these memorials - of locating Arlington National Cemetery here - and the opposing tension between the Lincoln Memorial and the Custis-Lee Mansion across the Potomac, what that meant in the sad retelling of the Union, Confederacy, and the Civil War. It is entirely inappropriate and a crude insult to put a triumphal arch in the midst of these sacred grounds like some bloated bauble.

name: Gail Newsome
text: I have read and I support the position of the National Trust for Historic Preservation, as outlined by Carol Quillen, with regard to the addition of the proposed arch. Let Paris be Paris! And let Lincoln be us!

name: Therese Andre
text: The proposed Monumental Arch does not fit into the design of the area. It would be a disgrace to have such a large, overdone thing put up for no good reason whatsoever.

name: Gail Millerdeforest
text: The arch will be an intruder to the wonderful planned out park that is there. It a very peaceful and beautiful, it brings many people solace just to walk it. I just don't understand why we are letting this man destroy the beauty of decades!

name: Carol Geu
text: The arch does not integrate with the other monuments/memorials in the proposed area. It is completely out of proportion with sacred sites. I strongly urge you to reject the arch.

name: Mark Tezel
text: I respectfully oppose the proposed Monumental Arch. The project's scale appears overbearing and would significantly disrupt and obscure historic and symbolic view corridors, particularly those connecting Arlington National Cemetery and the Lincoln Memorial. These vistas are an essential part of the nation's capital landscape and should be preserved. Additionally, the proposed funding for this project could be more effectively directed toward critical National Park maintenance needs or programs that directly benefit the American people. For these reasons, I urge the Commission to reconsider and not advance this proposal.

text: Strong Opposition I strongly oppose this project. The lack of justification for the project as a whole, the gaudy design, and obvious mismatch with other monuments in Washington, DC make this a horrible idea. It should be rejected in total.

text: We do not need or want a monumental arch. This will disrupt the views, and add a tacky vanity project in conflict with the solemnity of Arlington National Cemetery. Historical preservation must be considered. Do not honor someone who himself has no honor.

name: Cheryl Johnson
text: This will destroy the views that are iconic and beautiful and reflective for our visitors. Who is this for ? One man and his ego.

name: Sean Tucker
text: The proposed monumental arch should not be approved. Please decline it. It aesthetically disrupts the intent of DC's design, blocking the transition from the Lincoln Memorial to Arlington cemetery and thus disrupting the symbolic link between the sacrifice of the civil war and the end of slavery. It's also symbolically inaccurate. In Ancient Rome, a triumphal arch was built to memorialize a particular military victory. This one signifies nothing, tied to no specific event. As such, it risks mockery as a grand celebration of no accomplishment. Finally, it has grown politically divisive, which is a perfect illustration of why past planning commissions have never honored the living, always allowing the passage of time to place people and events in context before considering any request for a monument. Please protect the integrity of deliberative process, the symbolic meaning of our city's layout, and the need to accomplish great things before earning long-term acclaim by denying permission for the arch, or delaying the decision for 25 years to allow it to earn its proper context.

name: Donna Peronace
text: I am writing to share my concerns about the size and placement of the proposed Monumental Arch. The current layout of the area from the Lincoln Memorial over the Arlington Memorial Bridge to the Arlington National Cemetery and Arlington House was designed as a symbolic landscape and view. It represents the Post-Civil War reconciliation of the north and south. Memorial Circle is open for a reason. To suddenly insert this oversized Arch into the view is inappropriate and unattractive. Furthermore the size and placement is disrespectful to our honored dead at Arlington National Cemetery. Also, the placement would obscure the relationship between the Lincoln Memorial and Arlington House. And in certain views would frame Arlington House thus symbolically elevating Robert E. Lee's home. Given Lee's betrayal of his oath and resigning his commission to serve the Confederacy, this is completely inappropriate and sends a terrible message. The proposed size of the Arch is inconsistent with the other monuments on the National Mall and displays the current administration's lack of respect for our history. It is my understanding that the Commemorative Works Act requires the project be approved by Congress and should not "interfere with, or encroach on, an existing commemorative work and to the maximum extent practicable, protect open space, existing public use, and cultural and natural resources." Lastly, where is the money coming from for this project? I strongly object to taxpayer dollars being spent on an inappropriate, unnecessary Arch when so many Americans are struggling with high prices and lack of access to healthcare.

name: Liza Burney
text: "My opposition to the proposed 250‐foot triumphal arch between Arlington National Cemetery and the Lincoln Memorial comes from multiple fronts — legal, historical, and aesthetic. 1. Violation of historical sightlines The arch would block the long‐established, unobstructed view between the Lincoln Memorial and Arlington House (Robert E. Lee Memorial), a sightline symbolizing national unity after the Civil War. This view has been preserved for over a century and should not be interrupted. 2. Lack of congressional authorization The lawsuit led by Public Citizen claims the project is "flatly unlawful" because it was not authorized by Congress, which is the body that should approve new monuments in D.C. The plaintiffs argue only Congress can authorize such a structure, and the U.S. Commission of Fine Arts has no authority to approve it without that approval. 3. Symbolic and patriotic concerns Vietnam veterans and an architectural historian say the arch is being built without proper process and appears to be a monument to one man rather than a national commemoration. They frame it as disrespectful to fallen service members buried in Arlington, especially since one plaintiff had hoped to be interred there. 4. Aesthetic and design objections The arch is gaudy and much too big, it disrupts the historic landscape and is an affront to the area's dignity. Residents and visitors say it would "change the vibe of D.C." and look like a copy of the Arc de Triomphe in Paris. 5. Legal and procedural challenges The Justice Department has moved to dismiss the lawsuit, claiming the plaintiffs lack standing, while the plaintiffs counter that the project is illegal without congressional authorization. A federal judge has denied a temporary halt to construction, but the case is ongoing. 6. Potential impacts beyond sightlines The FAA is studying possible flight safety risks from the arch's height near Reagan National Airport, and some opponents warn it could alter the city's skyline and historical character WTOP News. In summary, the main arguments against the arch center on its disruption of a historic view, lack of proper legal authorization, perceived disrespect to veterans, and concerns over its scale and design."

name: Robbin Ossi
text: Arlington Memorial Bridge was intentionally designed with a low profile to respect the visual and symbolic vistas connecting the National Mall and National Cemetery. If constructed as planned at the proposed location, the new Triumphal Arch will obscure the intentional axial and aesthetic relationships between the Lincoln Memorial, Arlington Memorial Bridge, and Arlington House. The unprecedented height and scale of the proposed Triumphal Arch, will overwhelm the Lincoln Memorial, Arlington National Cemetery, and Arlington House. The proposed Arch would be double the size of the Lincoln Memorial and would risk disrespecting this powerful and beloved monument. As such, the Triumphal Arch is inconsistent with the McMillan Plan and subsequent planning decisions that have stewarded the National Mall as a unified composition characterized by long, open, and uninterrupted viewsheds, with a clear hierarchy of monumental elements, that culminates at its western end at the Lincoln Memorial. In addition, the proposed location of the Arch, at the entrance to Arlington National Cemetery, is inconsistent with the solemn historic character of Arlington National Cemetery. The hallowed resting place of 400,000 veterans and their families, Arlington National Cemetery is a powerful reminder of American military sacrifice, selfless service, and national unity, all within sight of the monumental core of the Nation's Capital. Distinguished by the Tomb of the Unknowns, Memorial Avenue, and rolling hillsides of uniform rows of simple headstones, Arlington National Cemetery is a living memorial that honors thirty funeral services each day. The Arch, as proposed, would dominate Arlington National Cemetery, and be inconsistent with its hallowed character of solemn graves with powerful, unadorned white markers.

name: Amy Nestor
text: We do not more government wasteful spending on an arch. Take that money and instead fund: 1. Veterans' housing and mental health care A lot of veterans are fighting battles long after the uniforms come off. Permanent housing programs, PTSD treatment, addiction recovery, job placement — that money could become actual stability instead of decorative stone. 2. Fixing collapsing infrastructure America has roads that feel like lunar craters and bridges older than disco. One flashy monument budget could repair water systems, transit lines, sidewalks, or public schools in struggling areas. 3. Child nutrition programs Feeding kids shouldn't be controversial. Expanded school breakfast/lunch access and summer meal programs produce measurable long-term benefits in health, learning, and crime reduction. 4. Affordable housing initiatives Rents are climbing like they're trying to escape Earth's atmosphere. Funding mixed-income housing, first-time buyer assistance, or homelessness prevention would help real families immediately. 5. Scientific research and disaster preparedness Hurricanes, floods, wildfires, pandemics — the future keeps sending invoices. Investing in research, climate resilience, emergency response systems, and medical innovation pays dividends for decades

name: Kevin King
text: From: Kevin King, AIA 4600 Connecticut Ave NW Washington, DC 443-465-0460 The proposed 250-foot triumphal arch, currently advancing toward a federal approval vote on June 4, would stand at Memorial Circle between the Lincoln Memorial and Arlington National Cemetery. That proximity deserves more scrutiny than it has received. The axis connecting those two landmarks was not designed by accident. Lincoln bore the weight of a war he knew would define the nation's soul, and he framed its meaning not as victory but as obligation to bind up wounds, to reconcile, to endure together. Arlington Cemetery, carved from the estate of Robert E. Lee, extended that meaning into the landscape itself. The view between them is an act of civic philosophy, sustained deliberately for over a century. A triumphal arch is a specific form with a specific meaning. It commemorates conquest. It announces dominance. It is the shape of a power that has prevailed over others. Placing that form on this axis doesn't add meaning to the site. It replaces the meaning already there by substituting triumph for reconciliation, dominance for grief shared across a divide. Washington's monumental landscape has always argued for something. This proposal argues for the wrong thing, in the wrong place. Kevin King, AIA Washington, DC

name: Ellen Malloy
text: I am writing to oppose the proposed Triumphal Arch at Memorial Circle, and I want to be direct about why. This site was chosen deliberately over a century ago to honor the dead of the Civil War — to frame, without obstruction, the view between Arlington National Cemetery and the Lincoln Memorial. That uninterrupted sightline has stood for over 100 years as a quiet act of national reconciliation. A 250-foot arch — taller than anything else in that landscape — does not honor that history. It buries it. The scale alone should give pause. The arch would stand more than twice the height of the Lincoln Memorial. Even the architect who first proposed an arch at this site has publicly said 250 feet is too large for the location. When the people most knowledgeable about a project's own design principles object to its execution, that's worth taking seriously. The process troubles me as much as the project itself. Both the Commission of Fine Arts and the NCPC have been stocked with political appointees loyal to the current regime who proposed this structure. Of approximately 1,000 public comments received before the Fine Arts Commission vote, 99.5 percent opposed the arch — and the commission approved it anyway. Public comment is not a formality. When virtually unanimous opposition is simply set aside, it stops being a process and becomes a performance. Vietnam veterans and an architectural historian have filed suit arguing that the project bypasses the legal requirement for congressional authorization of new monuments on federal land. That question deserves a real answer before any construction proceeds, not an end-run through a claimed loophole. DC News Now I'm asking the NCPC to do what the Commission of Fine Arts did not: take the public record seriously, weigh the legal questions that remain unresolved, and withhold approval until those questions are answered. Washington's monumental landscape belongs to all Americans and to history.

name: Bernard Resnick
text: May 29, 2026 Mr. Rodney Mims Cook, Jr., Chair U.S. Commission of Fine Arts 401 F Street, NW, Suite 312 Washington, DC 20001 Re: CFA 21/MAY/26-1 Memorial Circle, George Washington Memorial Parkway, Washington, DC. New Monumental Arch. Revised Concept. Dear Mr. Cook: I respectfully submit the following comments concerning the current proposal by the Executive Office of the President and the U.S. Department of the Interior to construct a new Triumphal Arch at Memorial Circle on the George Washington Memorial Parkway. I strongly OBJECT to this structure as currently designed. I also want to remind the members of the CFA that the Commemorative Works Act requires the project to be approved by Congress, which, as far as I am aware, has yet to happen. I am a lawyer practicing in the Philadelphia area, and I am also a former member of the Board of Directors of the Athenaeum Library in Philadelphia. The Athenaeum was founded in 1814, and which is one of the few remaining private shareholder libraries in the USA. The Athenaeum of Philadelphia Special Collections is globally recognized. Its holdings are among the premiere collections of Philadelphia architects and architecture and include 360,000 architectural drawings, 300,000 photographic images, and a 60,000-volume library. Included amongst the Athenaeum's collections are the architectural drawings of Frederick Law Olmsted, in particular his original designs for the dome of the US Capitol. Olmstead was an American landscape architect, journalist, social critic, and public administrator, and he is considered to be the father of landscape architecture in the United States. One of the wonderful things about Washington, DC is that it is a planned city, where those in charge of public buildings and monuments have always used these structures to inspire its visitors, rather than to intimidate them. Most of the public edifices in Washington are appropriate in height, are harmoniously placed in a way that pleases the eye, honor our nation's humble heritage, and respect local flora and fauna. If built as it is currently planned, this oversized Monumental Arch will be the antithesis of these time-honored concepts. Given the plethora of already existing monuments in the Washington, D.C. area, as well as the huge expense of this project, I question why building an "XL"-sized structure which will interrupt the sightlines from the District to Arlington National Cemetery and dwarf the surrounding monuments is even necessary. Instead, I respectfully suggest that the CFA take a fresh look at the Vietnam Veterans Memorial, the memorial arch in Valley Forge National Park, or the Tomb of the Unknown Revolutionary War Soldier in Washington Square in Philadelphia. These memorials are places of quiet reflection. They are of a scale that respectfully honors those who sacrificed their lives to serve our nation, and allow the visitors to quietly remember those who were not able to return home to follow their American dreams. In my opinion, erecting this garish white elephant smacks of an attempt to duplicate some of the war memorials in Europe, which do more to self-aggrandize the emperor who had them built than honor the deceased to whom they are supposedly dedicated. It is clear to me that the current plan for this Memorial Arch is, at best, an ego-driven eyesore. I also fail to see the wisdom of spending millions of dollars to build this unnecessary, cheezy arch in this difficult economic time, when many of our fellow citizens are being forced to make the awful choice of whether to sacrifice on groceries, gasoline or medical care just to stay financially afloat. In conclusion, I wholeheartedly object to the CFA approving this Memorial Arch as currently designed, if at all. I fervently disagree with spending some of my hard-earned taxpayer dollars on this wasteful project. Thank you for considering my concerns and hearing my voice. Very truly yours; Bernard M. Resnick, Esq.

text: Subject: Comment on proposed Washington Mall Triumphal Arch monument – urban design concerns I am a licensed architect submitting comments on the proposed monument. The project is not well aligned with the L'Enfant Plan's principles of axial order, landscape- integrated monumentality, and protected civic sightlines. As proposed, the freestanding arch introduces a dominant object that disrupts established spatial hierarchies within the federal core. Its scale and typology are inconsistent with Washington's precedent of distributed, compositionally integrated memorial design, and risk setting a precedent for isolated monumental forms in protected federal landscapes. I recommend reconsideration of its siting, scale, and fundamental design approach to ensure compatibility with the city's historic planning framework. As an architect specializing in historic preservation I find the proposal fundamentally misaligned with the planning principles that have long governed the capital. The monumental core of Washington is defined by clarity, balance, and a disciplined relationship between built form and open space. This proposal introduces an object that is not only symbolically incongruous, but markedly out of scale with its surroundings. The arch's size and visual dominance would disrupt the carefully calibrated proportions of the existing plan, competing with established landmarks rather than reinforcing their presence. Washington's civic landscape derives its power from restraint and spatial coherence; inserting an oversized, triumphalist form undermines both. From a planning perspective, this raises serious concerns about precedent and cumulative impact. Introducing a structure of this scale and character risks eroding the integrity of the capital's framework and opens the door to further interventions that privilege spectacle over continuity and public meaning. There are also unresolved questions regarding cost, necessity, and the absence of clear, broad- based civic support for such a project. Washington, D.C. does not benefit from the addition of an oversized symbolic gesture of this kind. It requires thoughtful stewardship of its existing assets and guiding principles. I urge the National Capital Planning Commission to reject this proposal. Steve Gallagher North Liberty, IA From: Kevin King Sent: Friday, May 22, 2026 10:10 AM To: NCPC General Information <info@ncpc.gov> Subject: [External] A Triumphal Form on a Reconciliation Axis: Comment on the Proposed Memorial Circle Arch Dear National Capitol Planning Commission: I write as an architect and planner, and as a Washington DC resident, regarding the proposed 250- foot triumphal arch at Memorial Circle. The National Capital Planning Commission exists to ensure that development in the National Capital Region is consistent with the long-range planning frameworks, viewshed protections, and civic relationships that give Washington its meaning. This proposal tests that mandate directly — not primarily because of its scale or its impact on views, though both are serious, but because the chosen typology is fundamentally incompatible with the site's established civic meaning. That is a planning failure, and it falls squarely within this Commission's authority to address. Symbolic incoherence with the federal planning context. The triumphal arch is a specific form with a specific meaning: it commemorates military victory and the dominance of a conquering power. The axis on which this structure is proposed was designed to express the opposite — reconciliation between North and South through shared grief, not triumph. That relationship, between the Lincoln Memorial and Arlington National Cemetery, was not accidental. It was one of Washington's most deliberate acts of civic design, sustained and protected for over a century. Placing a triumphal form directly on that axis does not add meaning to the site. It contradicts and displaces the meaning already there. NCPC's mandate includes ensuring that new development in the Monumental Core is consistent with the long-range planning frameworks that govern it. A structure whose core symbolism conflicts with the documented civic intent of its site fails that standard at the most fundamental level. Destruction of a protected viewshed. The sightline between the Lincoln Memorial and Arlington National Cemetery is among Washington's most intentionally constructed civic relationships. This Commission has a direct planning responsibility for the integrity of the Monumental Core's viewsheds. The proposed structure, at this location and height, would permanently sever that relationship — eliminating not just a view, but the spatial expression of the reconciliation narrative the axis was built to sustain. The Commission should evaluate whether any approval would be consistent with its own Monumental Core Framework and the federal interest in preserving this corridor. Scale and site incompatibility. The 250-foot height was not derived from site analysis, programmatic requirements, or compositional logic. It reflects the anniversary year. That is not a planning rationale. The structure would stand more than twice the height of the Lincoln Memorial and would visually overwhelm the carefully calibrated scale relationships of the Monumental Core. Even Catesby Leigh, the architecture critic who originally championed a monumental arch at this location, has called the 250-foot version "way too big for that site." Procedural concerns. As a commemorative work in the nation's capital, this project may require congressional authorization under the Commemorative Works Act. NCPC is well-positioned to ensure that the full statutory review process is observed before any approval advances. Preliminary site surveys and testing should not substitute for that process. This Commission was established precisely for moments like this — when a proposal with political momentum requires independent planning judgment. The frameworks, protections, and civic relationships that define Washington's monumental landscape exist because earlier generations understood that the capital's meaning must be held in trust, insulated from the pressures of any particular moment. Approving a structure that contradicts the documented intent of its site would set a precedent that weakens those protections for every proposal that follows. The Commission has both the authority and the obligation to require that any structure permanently altering the Monumental Core be proportionate to its site, consistent with long-range federal planning frameworks, and symbolically coherent with the civic relationships it will permanently affect. The current proposal fails on all three counts. I urge the Commission to withhold approval and require the design team to produce alternatives that are site-responsive, symbolically coherent with the axis they would occupy, and original in conception — not a scaled imitation of a European monument imposed on one of Washington's most historically significant landscapes.
